We introduce Conditional Program (CP), a compressed representation that reconstructs only the rows an input requests. CP represents each row by a short code and a local scale, with a reconstruction program shared across the table. We instantiate this representation with a Gaussian trellis, norm restoration and independently decodable row records. CP's two-bit code lowers output KL by 41--63\% relative to 2-bit round-to-nearest. Analysis across three trained n-gram memory families shows that Gaussian-like coordinate statistics coexist with learned relationships among rows; at matched storage budgets, the shared trellis outperforms the fitted codebooks and low-rank residual variants we test. For DeepSeek, it reduces table storage from 203GB to 51GB, leaving room for larger workloads when the table is kept on GPU.
papers.ja_title: ルックアップテーブルを2 bit まで圧縮する Conditional Program
papers.summary: n-gram のような条件付きメモリは入力ごとに一部の行だけを呼び出すが、全ての行を載せられる埋め込みテーブルをメモリに置いておく必要があり容量を圧迫する。提案手法 Conditional Program (CP) は要求された行だけを短いコードと復元プログラムから再構成する方式で、通常の2 bit 最近接量子化に比べ出力の KL ダイバージェンスを41〜63%下げた。DeepSeek のテーブルではストレージを203GB から51GB に圧縮し、テーブルを GPU に載せたまま余力を残せるようになった。
papers.why: テーブル全体を常駐させずに必要な行だけ復元する発想で、巨大な条件付きメモリを GPU に載せて推論したい人に直接効く低精度化の手法。
papers.summary_en: Conditional memory expands language-model capacity through selective lookup, but the full embedding table must remain available for every possible input. Conditional Program (CP) represents each row by a short code and a local scale reconstructed via a reconstruction program shared across the table, lowering output KL by 41-63% relative to 2-bit round-to-nearest; for DeepSeek it reduces table storage from 203GB to 51GB, leaving room for larger workloads when the table is kept on GPU.
papers.why_en: A row-reconstruction scheme that compresses large conditional-memory lookup tables well below naive 2-bit quantization, directly useful for keeping such tables resident on GPU.

papers.title: A Closed Form Depth-Width Law for Neural Collapse in Deep Linear Networks
papers.abstract: How depth and width of neural networks shape learned representations is usually studied only after training. We show that, in a tractable feature-learning setting, this dependence can instead be obtained in closed form. Using neural collapse as a probe of representation geometry, we express NC1--NC3 directly in terms of the learned feature kernel, extending an identity known for NC1 to the angular part of NC2 and to NC3 under a ridge readout. For deep linear networks with exchangeable class structure, the resulting kernel equations yield a geometric law, exact within the theory, for the layerwise evolution of within-class variability. At large width, the accumulated compression becomes a function of the depth-to-width ratio $L/N$, with its rate determined self-consistently by the data, prior and architecture. Numerical experiments support the derived dependence on depth, width and signal-to-noise ratio. The result is a representation-level scaling law derived from feature-learning theory rather than fitted after training.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 深さと幅の比だけで決まる表現の崩れを閉じた式で求める
papers.summary: ニューラルネットワークの層の深さと幅が学習後の表現にどう影響するかは、普通は学習が終わってから測るしかなかった。この研究は「ニューラル・コラプス(クラス内の特徴がどれだけ一つの点に潰れるか)」を手がかりに、深い線形ネットワークではこの潰れ具合が深さと幅の比(L/N)だけで決まる式を学習前に導いた。幅を大きくした極限での数値実験はこの式の通りに振る舞うことを確かめた。
papers.why: 学習済みモデルを測らずに深さと幅の設計が表現にどう効くかを式で予測できる点が、アーキテクチャ設計やスケーリング則を考える人の参考になる。
papers.summary_en: How depth and width shape learned representations is usually studied only after training finishes. This paper shows that, in deep linear networks with exchangeable class structure, within-class variability (neural collapse) can instead be expressed in closed form directly from the learned feature kernel, with the accumulated compression at large width becoming a function of the depth-to-width ratio L/N, its rate determined self-consistently by the data, prior and architecture. Numerical experiments support the derived dependence on depth, width and signal-to-noise ratio.
papers.why_en: A representation-level scaling law derived from feature-learning theory rather than fitted after training, offering a predictive handle on how depth-width tradeoffs shape representations before any training is run.

papers.title: Learning Lean Feedback for Efficient Proof-Candidate Evaluation on GPUs
papers.abstract: Training language models for formal theorem proving requires large numbers of verifier calls. Slow checks and timeouts often leave GPUs waiting and withhold rewards from potentially correct proofs. We train neural evaluators to predict Lean 4 verdicts and compiler feedback on GPUs using 4.84M labelled programs. We compare two validity classifiers with a feedback model that annotates proof attempts with predicted goal states and error messages. A two-stage evaluator that screens candidates with a classifier and scores its positive predictions with the feedback model reaches 87.8% accuracy in predicting whether Lean accepts a candidate proof, evaluated on a 68,932-program benchmark collected from public provers. The combined evaluator processes 3.5 candidates per second on one H100, 4.2x the throughput of our 64-worker Lean baseline with environment reuse. Finally, we combine our evaluator with Lean verdicts to obtain a hybrid reward system that shortens GRPO training steps by approximately 31%. After one GRPO epoch with hybrid rewards, the prover achieves nearly the same miniF2F pass@1 as with Lean-only rewards (62.2% versus 62.4%) and a pass@32 of 72.4% versus 71.3%.
papers.ja_title: Lean の検証をGPU上のモデルで肩代わりする報酬高速化
papers.summary: 定理証明をRLで学習するには検証器(Lean)への呼び出しが山ほど必要だが、検証が遅くタイムアウトすると GPU が待たされ、正しい証明にも報酬が届かないことがある。この研究は488万件のラベル付きプログラムを使い、Lean の判定結果とコンパイラのフィードバックをGPU上で予測するニューラル評価器を学習し、分類器で絞り込んでからフィードバックモデルで採点する2段構成で、6.9万件のベンチマークに対して87.8%の精度で Lean の受理を当てた。この評価器は H100 1枚で毎秒3.5件を処理でき、64並列の Lean ベースラインの4.2倍のスループットで、Lean の判定と組み合わせたハイブリッド報酬は GRPO の学習ステップ数を約31%短縮しつつ、miniF2F の pass@1 を Lean だけの報酬とほぼ同じ精度(62.2% 対 62.4%)に保った。
papers.why: 遅い検証器がボトルネックになる RL 後学習で、検証をニューラル評価器に肩代わりさせてスループットを上げる具体的な設計例として基盤チームの参考になる。
papers.summary_en: Training language models for formal theorem proving requires large numbers of verifier calls, and slow checks or timeouts leave GPUs waiting and withhold rewards from potentially correct proofs. The authors train neural evaluators on 4.84M labelled programs to predict Lean 4 verdicts and compiler feedback, and a two-stage evaluator that screens candidates with a classifier then scores positive predictions with the feedback model reaches 87.8% accuracy predicting whether Lean accepts a candidate on a 68,932-program benchmark, processing 3.5 candidates per second on one H100, 4.2x the throughput of a 64-worker Lean baseline with environment reuse. Combining this evaluator with Lean verdicts as a hybrid reward shortens GRPO training steps by approximately 31% while nearly matching Lean-only-reward miniF2F pass@1 (62.2% vs 62.4%) and a pass@32 of 72.4% vs 71.3%.
papers.why_en: A concrete case of replacing a slow, blocking verifier with a fast learned evaluator to unblock GPU-bound RL training, with measured throughput and accuracy trade-offs.

papers.title: Interfaces and Modules: A Scalable Representation for Weight-Space Learning across Architectures
papers.abstract: Weight-space learning across architectures requires representations that respect parameter symmetries and scale to large networks. Existing equivariant tensor encoders require architecture-specific symmetry specifications, while neuron graphs make global attention costly. We introduce a typed graph organized around shared coordinate-permutation actions. Its nodes, called interfaces, represent coordinate spaces whose bound tensor axes must be permuted jointly; operation occurrences, called modules, form typed hyperedges. A compiler derives this graph from supported PyTorch models, with exact recovery of the permutation factors defined by its constraints. The Universal Weight Encoder (UWE) combines local equivariant updates to parameter features with global attention over invariant interface summaries. The small number of interfaces makes global attention practical, and a single encoder processes different supported architectures. UWE is competitive with architecture-specific state-of-the-art methods on established benchmarks. On a new zoo of 1,200 transformers spanning 100 architectures, it outperforms the evaluated baselines at ranking networks within unseen architectures, including architectures larger than those used for training, while using substantially less memory.

papers.title: Close Enough is Nowhere Near: Fidelity-Consumability Decoupling in KV Caches
papers.abstract: Multi-agent LLM systems communicate in text, which is lossy and wasteful: the sender throws away the reading it already did. A growing literature instead transmits the KV cache, the natural carrier of that reading. We study the most appealing form of the idea: both models stay frozen and the sender's cache is substituted for the reader's with nothing trained. It does not work, and the obstruction belongs to the reader. A frozen transformer reads only caches close to the one it would have written itself, a region we call its tolerable set. We show that geometric similarity to that cache does not predict whether the reader can use it, and the failure is not gradual, so a more faithful substitute is not the remedy it appears to be. We explain this phenomenon with competitive attention. Experimentally, we test eight diverse substitution methods against two measured anchors: an uninformative cache baseline and the reader's own accuracy from having read the passage. All sit at the baseline. That turns a long tail of separate negative results into one outcome with a stated condition for overturning it. A different design does work: if the reader keeps its own cache and attends over the sender's as extra context, adapting only its queries, it beats its own baseline, and also clears the baseline with eight senders pooled where undirected attention over the same union falls below it. We offer this as a characterization on one probe, not a leaderboard claim. Our central contribution is a redirection: pursuing faithful substitute caches is the wrong target; adding a cache to what the reader already has is the promising one.
papers.ja_title: KV キャッシュの使い回しが効かない理由を突き止める
papers.summary: 複数のAIが連携するシステムが文章でやり取りすると、送り手がすでに読み込んだ内容を捨ててしまう無駄が生まれるため、代わりに KV キャッシュ(読み込み結果そのもの)を渡す手法が注目されている。この研究は両方のモデルを凍結したまま送り手のキャッシュを受け手のものに単純に差し替える方法を8種類試したが、どれも「何も渡さない場合」と「受け手自身が読んだ場合」という2つの基準点のところに留まり効果がなかった。代わりに受け手が自分のキャッシュを保ったまま送り手のキャッシュへの注意だけを学習させると、自分だけの場合を上回り、複数の送り手を束ねても劣化しなかった。
papers.why: KV キャッシュを跨いで渡す発想そのものを測定で否定し、代わりに「追加の文脈として注意させる」設計に転換すべきだと示した点が、マルチエージェント推論の設計に直接影響する。
papers.summary_en: Multi-agent LLM systems communicate in text, which throws away the reading the sender already did, motivating transmission of the KV cache instead; this paper tests the most appealing frozen-both-models version, substituting the sender's cache for the reader's with nothing trained, across eight diverse substitution methods, and finds all of them sit at one of two measured anchors, an uninformative-cache baseline and the reader's own from-text accuracy, with geometric similarity to the reader's own cache failing to predict usability. A different design does work: the reader keeps its own cache and attends over the sender's as extra context while adapting only its queries, which beats its own baseline and still clears it when pooling eight senders, where undirected attention over the same union falls below it.
papers.why_en: Turns a long tail of separate negative results on KV-cache transfer into one stated outcome with a condition for overturning it, and redirects the design target from faithful cache substitution to adding the sender's cache as extra context.

review.note: 「渡さない基準」と「本人が読んだ基準」という2つの測定の目印(アンカー)を置くことで、バラバラな失敗報告をひとつの反証可能な結論にまとめる測り方。
review.note_en: Placing two measured anchors (an uninformative-cache baseline and the reader's own from-text accuracy) turns a long tail of scattered negative results into one falsifiable finding with a stated condition for overturning it.

papers.title: Augment the Cache, Replace the Activation: A 2x2 Study of Internal-State Sharing
papers.abstract: Multi-agent systems built from frozen language models communicate through text, which discards the internal state the sender already computed and makes the receiver pay to rebuild it. Work on internal channels avoids that cost, framing the problem as transfer: agent A sends information to agent B. Every agent pair that must communicate needs its own transfer bridge, and every agent added to a system needs a new bridge fitted against each previous agent. We reframe this problem as sharing: an agent publishes its internal state once into a pool, and every peer reads that pool through a single mechanism fitted to no sender in particular, so adding an agent adds a publisher and no new bridge. Whereas the carrier of the internal state and the fusion mechanism are usually chosen independently in the literature, our main finding is that these two choices are coupled; the deciding factor is where the carrier enters the receiver's computation. Consumability is a property of the receiving computation rather than of the representation. We find that the key-value (KV) cache must be augmented rather than swapped in: the receiver cross-attends over a peer's cache while keeping its own, and with only a small query-side adapter trained, matches the accuracy it gets from reading the source document. Activations invert this. They are best written straight into the receiver, with no bridge, no adapter and no training, which beats exposing them alongside the receiver's own, though that advantage rests on knowing where in the receiver the state belongs. The rule is augment the KV cache, replace the activation, established under one protocol with a shared control ladder. One adapter, trained once, also serves publishers it never trained on, and a pool of several at once, but only those whose internal state lies close to the receiver's own.
papers.ja_title: KVキャッシュとアクティベーション、エージェント間で内部状態を共有する正しい方法
papers.summary: マルチエージェント系ではテキストでのやり取りだと送信側が一度計算した内部状態を受信側がまた作り直すコストがかかる。本研究は内部状態の受け渡しを「転送」ではなく共有プールへの「公開」として捉え直し、KV キャッシュ(推論中に溜まる中間データ)は置き換えずに追加(クロスアテンション)、中間層の出力であるアクティベーションはそのまま書き込むのが良いと実験で示した。小さなアダプタを1回学習するだけで、学習時に見ていない送信元や複数のプールにも対応できた。
papers.why: 複数エージェントを跨ぐ内部状態共有の設計指針(KV キャッシュは追加・アクティベーションは置換)を示し、エージェント数が増えても送信元ごとの橋渡しを増やさない構成の根拠になる。
papers.summary_en: Multi-agent systems built from frozen language models communicating through text force the receiver to rebuild internal state the sender already computed; the paper reframes this as sharing into a pool rather than pairwise transfer. It finds the KV cache must be augmented (cross-attended) rather than swapped in, while activations are best written straight into the receiver with no bridge or adapter, and one adapter trained once also serves publishers it never trained on.
papers.why_en: Gives a concrete rule (augment the KV cache, replace the activation) for sharing internal state across agents without needing a new bridge per sender pair as systems scale.

papers.title: Effectiveness of Hidden-State Probes for Localizing Reasoning Failures
papers.abstract: Verifying the final answer of a long reasoning trace may show that the trace is wrong but it does not distinguish three cases. The problem may lie beyond the model's capability, another attempt would succeed, or one step in an otherwise recoverable trace made the trace fail. Standard hidden-state probes are trained on final-answer correctness, a label that conflates these cases. Monte Carlo rollouts distinguish the cases and locate the failing step at additional inference cost. We test the hidden states of 4B and 8B reasoning models for the failure type and the failing step and compare each probe with the strongest baseline that uses no hidden states. On incorrect 8B traces, the confidence probe, a calibrated correctness probe at a midpoint cutoff, misses 81% of cases in which a single step makes the trace unrecoverable and 47% of cases in which another attempt would succeed. A probe with a different training design over the same states reverses the ordering of these two kinds of failure, so either ordering can be read from those states. At both scales, no single tested probe locates the failing step more accurately than a rule based only on trace length, and at 4B a probe trained to predict that step fails to outperform this rule in any of 10 runs on identical traces. The confidence probe therefore indicates that an answer is wrong, but its failure-type ordering depends on its training design.
papers.ja_title: 推論の失敗箇所は内部状態から当てられるか、それとも長さだけで分かるのか
papers.summary: 長い推論の結果が間違っていても、能力不足・もう一度やれば直る・1 ステップの誤りが原因、の3 通りが区別できない問題に対し、IBM は 4B と 8B の推論モデルの内部状態(隠れ層)を使った分類器(プローブ)を調べた。8B モデルの誤った推論では、確信度を測るプローブは「1 ステップの誤りで回復不能になった」ケースの 81%、「もう一度やれば直る」ケースの 47%を見逃し、どちらのモデルでも失敗ステップの特定精度は推論の長さだけを見る単純な規則を上回らなかった。
papers.why: ベンチマークや評価の作り方の落とし穴を示す結果で、内部状態を使った複雑な判定器を導入する前に単純な基準(トレース長)と比較する必要性を裏付ける。
papers.summary_en: Verifying only the final answer of a long reasoning trace cannot distinguish whether the model lacked the capability, another attempt would succeed, or a single step broke an otherwise recoverable trace, so IBM tests hidden-state probes on 4B and 8B reasoning models for exactly this. On incorrect 8B traces, the confidence probe misses 81% of unrecoverable single-step failures and 47% of retry-recoverable ones, and at both scales no tested probe locates the failing step more accurately than a rule based only on trace length.
papers.why_en: A direct demonstration that a sophisticated hidden-state classifier can still lose to a trivial length-based baseline, a caution for anyone designing evaluation probes before trusting them over simple heuristics.

review.note: 複雑な内部状態プローブを評価するときは、トレース長のような単純な基準を必ずベースラインに置いて比べる、という検証の仕方を示している。
review.note_en: Shows the practice of always comparing a sophisticated hidden-state probe against a trivial baseline such as trace length before trusting its evaluation claims.

papers.title: DropKV: Decoupling Residual-Output Perturbation for Near-Optimal KV-Cache Eviction
papers.abstract: Key-value (KV) cache management has become a critical bottleneck for scaling Large Language Models (LLMs) to long-context scenarios due to linear memory growth. While recent eviction methods have moved beyond simple attention-score heuristics to incorporate value representations, they typically face a fundamental trade-off: the underlying optimization for minimizing output perturbation is an NP-hard combinatorial problem, leading to mathematically suboptimal heuristics or implementations that are difficult to kernelize. In this work, we propose DropKV, a simple principled eviction framework based on Decoupled Residual-Output Perturbation. By decoupling the joint eviction decision into independent per-token scoring, DropKV circumvents combinatorial intractability and admits a provable constant-factor approximation guarantee under a cone condition that we empirically verify on three long-context LLMs. To ensure practical viability, we provide a high-performance implementation using fused Triton kernels that avoid materializing the full attention matrix, delivering a 19.8x scoring-kernel speedup that translates to up to a 9.9% matched-batch end-to-end prefill speedup. Extensive evaluations on the RULER and LongBench benchmarks demonstrate that DropKV consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines at equivalent cache budgets, achieving the lowest inference latency among eviction methods while also remaining faster than the dynamic cache baseline.
papers.ja_title: DropKV: KV キャッシュの間引きをトークンごとの独立採点に分解して高速化
papers.summary: 長文脈 LLM では KV キャッシュ(推論中に溜まる中間データ)の管理がメモリのボトルネックになるが、出力への影響を最小にする間引き方法を厳密に解くのは NP 困難なため、既存手法は近似に頼っていた。NVIDIA と IBM は間引きの判断をトークンごとの独立採点に分解することでこの壁を回避し、Triton カーネルでスコアリングを 19.8 倍高速化、バッチを揃えた end-to-end のプレフィル(入力処理)も最大 9.9%速くした。RULER と LongBench の評価では、同じキャッシュ予算で既存の間引き手法より低いレイテンシ(応答までの時間)を達成した。
papers.why: KV キャッシュ間引きの最適化問題を数学的に扱いやすい形に分解し、カーネル実装まで含めて実用速度を出した例で、長文脈サービングのメモリとレイテンシ両方を改善する具体的な手法。
papers.summary_en: KV-cache management is a critical memory bottleneck for long-context LLMs, but the optimal eviction that minimizes output perturbation is NP-hard, forcing prior methods into suboptimal or hard-to-kernelize heuristics. DropKV decouples the joint eviction decision into independent per-token scoring, giving a provable constant-factor approximation and, via fused Triton kernels, a 19.8x scoring-kernel speedup that translates to up to a 9.9% matched-batch end-to-end prefill speedup, while outperforming state-of-the-art baselines on RULER and LongBench at equivalent cache budgets.
papers.why_en: Offers a mathematically tractable decomposition of KV-cache eviction plus a kernel implementation that actually delivers the latency win, relevant to anyone optimizing long-context serving memory and speed together.

papers.title: Realtime-Bench: Can Frontier Models Solve Real-time Interactive Problems?
papers.abstract: Real-time interaction requires agents to perceive evolving environments and act under temporal constraints, yet existing evaluations of real-time streaming models focus on conversational quality and streaming perception, leaving effective action under strict temporal constraints untested. We introduce Realtime-Bench, a suite of carefully curated dynamic tasks where delayed actions directly affect success. Under Wall Clock, where environments advance according to actual inference latency, the best success rate reaches only 44% and the best Pass^3 is only 36%, demonstrating that real-time interaction remains challenging. To separate serving latency from models' real-time streaming capability, we compare Wall Clock with Paused Clock, which removes inference delays as an idealized reference, and introduce Token Clock, which advances simulated time according to generated token counts, testing temporal awareness independently of physical serving speed. We find that temporal costs limit success in evolving environments and that higher reasoning effort has mixed effects under time pressure, reflecting a trade-off between decision quality and timely execution. Based on these results, we discuss future directions for improving real-time multimodal models, including adaptive reasoning with temporal awareness and continuous perception and action.
papers.ja_title: Realtime-Bench: 最先端モデルはリアルタイムの時間制約下で動けるか
papers.summary: リアルタイムで環境が変化する中でのエージェントの行動は、応答が遅いと成否に直結するが、既存の評価は会話の質や認識の質だけを見ていた。NVIDIA と UIUC の Realtime-Bench では、実際の推論の遅さが環境に反映される Wall Clock 条件で最高の成功率が 44%、3 回中 3 回とも成功する Pass^3 は最高で 36%にとどまった。推論の遅れを除いた Paused Clock や、生成トークン数で時間を進める Token Clock と比較することで、サービングの速さとモデル自体の時間感覚を分けて測れるようにした。
papers.why: 推論のレイテンシ(応答までの時間)がタスクの成否に直結する評価軸を作った点が、サービング側の速度改善の効果を切り分けて測る基準になる。
papers.summary_en: Real-time interaction requires agents to act under temporal constraints, yet existing evaluations of streaming models test only conversational quality and perception, leaving effective action under strict time pressure untested. Under Wall Clock, where the environment advances according to actual inference latency, the best success rate reaches only 44% and the best Pass^3 is only 36%; comparing this against an idealized Paused Clock and a token-count-based Token Clock lets the authors separate serving latency from the model's own temporal awareness.
papers.why_en: Establishes a benchmark axis where inference latency itself determines task success, useful for isolating how much serving-side speed improvements actually matter versus the model's intrinsic capability.

papers.title: LCT: Losslessly Compressed Tensors with GPU friendly execution for Training
papers.abstract: Lossless tensor compression could reduce memory usage during training, but training requires tensors to be repeatedly re-encoded. We introduce Losslessly Compressed Tensors (LCT), a GPU execution framework designed for this repeated encode-decode regime. LCT exploits the natural redundancy in floating point data to reduce storage for weights, activations and optimizer states. Highly optimized GPU kernels implement Huffman coding with precomputed codebooks for low compression and decompression overhead, essential for training. Our analysis characterizes LCT's storage costs and adaptation to magnitude shifts. LCT achieves a compression ratio of up to $1.455\times$, and is demonstrated in training and finetuning settings. On a 162M-parameter NanoGPT, LCT reduces memory usage by $24.6\%$ for a $7.2\%$ step-time increase. In Qwen3-4B fine-tuning, LCT saves up to $23.8\%$ of peak memory, enabling a $3.5\times$ larger context length in training on the same GPU.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: LCT: 学習中の重みや中間データを可逆圧縮してメモリを削減
papers.summary: 学習中は重み・中間出力(アクティベーション)・オプティマイザの状態を何度も符号化・復号する必要があり、可逆圧縮(情報を失わない圧縮)はこの繰り返しに耐える必要がある。Oxford/Cambridge の LCT は浮動小数点データの冗長性を使い、事前計算した符号表によるハフマン符号化を GPU カーネルで高速に行うことで最大 1.455 倍の圧縮率を達成した。162M パラメータの NanoGPT ではステップ時間 7.2%増でメモリ使用量を 24.6%削減し、Qwen3-4B の微調整では同じ GPU で学習時の文脈長を 3.5 倍に伸ばせた。
papers.why: 精度を落とさない可逆圧縮を学習中の繰り返し符号化・復号に対応する速さで実装した点が、同じ GPU でより長い文脈や大きいバッチを学習する余地を作る。
papers.summary_en: Training requires tensors to be repeatedly re-encoded, so lossless compression needs to survive this encode-decode cycle; LCT exploits the natural redundancy in floating point data and implements Huffman coding with precomputed codebooks in highly optimized GPU kernels to keep that overhead low, achieving a compression ratio of up to 1.455x. On a 162M-parameter NanoGPT it reduces memory usage by 24.6% for a 7.2% step-time increase, and in Qwen3-4B fine-tuning it saves up to 23.8% of peak memory, enabling a 3.5x larger context length on the same GPU.
papers.why_en: A lossless compression framework fast enough for the repeated re-encoding that training demands, directly freeing up memory for longer context or larger batches on the same hardware.

papers.title: Hy-Memory-30B-A3B: Attributed Reinforcement Learning for Long-Term Memory Writing
papers.abstract: External-memory systems extend language-model applications beyond a context window, but their quality depends critically on the model executing the write path: deciding what to retain, how precisely to represent it, and how new evidence should update persistent state. Existing frameworks typically place a general-purpose large language model behind framework-specific prompts. This raises serving cost, and a writer specialized for one protocol does not transfer directly to another; a unified model that can operate across established memory frameworks remains largely unexplored. We present Hy-Memory-30B-A3B, a compact long-term-memory writer trained across Mem0, MemOS, and Hy-Memory. Memory On-Policy Distillation teaches framework-specific write protocols on student-generated states; Memory RL then optimizes downstream answerability using dense per-chunk probes, attributed cross-chunk rewards, over-storage controls, and chunk-level GRPO. Carrying policy-written banks across windows keeps training aligned with deployment. On fixed 20% benchmark subsamples, Hy-Memory-30B-A3B ranks first on all four evaluated harnesses, including held-out EverMemOS, with a 55.49% macro average versus 54.62% for Claude Opus 5.
papers.ja_title: Hy-Memory-30B-A3B: 複数の外部メモリ規格を1つのモデルで書けるようにする
papers.summary: コンテキストウィンドウ(一度に読める範囲)を超えて記憶を保つ外部メモリシステムは、どの情報を残すかを決める書き込みの質に性能が左右されるが、既存の仕組みは汎用 LLM にフレームワークごとのプロンプトを与えるだけで、サービングコストが上がり他の規格に転用できなかった。Tencent の Hy-Memory-30B-A3B は Mem0・MemOS・Hy-Memory という複数の規格をまたいで書き込み方を学習し、オンポリシー蒸留とチャンク単位の GRPO(強化学習の手法)で下流タスクの正答率を直接最適化した。固定した 20%のベンチマーク部分集合では、未知の規格 EverMemOS を含む 4 つの評価すべてで 1 位となり、マクロ平均 55.49%で Claude Opus 5 の 54.62%を上回った。
papers.why: 1 つのモデルで複数のメモリ規格の書き込みを担えるようにし、規格ごとに専用モデルを立てるサービングコストを避ける設計。
papers.summary_en: External-memory systems let language models retain information beyond the context window, but their quality depends on the write path deciding what to retain, and existing frameworks place a general-purpose LLM behind framework-specific prompts, raising serving cost and failing to transfer across protocols. Hy-Memory-30B-A3B is trained across Mem0, MemOS, and Hy-Memory using on-policy distillation plus chunk-level GRPO that optimizes downstream answerability directly, and on fixed 20% benchmark subsamples it ranks first on all four evaluated harnesses, including held-out EverMemOS, with a 55.49% macro average versus 54.62% for Claude Opus 5.
papers.why_en: A single compact model that handles the memory write path across multiple established protocols, avoiding the serving cost of running a separate specialized writer per framework.

papers.title: Skill-Decoupled On-Policy Expert Distillation for Unified Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) can elicit specialized visual capabilities in vision-language models (VLMs), yet jointly optimizing heterogeneous objectives often introduces cross-capability gradient conflicts. Training experts independently mitigates this interference, but direct reward optimization may entangle specialized knowledge with reward-hacking biases. This paper proposes Skill-Decoupled On-Policy Expert Distillation (SCOPED), which trains capability-specific experts and extracts explicit skills through reward-guided reflection. During on-policy distillation, these skills guide expert supervision while remaining unavailable to the unified student, encouraging it to internalize procedural knowledge without explicit skills at inference time. Across eight multimodal benchmarks, SCOPED consistently outperforms the backbone and mixed-capability RL, demonstrating the effectiveness of skill-decoupled on-policy expert distillation for integrating independently acquired capabilities. Further analyses reveal interference during joint capability optimization and suggest that skill augmentation promotes more consistent expert trajectories, greater attention to task-relevant visual evidence, and better preservation of specialized expertise in the unified student. All code and data are available at https://github.com/NEUIR/SCOPED.
papers.ja_title: SCOPED: 得意分野ごとに育てた専門モデルの知識を1つの VLM にまとめる
papers.summary: 強化学習で視覚言語モデル(VLM)に複数の専門能力を同時に獲得させようとすると、能力同士の勾配(学習方向)が競合してしまう。Alibaba/Qwen の SCOPED は能力ごとに専門モデルを別々に育ててから、報酬を使った振り返りで明示的な手順を取り出し、それを使って統合モデルを on-policy 蒸留で指導する一方、統合モデル自身には明示的な手順を渡さず内面化させる。8 つのマルチモーダルベンチマークで、元のモデルや能力を混ぜたまま強化学習する手法を一貫して上回った。
papers.why: 専門能力同士が競合する強化学習の問題を、個別に育ててから蒸留で統合するという手順で回避する設計で、複数能力を持つモデルを育てる際の参考になる。
papers.summary_en: Jointly optimizing heterogeneous reinforcement-learning objectives in vision-language models often causes cross-capability gradient conflicts, while training experts independently risks entangling specialized knowledge with reward-hacking biases. SCOPED trains capability-specific experts, extracts explicit skills through reward-guided reflection, and uses those skills to guide on-policy distillation into a unified student that never sees the explicit skills itself, internalizing procedural knowledge instead. Across eight multimodal benchmarks, SCOPED consistently outperforms both the backbone and mixed-capability RL.
papers.why_en: Offers a train-experts-then-distill recipe for avoiding gradient conflicts when giving one model several reinforcement-learning-trained capabilities at once.

papers.title: Architecting for Hardware Diversity: Meta's End-to-End Co-Design for High-Performance AI Training on AMD GPUs
papers.abstract: Meta deploys a heterogeneous fleet comprising NVIDIA GPUs, AMD GPUs, and proprietary MTIA accelerators to reduce costs and mitigate vendor lock-in. However, the extensive history of NVIDIA-specific optimizations hinders performance portability to other hardware. This paper presents our methods for optimizing alternative accelerators, using AMD Instinct MI350X versus NVIDIA B200 for recommendation model training as a case study. We propose three reusable principles. First, hardware-model co-design is essential: rather than directly porting models from NVIDIA GPUs, revising model structures and software recipes allows full exploitation of accelerator-specific strengths (e.g., MI350X's 1.6x HBM capacity relative to B200). Second, our analytical performance model enables zero-warmup optimal kernel selection across diverse datatypes and matrix shapes in production models, drastically simplifying tuning. Third, increasingly mature agentic workflows have lowered the barrier to porting from the CUDA ecosystem; we extend these workflows for microarchitecture-aware kernel optimizations and custom shim generation. Compared to the directly ported baseline, these methods deliver up to 1.5x improvement in end-to-end training throughput. To our knowledge, this is the first hyperscaler report on productionizing AMD GPUs for large-scale training. Our contributions have been upstreamed to the open-source PyTorch, Triton, and ROCm ecosystems.
papers.ja_title: Meta が AMD GPU で大規模学習を本番投入するために行ったハードウェア協調設計
papers.summary: Meta は NVIDIA GPU・AMD GPU・自社 MTIA の混在環境を運用しているが、NVIDIA 向けに積み上げた最適化は他のハードウェアにそのまま移植できない。推薦モデルの学習で AMD の MI350X と NVIDIA の B200 を比較した事例では、モデル構造とソフトウェアをそのまま移すのではなく MI350X が持つ B200 の 1.6 倍の HBM(高帯域メモリ)容量などの特性に合わせて作り直すハードウェア・モデル協調設計と、warm-up 不要で最適なカーネルを選べる性能モデル、CUDA からの移植を助けるエージェント的な作業の3つを組み合わせた。素直に移植しただけの基準と比べ、end-to-end の学習スループットが最大 1.5 倍になった。
papers.why: 大規模ハイパースケーラーが NVIDIA 以外の GPU を本番の大規模学習に投入した初めての報告で、PyTorch/Triton/ROCm に成果を upstream している点も実務上の参考になる。
papers.summary_en: Meta runs a heterogeneous fleet of NVIDIA GPUs, AMD GPUs, and proprietary MTIA accelerators, but its long history of NVIDIA-specific optimizations does not port directly to other hardware. Using AMD MI350X versus NVIDIA B200 for recommendation-model training as a case study, the paper combines hardware-model co-design that exploits traits like MI350X's 1.6x HBM capacity relative to B200, a zero-warmup analytical performance model for optimal kernel selection, and agentic workflows for CUDA-to-ROCm porting, delivering up to a 1.5x improvement in end-to-end training throughput over a directly ported baseline.
papers.why_en: Described as the first hyperscaler report on productionizing AMD GPUs for large-scale training, with contributions upstreamed to PyTorch, Triton, and ROCm, making it a concrete reference for multi-vendor GPU training infrastructure.

papers.title: BitSparse: Compact Activation Storage for ReLU Feed-Forward Networks
papers.abstract: Reducing memory use in large language model (LLM) training is an ongoing challenge. Activation checkpointing saves memory by recomputation, while lossy compression changes the stored activations. The reemergence of sparse $\relu$ and $\relu^2$ activations creates a third opportunity: losslessly compressing the activation cache itself. We present BitSparse, a GPU-resident lossless compression format for sparse activations. Compression and reconstruction run in custom Triton kernels fused into an autograd function, shrinking the activation cache while recovering it exactly for the backward pass. Bfloat16 (BF16) and FP8 activations are supported. Optional sign-bit packing further increases compression up to close to the theoretical limit. We analyze its compression ratio and compare it to the theoretical optimum. BitSparse lowers per-token VRAM by 31\% and 30\% Modded-NanoGPT and Nemotron-H respectively, with overheads of no more than 1\% at practical sequence lengths. Additionally, a new preallocated buffer system avoids host synchronization during training when variable size tensors are allocated.
papers.ja_title: 疎な ReLU 活性化を無損失圧縮して学習メモリを削減する BitSparse
papers.summary: LLM 学習ではバックプロパゲーションのために中間出力 (活性化) をメモリに保存する必要があり、メモリ不足が課題になる。BitSparse は ReLU 系の疎な活性化を GPU 上で無損失に圧縮・復元する Triton カーネルを提案し、符号ビットのパッキングで理論上限近くまで圧縮率を高める。Modded-NanoGPT と Nemotron-H でトークンあたりの VRAM 使用量をそれぞれ 31% と 30% 削減し、実用的なシーケンス長では 1% 以下のオーバーヘッドで済む。
papers.why: 活性化チェックポイントや有損圧縮に代わる無損失な第三の選択肢を示し、メモリ制約下での学習基盤設計に直接使える。
papers.summary_en: Storing activations for backward passes is a major memory bottleneck in LLM training. BitSparse introduces a GPU-resident lossless compression format for sparse ReLU/ReLU^2 activations, with compression and reconstruction fused into custom Triton kernels inside an autograd function, plus optional sign-bit packing that pushes compression close to the theoretical limit. It lowers per-token VRAM by 31% and 30% on Modded-NanoGPT and Nemotron-H respectively, with overheads of no more than 1% at practical sequence lengths.
papers.why_en: Offers a lossless third option alongside activation checkpointing and lossy compression, directly usable for memory-constrained training infrastructure design.

papers.title: Librarian Agents: Training LLMs to Curate Long-Context Workspaces that Anticipate Future Queries
papers.abstract: Reasoning over long document contexts remains a challenge for large language models (LLMs). Standard retrieval methods are inherently reactive, bottlenecking agents with complex, cross-document reasoning at inference time, while precomputed structures like knowledge graphs often fall short because they rely on rigid heuristics. Instead, can we allow agents to perform anticipatory directed curation: learning to proactively reorganize unstructured corpora prior to inference to efficiently serve diverse future queries. We build on a key asymmetry in modern agentic harnesses (e.g., Claude Code): while LLM agents are adept at navigating existing filesystems to solve an immediate task, they are rarely trained to construct reusable workspaces for future use. To instantiate this capability, we introduce Librarian Agents, a framework in which a builder agent transforms raw documents into a hierarchical filesystem of synthetic files and reference links, which forms a workspace tailored for a downstream answering agent. We formulate workspace construction as a Markov decision process and optimize the builder policy via reinforcement learning to directly maximize downstream answering accuracy. Empirically, Librarian Agents outperforms the strongest retrieval and precomputation baselines by 33 percentage points on BrowseComp-Plus, amortizes upfront construction costs across repeated queries, and generalizes zero-shot to unseen domains on BRIGHT with a 31-point average accuracy improvement.
papers.ja_title: 将来の質問を見越して文書を整理するライブラリアンエージェント
papers.summary: 長い文書集合に対する推論では、検索はその場しのぎで複雑な文書横断推論に弱く、知識グラフなどの事前構築は硬直的な規則に頼るという課題がある。本研究は「ビルダーエージェント」が生文書を階層的なファイルシステム (合成ファイルと参照リンク) に事前整理し、後続の回答エージェントが使う作業場を作る仕組みを提案し、構築過程を強化学習でマルコフ決定過程として最適化する。BrowseComp-Plus で最良の検索・事前構築ベースラインを 33 ポイント上回り、未知領域の BRIGHT でも平均 31 ポイントの精度向上を示した。
papers.why: 推論時にコストのかかる検索を事前の構造化作業に移すという発想は、推論サービングのコスト配分を考える上で参考になる。
papers.summary_en: Reasoning over long document contexts is bottlenecked by reactive retrieval and rigid precomputed structures like knowledge graphs. The authors propose Librarian Agents, where a builder agent proactively reorganizes raw documents into a hierarchical filesystem of synthetic files and reference links for a downstream answering agent, formulating the construction as an MDP optimized via reinforcement learning to directly maximize downstream answering accuracy. Librarian Agents outperforms the strongest retrieval and precomputation baselines by 33 percentage points on BrowseComp-Plus and generalizes zero-shot to unseen domains on BRIGHT with a 31-point average accuracy improvement.
papers.why_en: Shifting costly retrieval work to an upfront, RL-trained curation step offers a useful pattern for thinking about amortizing inference-serving costs.

papers.title: Towards Continual Learning: Mitigating Forgetting With Subspace Tuning
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) acquire new skills through fine-tuning, but it can destroy capabilities they already have: catastrophic forgetting remains a central obstacle to continual learning in LLMs. Recent works connect forgetting to how far, and along which directions, fine-tuning moves the weights. On-policy methods such as reinforcement learning and on-policy distillation avoid updating the principal singular directions of weight matrices and thus forget less. In contrast, SFT concentrates updates along these directions and is susceptible to catastrophic forgetting. In this work, we introduce Subspace Tuning (SST), which restricts each weight update to the bottom singular subspace, eliminating changes along the principal directions. SST is optimizer-agnostic and composes well with fine-tuning recipes including SFT and self-distillation. SST combines tight subspace protection, dense gradient estimation, and a simple refresh mechanism, enabling stronger learning than prior orthogonal fine-tuning methods. With these mechanisms, protecting as much as 99\% of the weight subspace substantially improves retention while preserving strong target-task performance. This behavior strengthens with model and data size and nearly eliminates forgetting in the large-model regime. SST also keeps the model close to its base distribution, inducing $2$--$4\times$ less KL drift than the baseline recipes. Overall, SST advances the learning--forgetting Pareto frontier, making it a practical default for fine-tuning pre-trained language models.
papers.ja_title: 重要でない特異部分空間だけを更新して忘却を防ぐ Subspace Tuning
papers.summary: LLM をファインチューニングすると新しい技能を得られるが、既存の能力を壊す「破壊的忘却」が起きやすい。本研究は重み行列の主要な特異方向 (重要な変化方向) を避け、下位の特異部分空間だけを更新する Subspace Tuning (SST) を提案し、重み部分空間の 99% を保護しても目的タスクの性能を保てることを示した。SST はベースラインの学習手法に比べて KL 距離 (元のモデルからの乖離) を 2〜4 倍小さく抑え、モデルやデータが大きくなるほど忘却がほぼなくなる。
papers.why: SFT による継続学習で壊れやすい既存能力を守る実装可能な標準手法を提示し、学習効率と汎化のトレードオフを扱う人に有用。
papers.summary_en: Fine-tuning LLMs to acquire new skills often causes catastrophic forgetting of existing capabilities. The authors introduce Subspace Tuning (SST), which restricts weight updates to the bottom singular subspace while leaving the principal directions untouched, showing that protecting as much as 99% of the weight subspace substantially improves retention while preserving strong target-task performance. SST induces 2-4x less KL drift from the base model than baseline recipes, and this forgetting-mitigation behavior strengthens with model and data size, nearly eliminating forgetting in the large-model regime.
papers.why_en: Provides a practical, optimizer-agnostic default for fine-tuning that protects existing capabilities, directly relevant to anyone managing the learning-forgetting trade-off in post-training pipelines.

papers.title: KnowGPO: Knowledge-Grouped Policy Optimization for Search Agents
papers.abstract: Deep search agents solve knowledge-intensive tasks through long-horizon, multi-turn interactions, where assigning credit to individual search decisions is fundamentally difficult. Outcome-based reinforcement learning provides only a single terminal reward shared across an entire trajectory. Recent process-supervision methods aim to assign credit at finer granularity, but they typically anchor credit to either surface-level trajectory states or model-internal signals, both of which become unreliable in deep search where observations are heterogeneous and retrieved contexts are long and noisy. We propose KnowGPO, a reinforcement learning framework that aligns trajectories by the task-relevant knowledge they have acquired rather than by their surface observations. For each query, KnowGPO decomposes the information required to derive the answer into atomic knowledge conditions, and represents the state of a trajectory at each step by the subset of conditions it has satisfied. Trajectories sharing the same knowledge state are grouped for within-group comparison, and the incremental knowledge gain between consecutive steps serves as an environment-grounded process reward. Experiments on Xbench, BrowseComp-ZH, and GAIA show KnowGPO consistently outperforms outcome-only (GRPO) and process-supervision baselines (GiGPO, IGPO) by 3.8 to 4.2 points, with our 8B model rivaling or exceeding most 32B open-source systems.
papers.ja_title: 知識獲得状況でグループ化して報酬を与える検索エージェント学習 KnowGPO
papers.summary: 複雑な調査タスクをこなすエージェントは長い検索過程の途中の判断に報酬を割り当てるのが難しく、最終結果だけに報酬を与える手法では精度が粗い。KnowGPO は質問を答えに必要な原子的な知識条件に分解し、各手順がどの条件を満たしたかで軌跡を状態化してグループ比較し、知識が増えた分を過程報酬として与える強化学習手法を提案した。Xbench、BrowseComp-ZH、GAIA で結果のみの GRPO や既存の過程報酬手法 (GiGPO、IGPO) を 3.8〜4.2 ポイント上回り、8B モデルでも多くの 32B 級オープンソースシステムに匹敵する性能を示した。
papers.why: 検索エージェントの報酬設計をより細かく、観測ノイズに頑健な形で与える具体的な実装例として参考になる。
papers.summary_en: Deep search agents face difficult credit assignment across long, multi-turn trajectories, since outcome-based RL only gives a single terminal reward. KnowGPO decomposes each query's answer requirements into atomic knowledge conditions, groups trajectories by which conditions they have satisfied at each step, and uses the incremental knowledge gain between steps as an environment-grounded process reward. On Xbench, BrowseComp-ZH, and GAIA, KnowGPO consistently outperforms outcome-only GRPO and process-supervision baselines (GiGPO, IGPO) by 3.8 to 4.2 points, with its 8B model rivaling or exceeding most 32B open-source systems.
papers.why_en: Offers a concrete recipe for finer-grained, noise-robust process reward design for search-agent RL training.

papers.title: MLExpert: Towards a Generalist Agentic Model for Autonomous Machine Learning Engineering
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are expanding from assisting scientific research and engineering to autonomously developing and improving AI systems, advancing AI for AI (AI4AI) as a pathway toward recursive self-improvement (RSI). Workflow-driven machine learning engineering (MLE) systems provide a practical path toward this pursuit through complex orchestration that manages long-horizon experimentation, while recent MLE systems adopt model-directed interaction, allowing models to autonomously organize experiments and adapt optimization strategies based on execution feedback. However, feedback from each experiment reflects several preceding decisions, and a long MLE run contains many such costly experiments. Training must therefore select useful supervision from long interaction trajectories and learn from intermediate outcomes. We propose a post-training method for autonomous long-horizon MLE optimization and apply it to train MLExpert, a 35B Mixture-of-Experts agentic model. We design the Kaggle-MLE Factory to construct executable tasks and an interaction harness for model-directed experimentation. Hierarchical agentic SFT transfers general tool-use and coding capabilities to MLE through outcome-guided supervision. Windowed Interaction RL (WIRL) treats the multi-turn decisions between successive experiment results as an execution window and assigns it a shared outcome-based reward. Asynchronous collection and policy correction support policy updates before the trajectory ends. On MLE-Bench Lite, MLExpert improves the average medal rate of the base model from 37.9% to 72.7%, achieving performance comparable to larger frontier models such as Kimi-K3 and GLM-5.3. Further experiments show that MLExpert improves performance on NatureBench Lite, agent scaffold optimization, and algorithm optimization, suggesting that the learned optimization capability generalizes to other tasks.
papers.ja_title: 機械学習の実験を自律的に進める 35B エージェント MLExpert
papers.summary: 自動で機械学習の実験を何度も繰り返す「AI による AI 開発」では、1 回の実験結果が複数の過去判断を反映するため、どの判断を学習すべきかの選別が難しい。本研究は階層的なエージェント向け教師あり微調整と、連続する実験の間の多手番判断をひとつの窓として共有報酬を与える Windowed Interaction RL (WIRL) を組み合わせ、35B の MoE モデル MLExpert を学習した。MLE-Bench Lite での平均メダル獲得率はベースモデルの 37.9% から 72.7% まで向上し、Kimi-K3 や GLM-5.3 といった大規模フロンティアモデルに匹敵する性能を示した。
papers.why: 長期にわたる実験過程からの学習信号の切り出し方 (窓単位の報酬) を具体的に提示し、エージェント型 RL 後学習の設計に使える。
papers.summary_en: Autonomous, long-horizon machine-learning-engineering agents face a hard credit-assignment problem because feedback from each experiment reflects several preceding decisions across costly runs. The authors combine hierarchical agentic SFT with Windowed Interaction RL (WIRL), which treats the multi-turn decisions between successive experiment results as a window sharing one outcome-based reward, to train MLExpert, a 35B Mixture-of-Experts agentic model. On MLE-Bench Lite, MLExpert raises the base model's average medal rate from 37.9% to 72.7%, reaching performance comparable to larger frontier models such as Kimi-K3 and GLM-5.3.
papers.why_en: Shows a concrete way to carve learning signal out of long interaction trajectories via windowed shared rewards, useful for designing agentic RL post-training pipelines.

papers.title: OmniVerifier-C1: Decomposed Graded Verifier for Rule-Governed Generative World Modeling
papers.abstract: Generative visual verifiers play a crucial role in advancing multimodal intelligence. To enhance the robustness of visual verifiers in complex multimodal scenarios involving compositional requirements, we move beyond conventional binary verifiers that produce only True/False discrete judgments and introduce a verifier that automatically decomposes complex prompts or environmental rules into fine-grained components and assigns pointwise scores to provide a continuous and more informative critique signal. Our experiments further demonstrate that these structured and interpretable outputs improve the verifier's generalization to out-of-domain multimodal critic tasks. To train this verifier, we introduce a Decoupled RL training strategy that jointly optimizes sub-question-level binary judgment and global alignment scoring, using precise local feedback to develop fine-grained verification capabilities that provide a foundation for reliable continuous scoring at the global level. Under a general reinforcement learning framework, we first empirically demonstrate that the proposed pointwise graded verifier significantly outperforms binary verifiers in traditional text-to-image scenarios. We then extend our investigation to rule-governed generative world modeling where generative models are leveraged for world simulation and world reasoning under explicit rules. From a theoretical standpoint, we further show that a pairwise verification paradigm yields more accurate critiques than the pointwise formulation when ground-truth images are available, with empirical results on diverse structured world-modeling tasks such as Maze and Sudoku further validating the effectiveness of our approach. Overall, our findings suggest a key insight: the transition from generative models to structured world-modeling agents critically hinges on the availability of accurate pairwise graded visual verifiers.
papers.ja_title: True/False でなく細分点数で評価する生成ビジュアル検証器 OmniVerifier-C1
papers.summary: マルチモーダル生成モデルの検証器は従来 True/False の二値判定だけで、複合的な要求を持つ複雑な場面では粗すぎるという課題がある。OmniVerifier-C1 は複雑な指示や規則を細かい部分要求に分解して各部分に点数をつけ、部分問題レベルの二値判定と全体の整合性評価を同時に最適化する Decoupled RL で学習する。テキストから画像生成での従来の二値検証器を上回り、迷路やナンプレなどの規則に基づく世界モデリング課題でも、正解画像があるときはペアでの比較評価がより正確な批評を与えることを示した。
papers.why: 生成モデルの評価を細粒度・連続値にする設計は、RL 後学習の報酬モデル・検証器を作る人への具体的な指針になる。
papers.summary_en: Conventional generative visual verifiers produce only binary True/False judgments, which are too coarse for complex multimodal scenarios with compositional requirements. OmniVerifier-C1 decomposes complex prompts or rules into fine-grained components with pointwise scores, trained via a Decoupled RL strategy that jointly optimizes sub-question-level binary judgment and global alignment scoring. The pointwise graded verifier significantly outperforms binary verifiers in text-to-image scenarios, and on rule-governed world-modeling tasks such as Maze and Sudoku, the authors show that a pairwise verification paradigm yields more accurate critiques than the pointwise formulation when ground-truth images are available.
papers.why_en: Provides a concrete blueprint for building fine-grained, continuous reward/verifier models used in RL post-training pipelines.

papers.title: Harness-Delta Attribution: Dissecting Gains From Harness Evolution
papers.abstract: Harness evolution automatically optimizes the prompts, skills, tools, and orchestration code around a fixed-weight model, offering a way to improve agentic systems without updating model weights. The agent harness is iteratively optimized to achieve higher performance on the search set. But how much of this gain reflects benchmark-specific overfitting or additional inference-time compute, and how much may generalize beyond the search set? In this work, we introduce Harness-Delta Attribution (HDA), an evaluation protocol that dissects an evolution gain into artifact-driven overfitting, gains explained by test-time scaling, and the remainder, which gives an upper bound on residual generalizable improvement. We apply HDA to 11 executor models and three harness-evolution frameworks across math, coding, creativity, and agentic tasks. In 21 of these settings that show statistically significant search-set gains, we find that a large share of the improvement is explained by overfitting or test-time scaling. Specifically, among these 21 settings, overfitting and test-time scaling account for 54% and 14% of the gain on average; their combined share exceeds 50% in 14 settings. The residual and held-out transfer vary substantially across tasks, models, and frameworks. Importantly, search-set gains often fail to transfer to held-out tasks, and provide limited evidence that they will persist under practical distribution shifts. Moreover, validation-based signals are insufficient to prevent overfitting. These results motivate attribution-aware evaluation in future harness evolution research.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: ハーネス進化の性能向上を過学習・推論量・本当の改善に切り分ける Harness-Delta Attribution
papers.summary: モデルの重みを変えずにプロンプトや道具・オーケストレーションを自動改良する「ハーネス進化」は、探索に使ったベンチマークでの性能向上の多くが過学習や推論時の計算量増加によるものかもしれないという問題を持つ。本研究は性能向上を「ベンチマーク特化の過学習」「テスト時スケーリングで説明できる分」「残りの汎化可能な改善の上限」に分解する評価手法 Harness-Delta Attribution (HDA) を提案した。11 のモデルと 3 つのハーネス進化手法を数学・コーディング・創作・エージェントタスクにわたって調べ、統計的に有意な改善が見られた 21 件のうち、過学習とテスト時スケーリングが平均で 54% と 14% を占め、14 件では合わせて半分以上を占めることを示した。
papers.why: ベンチマーク上の改善を過学習・計算量増加・本当の汎化改善に切り分ける測り方を提示しており、評価設計のレビューに直接使える。
papers.summary_en: Harness evolution automatically improves agentic systems by optimizing prompts, tools, and orchestration around frozen model weights, but it is unclear how much of the resulting gain reflects benchmark-specific overfitting or extra inference-time compute rather than genuine generalizable improvement. The authors introduce Harness-Delta Attribution (HDA), an evaluation protocol that decomposes an evolution gain into artifact-driven overfitting, gains explained by test-time scaling, and a residual upper bound on generalizable improvement, applying it to 11 executor models and three harness-evolution frameworks across math, coding, creativity, and agentic tasks. Among the 21 settings with statistically significant search-set gains, overfitting and test-time scaling account for 54% and 14% of the gain on average, with their combined share exceeding 50% in 14 settings, and search-set gains often fail to transfer to held-out tasks.
papers.why_en: Offers a concrete measurement framework for separating genuine generalizable gains from overfitting and test-time compute inflation, directly useful for reviewing agentic-system evaluation claims.

review.note: ベンチマーク上の性能向上を発表する際は、過学習分・テスト時計算量分・本当の汎化改善分を切り分けて報告すべきという測り方の観点。
review.note_en: When reporting benchmark gains from agent-harness optimization, separate out overfitting and test-time-compute effects from genuinely generalizable improvement before claiming success.

papers.title: Pearl-Chat: Engineering a native Luganda language model from first principles in JAX and Flax NNX
papers.abstract: Autoregressive foundation language models predominantly target high-resource Indo-European languages, imposing computational and morphological penalties on under-represented African languages. Generic multilingual tokenizers routinely exceed fertility rates of 3.2 tokens per word on agglutinative Bantu languages, degrading context efficiency and inflating latency. We present Pearl-Chat, an 8,473,122-parameter ($\sim$8.5M) causal decoder-only transformer engineered for Luganda (Oluganda, ISO 639-2: lg), a low-resource Niger-Congo Bantu language spoken by over 10 million people in East Africa. Built from first mathematical principles in JAX and Flax NNX, Pearl-Chat uses explicit functional state decomposition (nnx.split and nnx.merge), deterministic resumable data streaming via Google Grain, and SPMD tensor parallelism using jax.sharding.Mesh. We introduce a byte-level byte-pair encoding (BPE) subword tokenizer trained from scratch on curated Luganda corpora ($V = 8,192$), achieving 4.88 characters per token compression and 1.60 tokens per word fertility, a two-fold compression improvement over LLaMA-3 (128K) and Gemma (256K). The model is trained with a two-stage curriculum: Stage 1 pre-training on 59,501 sequences across parallel, biblical, encyclopedic, and journalistic corpora, and Stage 2 instruction fine-tuning on 510 dialogues with assistant-only loss masking. Across 4,000 optimization steps, validation cross-entropy loss drops monotonically from 9.4695 (perplexity: 12,958.98) to 0.1818 (perplexity: 1.20), a decrease of 9.2877 nats. On a three-tier held-out diagnostic benchmark, Pearl-Chat achieves 0.9792 ROUGE-L and 0.9405 BLEU while maintaining concordial agreement across Bantu noun classes. We provide a Python Server-Sent Events (SSE) streaming runtime and open-source all weights, tokenizers, and code.

papers.title: MemLLM: End-to-end In-Storage Acceleration of On-device Retrieval-Augmented Generation using Precomputed KV Caches
papers.abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) on edge devices enables personalized large language model (LLM) inference while preserving privacy. However, RAG's inherent length asymmetry makes the prefill phase the dominant bottleneck. While precomputing the KV caches offline alleviates the prefill cost on server systems, the multi-gigabyte caches over the narrow interconnect create a severe I/O wall for on-device systems. To mitigate this, we propose MemLLM, an end-to-end in-storage processing (ISP) architecture that executes the complete attention pipeline based on precomputed KV caches within the SSD. MemLLM utilizes per-channel accelerators to fully utilize the aggregated NAND channel bandwidth and accelerates all KV cache-related computations on the storage-side to minimize PCIe transfers. To efficiently handle the sparse updates required by RAG, MemLLM introduces a fused recomputation-query kernel paired with a hardware-based filter logic to halve the NAND read volume and eliminate write-back penalties. Furthermore, MemLLM's global SRAM-based stateful reduction engine enables a completely DRAM-less dataflow, thereby removing the internal memory bottlenecks and bounding the PCIe egress to an $O(1)$ footprint. A full-stack software stack allows asynchronous, zero-copy transfers from the ISP to the host and provides transparent execution within modern ML frameworks. Evaluated across eight real-world RAG datasets and six on-device LLM models, MemLLM achieves an average end-to-end speedup of 4.06$\times$ over the GPU baseline.
topics: 集団通信・ネットワーク
papers.ja_title: SSD 内で注意計算まで完結させる端末向け RAG 高速化
papers.summary: 端末 (エッジデバイス) で検索拡張生成 (RAG) を行うと、事前に計算した KV キャッシュ (注意機構の中間データ) がギガバイト級になり、狭い転送経路がボトルネックになる問題があった。研究チームは SSD 内部で注意計算まで実行する MemLLM というストレージ内処理 (in-storage processing) アーキテクチャを作り、NAND チャネル帯域を最大限使うアクセラレータと再計算・検索を一体化したカーネルで読み出し量を半減、DRAM を使わない構成で PCIe 転送量も一定に抑えた。8 種類の実データセットと 6 種類の端末向け LLM で評価し、GPU ベースラインに比べて平均 4.06 倍の高速化を達成した。
papers.why: SSD 側で注意計算まで完結させる発想は、端末推論の I/O ボトルネック解消に直接役立つ新しいアーキテクチャ設計。
papers.summary_en: On-device RAG suffers from a severe I/O wall because multi-gigabyte precomputed KV caches must cross a narrow interconnect, making prefill the dominant bottleneck. The authors propose MemLLM, an in-storage processing architecture that runs the full attention pipeline inside the SSD using per-channel accelerators and a fused recomputation-query kernel that halves NAND read volume and removes write-back penalties via a DRAM-less, SRAM-based dataflow. Across eight real-world RAG datasets and six on-device LLMs, MemLLM achieves an average end-to-end speedup of 4.06x over the GPU baseline.
papers.why_en: Moving attention computation itself into the SSD is a concrete new architecture directly addressing the I/O wall of on-device inference.

papers.title: The Ephemeral Cost of Switching Optimizers Across LLM Training Stages
papers.abstract: Recent work suggests that switching optimizers between pretraining and subsequent training stages incurs a performance cost, but systematic investigation of this phenomenon is lacking. We study the mismatch between AdamW and Muon optimizers by pretraining 1.2B Llama-3 models from scratch while varying the proportion of updates taken with each optimizer, and similarly interpolating between the two optimizers during continued pretraining and supervised fine-tuning (SFT). Surprisingly, we find little evidence of a meaningful optimizer mismatch penalty: final performance is largely explained by the independent effects of the pretraining and post-training optimizers, with downstream performance generally improving as the proportion of Muon updates during SFT increases. Although matching the pretraining optimizer can reduce forgetting during SFT, this does not translate into improved final benchmark performance. We further evaluate AdamW and Muon for task-general SFT of open-weight models, across the Llama and Qwen families up to 14B parameters, where Muon remains competitive with AdamW, despite these models having been pretrained with AdamW. Together, our results suggest that the choice of optimizer for post-training can be made largely independently of the optimizer used during pretraining.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 事前学習と事後学習でオプティマイザを変えても実は損にならない
papers.summary: 事前学習 (pretraining) と事後学習でオプティマイザ (最適化手法) を変えると性能が落ちる、という懸念が指摘されていたが、きちんと検証されていなかった。研究チームは 1.2B パラメータの Llama-3 を AdamW と Muon の比率を変えて事前学習し、継続事前学習と教師付き微調整 (SFT) でも両者を切り替えて比較した。結果、最終性能はほぼ事前学習と事後学習それぞれのオプティマイザの効果の足し算で説明でき、切り替えによる罰則はほとんど見られず、SFT で Muon の割合を増やすほど下流性能が上がる傾向すらあった。Llama・Qwen 系の既存モデル (最大 14B) でも、AdamW で事前学習済みにもかかわらず Muon で SFT すると AdamW と同等の性能を保った。
papers.why: 事前学習と事後学習でオプティマイザを独立に選べるという知見は、学習パイプラインの設計自由度を広げる実用的な結果。
papers.summary_en: Prior work suggested that switching optimizers between pretraining and later stages incurs a performance cost, but this had not been systematically tested. The authors pretrain 1.2B Llama-3 models from scratch while varying the mix of AdamW and Muon updates, and interpolate between the two during continued pretraining and SFT. Surprisingly, they find little evidence of a meaningful mismatch penalty: final performance is largely explained by the independent effects of the pretraining and post-training optimizers, and downstream performance generally improves as the proportion of Muon updates during SFT increases; Muon also remains competitive with AdamW for SFT of open-weight Llama/Qwen models up to 14B despite those models being pretrained with AdamW.
papers.why_en: The finding that post-training optimizer choice can be made largely independently of the pretraining optimizer gives practical freedom in designing training pipelines.

review.note: 「オプティマイザの不一致は性能を損なう」という通説を、更新比率を細かく振った対照実験で検証し、ほぼ成り立たないことを示した実証のやり方。
review.note_en: A worked example of testing a widely assumed claim ('optimizer mismatch hurts performance') with a controlled sweep of update ratios, finding it largely does not hold.

papers.title: Exploring The Empirical Privacy Landscape of Synthetic Data
papers.abstract: Methods for training language models on sensitive data differ in how they balance capability gains against the risk of leaking private information. In this paper, we present a controlled comparison of data-level and training-level interventions for navigating the capability-privacy tradeoff on synthetic medical records with canaries to probe for leakage. Direct finetuning performs best on capability metrics but leads to the most privacy leakage, while DP-SGD reduces leakage at substantial cost to capabilities. Generating synthetic data from these records offers a more favorable balance, particularly when guided by a uniqueness-aware instruction to replace private details. Relative to naive paraphrasing, privacy-aware rewriting improves privacy protection across a variety of different rewriting models. We also find that more capable rewriting models generally reduce the risks of downstream privacy leakage, although held-out fit does not improve monotonically and increased test-time compute yields inconsistent gains. Overall, these results highlight privacy-aware rewriting as a promising direction for achieving a more favorable trade-off between capabilities and empirical privacy compared to other training-level methods, and our evaluation framework supports comparisons of future models and methods.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング

papers.title: Edit Discovery in Human-AI Interactions
papers.abstract: Human-AI interactions are becoming a rich source of data for improving AI systems: while many model responses are already satisfactory, others expose failures that could become valuable supervision if identified and corrected. We study this setting through the notion of an editor: a more capable evaluation process that can inspect a response and either confirm it or modify it, but whose invocation is costly. The editor may be a human expert, a stronger AI system, or the same model equipped with additional computation, context, tools, or information. The key challenge is to decide which interactions to send to the editor before knowing whether an edit will actually be made, since invoking the editor itself consumes limited resources such as expert time, inference cost, latency, or tool-use overhead. We formulate this problem as Edit Discovery Optimization (EDO), which seeks to minimize edit opportunities missed among skipped interactions while controlling unnecessary confirmations and respecting an editor-cost budget. We characterize the population-optimal policy and show that it takes the form of a cost-adjusted threshold on the posterior probability of an edit. Building on this structure, we develop EDIT (Edit Discovery via Iterative Thresholding), an online algorithm for the partial-feedback setting in which edit labels are revealed only for selected interactions. EDIT combines an adaptive edit score, a confirmation-control threshold, and a cost-aware selection rule; it satisfies the editor budget at every round and controls the average confirmation rate up to a vanishing finite-horizon term, without distributional assumptions on the interaction stream. Across four reasoning and factual question-answering benchmarks, EDIT achieves a better trade-off between editor cost, Type-I error, and Type-II error than direct LLM-based batch selection.
papers.ja_title: どの応答を人間や上位モデルに修正してもらうかを決める理論
papers.summary: 人間と AI のやり取りは、失敗した応答を見つけて修正すれば貴重な学習データになるが、より高性能な「編集者」(人間の専門家や上位モデル) を呼ぶのにはコストがかかる。研究チームは、編集される前にどのやり取りを編集者に送るべきかを決める問題を Edit Discovery Optimization として定式化し、事後確率にコスト調整した閾値を使う最適な方針を導いた。この方針を部分的なフィードバックだけで動かせるオンラインアルゴリズム EDIT として実装し、4 つの推論・事実質問応答ベンチマークで、LLM によるバッチ選択よりも編集コストと誤判定 (第一種・第二種の誤り) のバランスが良いことを示した。
papers.why: どの応答を上位の編集者に回すかをコスト制約付きで最適化する枠組みは、RLHF やデータ収集の前段にあたる選別パイプラインの設計に直接使える。
papers.summary_en: Human-AI interactions are a rich source of correction data, but invoking a more capable 'editor' (a human expert or stronger AI) to inspect and fix a response is costly. The authors formulate the problem of deciding which interactions to send to the editor before knowing whether an edit will occur as Edit Discovery Optimization, characterize the population-optimal policy as a cost-adjusted posterior threshold, and build EDIT, an online algorithm for the partial-feedback setting that satisfies the editor budget while controlling confirmation rate. Across four reasoning and factual QA benchmarks, EDIT achieves a better trade-off between editor cost, Type-I error, and Type-II error than direct LLM-based batch selection.
papers.why_en: A cost-budgeted framework for deciding which responses to escalate to a stronger editor is directly applicable to designing supervision-collection pipelines upstream of RL post-training.

papers.title: Chance-Constrained Personalized LLM Routing with Online Preference Learning
papers.abstract: We study personalized LLM routing, where a router selects among heterogeneous models with different costs and capabilities. The router must minimize cumulative inference cost while ensuring reliable realized response quality, even though user preferences are unknown and must be learned from feedback during deployment. We formulate this problem as a constrained contextual bandit and develop an algorithm that learns preferences while balancing cost and quality. Under a logistic preference model and a strict-feasibility condition, we establish sublinear expected cost regret relative to an optimal stationary randomized contextual oracle and a high-probability guarantee on realized cumulative satisfaction. The framework extends beyond LLM routing to broader online model-selection problems with reliability requirements.
papers.ja_title: 品質保証付きで安く振り分ける LLM ルーティングの理論保証
papers.summary: 複数の LLM をユーザーごとに振り分ける「ルーティング」では、ユーザーの好みが分からないまま、コストを抑えつつ応答品質も保証したい。研究チームはこの問題を制約付き文脈付きバンディット (フィードバックを受けながら選択を学ぶ手法) として定式化し、ロジスティック選好モデルの下で累積コストの後悔 (regret、最適解との差) が準線形にしか増えず、実際の満足度の累積についても高確率で保証が成り立つアルゴリズムを示した。
papers.why: コストと品質の両方に制約を持つモデル選択問題に理論的な保証を与える枠組みは、実運用のルーティングシステム設計の根拠として使える。
papers.summary_en: In personalized LLM routing, a router must minimize cumulative inference cost while guaranteeing reliable response quality, even though user preferences are unknown and must be learned online. The authors formulate this as a constrained contextual bandit and, under a logistic preference model and a strict-feasibility condition, establish sublinear expected cost regret relative to an optimal stationary randomized oracle and a high-probability guarantee on realized cumulative satisfaction.
papers.why_en: A theoretically grounded framework for model selection under joint cost and reliability constraints gives a principled basis for designing production routing systems.

papers.title: Repair, Retry, and the Cost of Hindsight: Verifier Feedback in Formal Theorem Proving
papers.abstract: Verifier-guided self-repair conditions a model on feedback from failed attempts before it tries again, without weight updates. Yet two findings in prior work are in tension: verifier feedback can improve repair of failures, but self-repair itself can provide little-to-no advantage over independent resampling. We reconcile these findings in Lean theorem proving through controlled one-step experiments that hold the preceding failure fixed while varying whether the failed proof is shown, whether the compiler error corresponds to that failure, and the retry instruction. We test frozen Qwen3.6-27B, a general-purpose model, and DeepSeek-Prover-V2-7B, a specialized prover, on difficult MiniF2F problems. We find two opposing effects. Showing the model its failed predecessor reduces success and sharply increases copying of it, while on Qwen adding that attempt's compiler error recovers the loss, to the level of the diagnostic alone. Replacing the predecessor with another theorem's failed proof largely removes the degradation on both models; on Qwen, replacing the diagnostic with another problem's error substantially reduces the recovery. Without the failed proof, correct diagnostics show no resolved advantage over wrong-diagnostic controls on either model. The failed-proof penalty persists with and without the retry instruction, whereas Qwen's diagnostic recovery is weaker without it. In 11-problem sequential experiments through 64 attempts, Qwen retains a correct-diagnostic benefit within failed-proof histories, while DeepSeek-Prover shows no resolved recovery. However, no tested one-step feedback condition establishes an advantage over instruction-only resampling, nor does 64-attempt sequential repair with failed proofs and correct diagnostics at equal token budgets. Verifier feedback can thus improve repair without overcoming the performance loss from conditioning on a failed attempt.
papers.ja_title: 定理証明の自己修復はなぜ効くように見えて実は効かないのか
papers.summary: 重みを更新せず、検証者 (verifier) からのフィードバックを見て再挑戦させる「自己修復」は、失敗への対処には効くという報告と、独立に何度も試すだけと大差ないという報告が対立していた。研究チームは Lean の定理証明で、前の失敗した証明を見せるか、コンパイラのエラーをその失敗に対応させるか、再試行の指示を入れるかを個別に変える一段階の実験を、汎用モデル Qwen3.6-27B と専門モデル DeepSeek-Prover-V2-7B で行った。失敗した証明そのものを見せると成功率が下がり単純なコピーが増えるが、Qwen ではコンパイラエラーを加えるとこの劣化が診断のみの場合まで回復し、64 回まで試行する逐次実験でも、どの条件も「指示だけで再試行する」だけのベースラインを上回ることはなかった。
papers.why: 自己修復の効果を「失敗証明を見せる」「エラーを対応させる」などの要素に分解し因果を切り分けた実験設計は、推論改善手法の評価を正しく行う上での手本になる。
papers.summary_en: Verifier-guided self-repair without weight updates has shown conflicting results: feedback can improve repair of failures, yet self-repair itself can offer little advantage over independent resampling. The authors reconcile this in Lean theorem proving via controlled one-step experiments on Qwen3.6-27B and DeepSeek-Prover-V2-7B, finding that showing the failed proof reduces success and sharply increases copying, while for Qwen adding the matching compiler error recovers the loss to the diagnostic-only level; crucially, no tested one-step or 64-attempt sequential feedback condition beats instruction-only resampling at equal token budgets.
papers.why_en: The factorial ablation that isolates which components of 'self-repair' actually drive the effect is a model for correctly evaluating reasoning-improvement methods rather than taking surface-level claims at face value.

review.note: 自己修復の効果を「失敗証明を見せる」「コンパイラエラーを対応させる」「再試行指示」といった要素ごとに個別に操作し、対照群と比較して因果を切り分ける実験設計の観点。
review.note_en: A controlled-ablation approach that varies whether the failed proof is shown, whether the compiler error matches it, and whether a retry instruction is present, to isolate which factor actually causes the observed effect in self-repair.

papers.title: CMM-MP: A Novel Memory Pooling Architecture using Purpose-built Memory Device with CXL and Ethernet
papers.abstract: CXL Memory Module - Memory Pooling (CMM-MP) introduces a novel memory pooling architecture to meet the unique requirements of emerging memory-intensive workloads. This industry-first, purpose-built memory-pooling device combines the benefits of Compute Express Link (CXL) with the scalability and cost advantages of Ethernet. Multiple CMM-MP devices together provide a flexible, composable, and disaggregated memory expansion solution. The CMM-MP enables 100s of TB capacity for GPU/CPU applications without modifications. The memory pool is exposed as a large-capacity logical aggregate memory, with all pool discovery, composition, and backend network datapath tasks fully offloaded to the device. CMM-MP supports both memory pooling and sharing usage modes. It provides an application latency of 2.7 us and up to 23 GB/s of memory throughput. Our evaluations demonstrate that CMM-MP significantly outperforms RDMA-based solutions in latency and throughput. We also evaluated real-world use cases of Valkey+YCSB and DiskANN using CMM-MP.
topics: 集団通信・ネットワーク
papers.theme: 集団通信・ネットワーク
papers.ja_title: CXL と Ethernet を組み合わせた専用メモリプーリング装置
papers.summary: GPU や CPU 向けに数百 TB 規模のメモリを増やしたいが、既存の RDMA (遠隔メモリ直接アクセス) 方式では遅延や帯域に限界があった。Samsung は CXL (Compute Express Link) と Ethernet を組み合わせた専用のメモリプーリング装置 CMM-MP を開発し、メモリプールの管理やネットワーク経路の処理をすべて装置側で行うことで、アプリケーション遅延 2.7 マイクロ秒、メモリ帯域最大 23 GB/s を実現した。Valkey+YCSB や DiskANN といった実アプリケーションでの評価でも、RDMA ベースの手法を遅延・帯域の両方で大きく上回ることを示した。
papers.why: CXL と Ethernet を併用した分離型メモリプーリングのハードウェア実装例は、分散システムでのメモリ拡張設計に直接参考になる。
papers.summary_en: Memory-intensive GPU/CPU workloads want hundreds of TB of expandable memory, but existing RDMA-based solutions hit limits in latency and throughput. Samsung's CMM-MP is a purpose-built, industry-first memory-pooling device combining CXL with the scalability and cost advantages of Ethernet, offloading pool discovery, composition, and network datapath entirely to the device, achieving 2.7 us application latency and up to 23 GB/s of memory throughput, and significantly outperforming RDMA-based solutions in both latency and throughput on real workloads such as Valkey+YCSB and DiskANN.
papers.why_en: This hardware implementation of disaggregated memory pooling combining CXL and Ethernet is directly relevant to designing scalable memory expansion for distributed systems.

papers.title: One Communicator, Three Vendors: Extending the MoA Predictive Theory to a Real NVIDIA+AMD+CPU MPI Ensemble
papers.abstract: The companion MPI-extension paper validated the first communication-bearing machine-shape ensemble: four NVIDIA A100 ranks and four CPU ranks on one NCSA Delta node under one Open MPI job, reassembled by MPI_Gatherv. This paper extends it to a multi-vendor communicator. A Slurm heterogeneous job spanning Delta's A100 and AMD MI100 partitions places A100, MI100 and CPU ranks (nine in all) under one communicator for the first time. We give the theory (a w_i proportional to 1/t_i weight split for three concurrent realizations; a het-job specification as an admissible directive) and report real results, including what the run exposed: the 1/t split assumes time linear in rows, and this fails for the MI100 rank (6 rows took 597 ms against a linear prediction of 1.6 ms). A launch-geometry model, with predictions recorded before measuring, succeeds for the A100 (time flat from 128 to 3456 rows, stepping at exactly 3520 and 6976) and places the MI100 floor in the key loop; changing its launch settings cut about 600 ms to 14.6 ms and the energy per call at 6 rows by 32x, though the MI100 remains about 95x slower than an A100 at 8192 rows. Controlled reruns show that the companion paper's 8.1x A100 result and 22 ms Gatherv were artifacts of four ranks sharing one GPU under Open MPI's default transport. A key/value-split partition whose message sizes are derived from shapes alone is then run: the ring Allreduce of the 8.5 MB message took 11.3, 16.0 and 15.3 ms against a predicted 11-12 ms, the small Allreduce missed its prediction in every run, and compute times reproduce to about 1% while communication times vary up to 4x between runs. Each idea is introduced with a figure and closed with worked examples.
topics: 集団通信・ネットワーク
papers.theme: 集団通信・ネットワーク
papers.ja_title: NVIDIA+AMD+CPU 混在 MPI 通信の実測で見えた予測理論のズレ
papers.summary: 複数ベンダーの GPU と CPU を1つの通信路 (コミュニケータ) で混在させると、速度の予測が難しい。この論文は NCSA Delta クラスタで NVIDIA A100・AMD MI100・CPU を合わせた 9 ランクを1つの MPI ジョブで動かし、理論予測と実測を比較した。MI100 では6行の処理が予測 1.6 ミリ秒に対し実測 597 ミリ秒と大きく外れたが、起動設定を変えることで約 600 ミリ秒から 14.6 ミリ秒に短縮し、1回あたりの消費電力も 32 倍改善した。また、以前の論文で報告された「A100 が 8.1 倍速い」という結果は、4 ランクが1つの GPU を共有する設定による見せかけ (artifact) だったことも判明した。
papers.why: 複数ベンダーの GPU/CPU 混在クラスタでの通信性能予測とその限界、計測の落とし穴を具体的に示しており、分散学習・推論基盤の性能評価設計に直接役立つ。
papers.summary_en: Mixing GPUs from multiple vendors and CPUs under one MPI communicator makes performance hard to predict. The paper runs nine ranks (NVIDIA A100, AMD MI100, CPU) on NCSA Delta under one heterogeneous Slurm job and compares a launch-geometry theory against real measurements. The naive 1/t_i linear-time split failed badly for MI100 (6 rows took 597 ms against a predicted 1.6 ms), but tuning its launch settings cut this to about 14.6 ms from roughly 600 ms and lowered energy per call at 6 rows by 32x, though MI100 remained about 95x slower than A100 at 8192 rows. Controlled reruns also revealed that the companion paper's reported 8.1x A100 speedup and 22 ms Gatherv time were artifacts of four ranks sharing a single GPU under Open MPI's default transport.
