papers.why_en: Gives concrete, measured pitfalls and predictive limits for performance modeling of multi-vendor GPU/CPU communicators, directly useful for designing and evaluating heterogeneous distributed training/inference infrastructure.

review.note: 以前の結果が特定の設定 (GPU 共有・デフォルト通信経路) による見せかけだったと再実験で判明した例。ベンチマークの設定条件を疑って再現実験する観点。
review.note_en: An example where a prior result turned out to be an artifact of a specific setup (shared GPU, default transport), revealed by controlled reruns—a lesson in questioning benchmark conditions and re-verifying results.

papers.title: Reasoning Reranking with Semantic IDs as the Sole Item Representation
papers.abstract: Reasoning rerankers write a rationale before ranking a candidate slate, and existing systems read item metadata to do so, even though generative recommenders increasingly represent items as compact Semantic IDs (SIDs). Ranking from SIDs alone has two appeals: SID prompts are far shorter than the matched item text, and although item codes are fixed from content, the backbone learns their token embeddings in part from user-item interaction sequences, so the tokens can carry behavioral signal that item text lacks. That training targets next-item generation, and whether it supports ranking a supplied slate from SIDs alone is untested. We build ReRankID, a controlled testbed in which models reason and rank from a history and slate shown only as SIDs, varying item rendering, history length, and slate size one at a time. On this testbed, such models often copy the input order instead of reranking, and readable metadata does not repair the failure. We compare supervised fine-tuning, rejection-sampled self-training, on-policy distillation, and verifier-based reinforcement learning as post-training methods and find that they elicit the missing behavior. The strongest post-trained model, the 8B model trained with a graded ranking reward, gives the best SID-only ranking and matches strong text-reading LLMs whose prompts are about 20x longer. It ranks above random with no history at all, where a caption-reading reference does not, and it keeps its gains at long histories, where text prompts pass 50k tokens and the caption-reading reference stops improving. In a paired rationale audit, this model argues trade-offs better than that reference but describes items less accurately. The common post-training methods we test thus elicit ranking from SIDs but not faithful item descriptions, which calls for post-training that improves the reasoning itself, not only the ranking it produces.
papers.ja_title: 推論でSemantic IDだけからランキングできるLLMを育てる
papers.summary: 生成型推薦システムでは商品を Semantic ID (意味を圧縮した短いコード) として表すが、既存の「理由付けして並べ替える」モデルは商品の説明文 (メタデータ) を読んで判断しており、ID だけでは並べ替えができるか分かっていなかった。研究チームは ID のみを見せる評価環境 ReRankID を作り、素のモデルは入力順をそのままコピーしてしまい、説明文を見せても直らないことを確認した。その上で教師ありファインチューニングや強化学習など複数の事後学習手法を試し、8B モデルを段階評価の報酬で学習すると、約 20 倍長い説明文を読む強い LLM と同程度の性能になり、履歴が無い場合やコンテキストが 5 万トークンを超える長い履歴でも性能が落ちなかった。
papers.why: Semantic ID ベースの推薦システムにおける推論・ランキングの事後学習手法の効果と限界 (説明の正確さは向上しない) を示し、推薦基盤の学習設計に参考になる。
papers.summary_en: Reasoning rerankers for generative recommenders usually read item text metadata, even though items are increasingly represented as compact Semantic IDs (SIDs) whose embeddings can carry behavioral signal; whether ranking works from SIDs alone was untested. The authors build ReRankID, a controlled SID-only testbed, and find models often just copy the input order, with readable metadata failing to fix this. The strongest post-trained model (an 8B model trained with a graded ranking reward) matches strong text-reading LLMs whose prompts are about 20x longer, ranks above random with no history where a caption-reading reference does not, and keeps gains at long histories where the text-reading reference's improvement stops past 50k tokens; however it still describes items less accurately in a paired rationale audit.
papers.why_en: Shows how far post-training (SFT, self-training, distillation, RL) can push ranking from compact Semantic IDs alone versus full text, informative for anyone building generative-recommendation reasoning pipelines on learned item codes.

papers.title: Understanding KV Residency in Production-Scale Agentic LLM Workloads
papers.abstract: Agentic large language model (LLM) applications turn one user request into a sequence of model and tool calls over a growing context. Retaining this context's key-value (KV) state in GPU memory lets later calls reuse it instead of recomputing it, but at fleet scale this needs substantial memory. We characterize four production Microsoft M365 workload traces (Deep Research, Enterprise Assistant, Coding Agent and Enterprise Chat) spanning more than 121 million model calls. In Deep Research, the application issues 89% of model calls and the median context grows from about 10K to 68K tokens by the 30th call. About 80% of context tokens are served from the prefix cache. With the public Llama-2-70B KV layout standing in for confidential models, one 99th-percentile Deep Research session exceeds the 80 GB HBM of an NVIDIA H100, and holding all live sessions at their peak needs an estimated 501.8 TB of HBM, although inference occupies only 5.6% of that retention time. Trace-driven replay shows that a one-hour idle cap cuts this ceiling by 3.6x while raising the share of calls that recompute context only from 4.07% to 4.53%. Under tighter budgets, eviction alone is insufficient: at one tenth of the busiest hour's demand, LRU eviction makes 63% of Deep Research calls recompute and clairvoyant furthest-next-use 31%, whereas multi-resolution retention (MRR), which demotes the LRU session's KV state to int4, lowers this to 13.6%. Placement imposes a separate limit: when the next call reaches a different deployment, cached-context reuse drops from 89% to 29%, and treating KV state as deployment-local raises the recompute floor under unlimited memory from 5.4% to 20.2%. These findings motivate retention that changes the representation of KV state, together with deployment-aware routing or migration. We plan to release AgenticTraceSim, a parametric trace generator, and a residency replay framework.
papers.ja_title: 本番のエージェント型LLMワークロードでKVキャッシュがどれだけメモリを食うか実測
papers.summary: 対話の文脈をキー・バリュー (KV) 状態として GPU メモリに保持すると再計算を省けるが、エージェント型 LLM アプリでは文脈がどんどん伸びて大量のメモリを使う。Microsoft M365 の実運用トレース (1.21 億回以上の呼び出し) を分析したところ、Deep Research では 30 回目の呼び出しまでに文脈が平均約 1 万トークンから 6.8 万トークンに増え、全セッションを保持するには推定 501.8 TB の HBM が必要と分かった。アイドル状態を 1 時間で切り捨てると上限を 3.6 倍減らせるが再計算が増える割合はわずかに増えるだけで済み、さらにキャッシュを int4 に落とす多段階保持 (MRR) は LRU 方式より再計算を 63% から 13.6% に抑えられることを示した。
papers.why: エージェント型 LLM 運用における KV キャッシュの実測メモリ要件と、保持方式 (待機時間切り捨て・精度低下・配置) の効果をデータで比較しており、推論基盤のメモリ管理設計に直接使える知見。
papers.summary_en: Agentic LLM apps keep growing context, and retaining its key-value (KV) state in GPU memory avoids recompute but costs substantial memory at fleet scale. Analyzing four Microsoft M365 production traces (121M+ model calls), the authors find Deep Research's median context grows from ~10K to 68K tokens by the 30th call, and holding all live sessions at peak would need an estimated 501.8 TB of HBM even though inference occupies only 5.6% of that retention time. A one-hour idle cap cuts the memory ceiling by 3.6x while raising calls that recompute context only from 4.07% to 4.53%, and under tight budgets a multi-resolution retention scheme that demotes the least-recently-used session's KV to int4 lowers the recompute rate to 13.6% versus 63% for plain LRU eviction.
papers.why_en: Provides measured, fleet-scale memory requirements and a quantitative comparison of retention/eviction/placement strategies for KV caches in agentic LLM serving, directly relevant to building inference memory-management infrastructure.

papers.title: BS-Spec: BFP-Based Bit-Sharing for Self-Speculative LLM Decoding with LUT-Driven Mixed-Precision Acceleration
papers.abstract: As large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed across diverse inference services, serving workloads span a wide range of batch sizes, context lengths, and performance requirements. Speculative decoding improves inference throughput, but conventional approaches require a separate draft model and KV cache, while existing self-speculative methods suffer from workload-insensitive draft configurations and inefficient mixed-precision execution. In this paper, we present BS-Spec, a block floating point (BFP)-based bit-sharing framework that jointly optimizes draft construction, workload-aware precision selection, and hardware execution. BS-Spec derives multiple draft representations directly from a single BFP target model by partially loading the most significant bits of weights and the KV cache while preserving shared exponents, eliminating separate draft-model storage. Offline calibration selects the weight and KV-cache precision pair that maximizes estimated speedup for each serving regime, and a precision lookup table applies the selected configuration at runtime. To support this adaptive execution, we design a mixed-precision BFP accelerator with a lookup table (LUT)-based variable-precision datapath for both draft and target computation. Experimental results show that BS-Spec achieves up to $1.9\times$ speedup over conventional autoregressive decoding and improves speedup over the evaluated bit-sharing self-speculative decoding baselines by $67.2\%$ on average, demonstrating the benefits of jointly co-designing bit sharing, precision adaptation, and specialized hardware for diverse LLM serving workloads.
papers.ja_title: 重みの上位ビットだけ使う自己スペキュレイティブ・デコーディング BS-Spec
papers.summary: LLM 推論を速める投機的デコーディングは通常、別の小さな下書きモデルと KV キャッシュを追加で持つ必要があり無駄が多い。BS-Spec はブロック浮動小数点 (BFP) 形式の重みから上位ビットだけを読み込んで下書き用の軽量モデルを作り、別モデルの保存を不要にした。さらにワークロードに応じて重みと KV キャッシュの精度を選ぶ事前計算と、専用のルックアップテーブル型ハードウェアを組み合わせることで、通常のデコーディングに比べ最大 1.9 倍の高速化、既存のビット共有型手法に比べ平均 67.2% の高速化を達成した。
papers.why: 投機的デコーディング用の下書きモデルを別途持たずに済ませる手法とハードウェア共設計を示し、推論サービング基盤のコスト・精度トレードオフ設計に使える。
papers.summary_en: Speculative decoding usually requires a separate draft model and its own KV cache, which is wasteful. BS-Spec instead derives draft representations directly from a single block-floating-point (BFP) target model by loading only the most-significant weight/KV bits, avoiding separate draft storage, and pairs this with workload-aware precision selection and a lookup-table-based mixed-precision accelerator. It achieves up to 1.9x speedup over conventional autoregressive decoding and improves speedup over evaluated bit-sharing self-speculative baselines by 67.2% on average.
papers.why_en: Demonstrates a joint bit-sharing/precision-selection/hardware co-design that removes the separate draft-model and KV-cache overhead of speculative decoding, useful for inference-serving systems balancing precision and throughput across varied workloads.

papers.title: Scalable Levenberg-Marquardt Training Framework for Deep Learning
papers.abstract: The Levenberg-Marquardt (LMA) algorithm is a widely used nonlinear least-squares solver known for its rapid convergence. For small-scale neural networks, LMA provides better convergence and architectural robustness than first-order optimizers like Adam. However, LMA imposes prohibitive memory and computational costs. These costs are primarily from the Jacobian matrix, whose dimensions scale with both the number of samples and parameters. This bottleneck prevents its use in large-scale neural networks. Recent efforts scale LMA using preconditioned conjugate gradient (PCG) solvers to avoid materializing the Jacobian. However, PCG only approximates the solution, requiring many network propagations and a task-specific preconditioner. Other studies optimize LMA to reduce costs, but they restrict their methods to specific tasks or network architectures. As a result, LMA remains impractical for training general large-scale neural networks. In this paper, we propose LeMA, a distributed LMA algorithm for large-scale neural network training on multi-GPU platforms. Our contributions are twofold: First, an exact dual formulation of LMA removes the memory dependence on the parameter dimension. Second, a Jacobian sharding strategy computes Jacobian shards on the fly and in parallel to avoid materializing the full Jacobian. For large-scale neural networks, LeMA reduces the memory footprint of LMA from quadratic in the number of parameters to quadratic in the batch size. This makes exact LMA steps feasible for billion-parameter models without approximate PCG solves. Furthermore, for a convolutional neural network with 1,000,022,632 parameters on an 8-GPU node, LeMA achieves a 7.97x speedup over a single GPU, corresponding to a 99.7% strong scaling efficiency.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 10億パラメータのモデルでも使える分散版 Levenberg-Marquardt 学習法
papers.summary: Levenberg-Marquardt 法 (LMA) は Adam より速く収束する最適化手法だが、ヤコビ行列のサイズがパラメータ数とサンプル数の両方に比例して増えるため、大規模ニューラルネットには使えなかった。この研究は LMA の双対形式を使ってメモリ消費をパラメータ数ではなくバッチサイズの2乗に抑え、さらにヤコビ行列を分割して並列・オンザフライで計算する手法 (LeMA) を提案した。10 億 2263 万パラメータの畳み込みネットワークを 8GPU で学習させたところ、1GPU 比で 7.97 倍の高速化 (強スケーリング効率 99.7%) を達成した。
papers.why: これまで大規模モデルに適用できなかった2次最適化法を実用的なメモリ量で分散実行できるようにし、学習の収束特性を変える選択肢を分散学習基盤に加える。
papers.summary_en: The Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm (LMA) converges faster than Adam but its Jacobian matrix scales with both parameter count and sample count, making it impractical for large models. The authors propose LeMA, which uses an exact dual formulation to cut LMA's memory footprint from quadratic in parameter count to quadratic in batch size, and shards the Jacobian for on-the-fly parallel computation across GPUs. On a convolutional network with 1,000,022,632 parameters across 8 GPUs, LeMA achieves a 7.97x speedup over a single GPU, corresponding to 99.7% strong scaling efficiency.
papers.why_en: Makes an exact second-order optimizer practical for billion-parameter distributed training within feasible memory, offering a new convergence-behavior option for distributed training infrastructure.

papers.title: Prism Attention: Proposal-Refined Index Sharing Mechanism for Efficient LLMs Inference
papers.abstract: Long-context decoding in large language models (LLMs) is increasingly bottlenecked by the memory and computation required to attend over an ever-growing Key-Value (KV) cache at each autoregressive step. Although token-level sparse attention reduces this burden by restricting computation to a small subset of relevant past tokens, its practical gains are often offset by repeatedly recomputing layer-wise sparse indices as the context grows. A common remedy is to share sparse indices across layers by computing them only at designated anchor layers, but such static reuse ignores the layer-wise evolution of attention patterns, causing the reused indices to progressively deviate from the layer-specific optima and incur substantial attention loss. By revisiting cross-layer sparsity from the perspective of attention dynamics, we find that inter-layer salient token shift is highly localized: although the exact top-$κ$ indices differ across layers, the core high-attention tokens remain stable, with changes concentrated near the expanded boundary of previously selected regions. Motivated by this, we propose Prism Attention, a proposal-refined sparse attention framework. It replaces rigid cross-layer index reuse with a coarse-to-fine strategy, preserving layer-wise adaptability while retaining the efficiency benefits of cross-layer sharing. Extensive experiments show that Prism Attention achieves state-of-the-art performance among mainstream sparse attention methods on both reasoning and long-context benchmarks, while attaining a $3.4\times$ end-to-end decoding speedup over FlashAttention at 128K context length.
papers.ja_title: 層ごとに少しだけ調整するスパース注意機構 Prism Attention
papers.summary: 長い文脈を扱う LLM では、過去の全トークンに注意を向ける代わりに重要な一部だけを選ぶスパース注意 (疎な注意機構) が使われるが、層ごとに重要トークンを選ぶ計算をやり直すとコストが高く、代表の層だけで選んで他の層に使い回すと精度が落ちる。この研究は、層をまたいで重要トークンが大きくは変わらず、選んだ範囲の境界付近だけが変化することを発見し、その変化部分だけを補正する「提案→精密化」方式の Prism Attention を提案した。実験では主要なスパース注意手法の中で最高性能を保ちながら、文脈長 12.8 万トークンで FlashAttention に対し 3.4 倍のデコーディング高速化を達成した。
papers.why: 層間でのスパース注意インデックス共有の精度劣化問題を解決する手法で、長文脈推論を高速化しつつ精度を保つアルゴリズム・カーネル設計に役立つ。
papers.summary_en: Long-context LLM decoding increasingly relies on sparse attention that attends only to a subset of past tokens, but recomputing layer-wise sparse indices is costly while statically reusing indices from a few anchor layers causes the reused indices to drift from each layer's optimum. The authors find that salient tokens shift only near the boundary of previously selected regions across layers, and propose Prism Attention, a coarse-to-fine 'propose-then-refine' scheme that keeps per-layer adaptability while retaining cross-layer sharing's efficiency. It achieves state-of-the-art performance among mainstream sparse attention methods on reasoning and long-context benchmarks, with a 3.4x end-to-end decoding speedup over FlashAttention at 128K context length.
papers.why_en: Addresses the accuracy loss caused by naive cross-layer sparse-index sharing, offering an algorithm/kernel design useful for speeding up long-context LLM inference without sacrificing accuracy.

papers.title: PersonaCUABench: Benchmarking Computer-Use Agents Serving Diverse Personas
papers.abstract: Computer-use agents (CUAs) are commonly evaluated against fixed task specifications, but users may omit requirements, add constraints, or require approval before consequential actions. Completing the benchmark instruction does not guarantee serving the person who asked. We introduce PersonaCUABench, which holds 74 tasks across 11 domains fixed and varies only who asks. A persona agent, playing one of 44 personas in four groups, rewrites each instruction in that user's own words and answers the CUA's questions, while the CUA sees only the dialogue, never the profile or the original instruction. Across nine backbones (3,330 runs), mean task completion falls by 36% relative to the original requests. The losses have two sources: in 59.9% of cells that lose points, the agent engages with what the user asked for and still gets it wrong, and 11.2% are stops the user requested that the checker scores as failures. Even when a persona request is fully completed, the user gives the top satisfaction rating in only 62.7% of cells, against 84.1% for the original requests. CUAs should therefore be evaluated not only on task completion but also on whether they meet the requirements and constraints users express. Code: https://github.com/MatrAIx-ai/PersonaCUABench. Project page: https://matraix.ai/research/persona-cua.html

papers.title: TALLOP: Joint Optimization of Local Training and Communication Compression for Time-Constrained Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Minimizing the wall-clock time required to reach a target accuracy is crucial in federated learning (FL), where many applications require frequent model updates as data distributions evolve over time. Nevertheless, in heterogeneous environments, slow clients with limited computational and communication capabilities can delay global synchronization, forcing faster clients to wait and increasing the overall training time. To mitigate this straggler effect, recent studies have introduced per-round time constraints and adapted client workloads within the available time. However, these approaches primarily focus on local computation, whereas communication can become a major bottleneck in communication-limited environments, motivating the joint optimization of training workload and communication compression. Although previous studies have explored such joint optimization, determining an effective training--communication balance under a fixed per-round time budget remains challenging, as the resulting model performance depends on both training progress and compression-induced degradation. We therefore propose TALLOP, which jointly optimizes the local training workload and communication compression under per-round time constraints. TALLOP predicts the training loss achievable under different computation budgets from the early-stage mini-batch loss trajectory (LENS), and estimates the degradation caused by communication compression using a compression-error model (CLEN). TALLOP combines these predictions to select the training-communication allocation that minimizes the post-compression loss under the given round time constraint. Experiments in heterogeneous FL environments show that TALLOP generally achieves competitive or improved time-to-accuracy compared with approaches that optimize only local training or neither, although the benefit over training-only adaptation depends on the setting.
papers.ja_title: 時間制限下のフェデレーテッドラーニングで学習量と通信圧縮を同時に最適化する TALLOP
papers.summary: フェデレーテッドラーニング (端末ごとにデータを持ったまま学習する分散学習) では、通信や計算が遅い端末 (ストラグラー) が全体の同期を遅らせてしまう。既存手法はラウンドごとの時間制限内で各端末の学習量だけを調整していたが、通信がボトルネックになる環境には対応できていなかった。この研究は、初期の損失変化から学習の効果を予測するモデル (LENS) と圧縮による劣化を予測するモデル (CLEN) を組み合わせ、学習量と通信圧縮の配分を同時に最適化する TALLOP を提案し、異なる環境での実験で目標精度までの時間が、学習のみを調整する手法と同等かそれ以上に改善することを確認した。
papers.why: 計算と通信を別々に扱っていたフェデレーテッドラーニングの時間制約下最適化を統合し、通信がボトルネックになる分散学習環境の設計に新しい調整軸を示す。
papers.summary_en: In federated learning, slow clients (stragglers) with limited compute or communication capacity delay global synchronization, and existing methods adapt only the local training workload under per-round time budgets, leaving communication as an unaddressed bottleneck. The authors propose TALLOP, which jointly optimizes local training workload and communication compression by predicting achievable training loss from early mini-batch loss trajectories (LENS) and compression-induced degradation via a compression-error model (CLEN). Experiments in heterogeneous FL settings show TALLOP generally achieves competitive or improved time-to-accuracy compared with approaches that optimize only local training or neither, though the benefit over training-only adaptation depends on the setting.
papers.why_en: Extends per-round time-constrained federated learning optimization to jointly cover both computation and communication compression, giving a new tuning axis for communication-bottlenecked distributed training deployments.

papers.title: QuarkShard: Decomposing Cross-Shard Requests into Single-Input Transactions
papers.abstract: Sharding blockchains enhance scalability by distributing the workload across multiple shards. Within sharding blockchains, securely and efficiently processing cross-shard user requests remains a pivotal challenge. Traditional sharding blockchain protocols execute cross-shard requests under a processing paradigm that treats each user request as a monolithic entity to preserve its atomicity, inherently introducing significant intra-shard BFT execution overhead and cross-shard communication overhead. We propose QuarkShard, a sharding protocol that breaks away from this traditional paradigm to achieve intra-shard and cross-shard overheads below the lower bounds imposed by conventional approaches. QuarkShard decomposes cross-shard requests into single-input-shard transactions, where each transaction requires consensus and processing within only a single shard, thereby substantially reducing total request processing overhead. Meanwhile, through a carefully designed request decomposition algorithm, QuarkShard guarantees fund atomicity or location atomicity during request execution. QuarkShard also enhances the security of blockchain sharding systems against MEV attacks and flooding attacks. Empirical evaluation across a wide-area network spanning four AWS regions demonstrates that QuarkShard achieves superior performance, attaining a peak throughput of $1024$k requests per second with sub-$4$-second latency. Benchmark comparisons show that QuarkShard achieves up to $210.7\%$ and $314.8\%$ of the maximum throughputs of Kronos and 2PC, respectively.

papers.title: GR-OPD: Group-Relative Sequence Credit for On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) provides token-level teacher feedback, yet common sampled-token updates assign credit locally and omit the effects of earlier actions on subsequent feedback. We introduce \method{} (Group-Relative On-Policy Distillation), which decouples feedback computation from credit assignment by aggregating token feedback into calibrated sequence-level credit. We establish a theoretical basis for this approach by showing that, under ideal on-policy assumptions, broadcasting raw summed feedback to every response token yields an unbiased estimate of the negative gradient of the sequence-level reverse-KL objective. To support effective learning in practice, \method{} discounts later feedback that may become less reliable under distribution shift and uses same-prompt rollout groups to calibrate teacher guidance. It preserves relative response preferences while retaining a controlled fraction of the group mean, which we term collective teacher pressure. Across five Qwen3 teacher--student settings and six mathematical reasoning benchmarks, \method{} outperforms vanilla OPD in macro Avg@K in every setting, including gains of 10.9 and 11.5 percentage points in two settings with matched thinking patterns. It also maintains stable training under mismatched thinking patterns, where vanilla OPD collapses. Ablations show that retaining an appropriate amount of collective teacher pressure can improve learning, while excessive collective teacher pressure or an unrestricted feedback horizon can destabilize training.
papers.ja_title: GR-OPD: オンポリシー蒸留のための系列単位の功績割り当て
papers.summary: 教師モデルがトークンごとにフィードバック (手がかり) を与える「オンポリシー蒸留」では、各トークンの更新がその場だけの評価になり、前の行動が後のフィードバックに与える影響を無視してしまう問題があった。GR-OPD は、トークンごとのフィードバックを集計して系列全体での功績 (どの行動がどれだけ良かったかの割り当て) に変換し、時間が経つほど信頼性が下がる後半のフィードバックは割引し、同じ問いから複数の応答を集めたグループで教師の指示を補正する。Qwen3 を使った 5 つの教師・生徒組み合わせと 6 つの数学推論ベンチマークで、通常のオンポリシー蒸留に対して全設定で平均精度 (macro Avg@K) が上回り、2 つの設定では 10.9 ポイントと 11.5 ポイント改善し、思考パターンが教師と生徒でずれていても通常手法が崩壊する状況で安定して学習できた。
papers.why: トークン単位のフィードバックを系列単位の功績割り当てに変換する理論的裏付けと、教師・生徒の思考パターンがずれても学習が崩れない工夫は、RL 後学習や蒸留を実装する人にとってすぐ使える知見になる。
papers.summary_en: On-policy distillation gives token-level teacher feedback, but common sampled-token updates assign credit locally and omit how earlier actions affect later feedback. GR-OPD aggregates token feedback into calibrated sequence-level credit, discounts later feedback that becomes less reliable under distribution shift, and calibrates teacher guidance using same-prompt rollout groups, with a theoretical basis showing this yields an unbiased estimate of the sequence-level reverse-KL gradient under ideal on-policy assumptions. Across five Qwen3 teacher-student settings and six math reasoning benchmarks, GR-OPD outperforms vanilla OPD in macro Avg@K in every setting, including gains of 10.9 and 11.5 percentage points in two settings, and stays stable under mismatched thinking patterns where vanilla OPD collapses.
papers.why_en: The sequence-level credit assignment with a theoretical grounding, plus robustness to teacher-student thinking-pattern mismatch, gives builders of RL post-training/distillation pipelines a concrete, usable improvement over standard on-policy distillation.

papers.title: SpikeQ: Spike-Guided Post-Training Quantization for Spiking Neural Networks
papers.abstract: On neuromorphic chips, spiking neural networks (SNNs) consume far less energy than artificial neural networks (ANNs), but the limited memory of these chips requires low-bit synaptic weights and membrane potentials. Existing post-training quantization (PTQ) methods provide them without retraining and, like those for ANNs, minimize numerical errors such as the mean squared error (MSE). In an SNN, however, a quantization error reaches later layers only through the spikes it flips. We find that errors of equal MSE can cause very different accuracy losses, whereas errors that flip the same fraction of spikes cause the same loss. We therefore propose SpikeQ, a spike-guided PTQ framework. For weights, we select the level of each weight by simulating the downstream neurons and minimizing their spike errors. For membrane potentials, most existing methods quantize the state after the reset, whereas neuromorphic chips compare the threshold with the membrane potential stored at a fixed bit width. We target this pre-fire quantization and build a reset-aware grid that places the threshold on a rounding boundary, so rounding never flips the spike at the current time step. We evaluate SpikeQ on seven benchmarks of image classification, semantic segmentation, and object detection. With 2-bit pre-fire membrane potentials, every existing grid collapses, whereas SpikeQ retains most of the full-precision accuracy. With both at 4 bits, the models stay within 2.59 points of full precision, shrink their memory footprint 7.8--7.9 times, and use 6.4--6.9 times less energy.
papers.ja_title: SpikeQ: スパイクの発火を基準にしたスパイキングニューラルネットワークの量子化
papers.summary: ニューロモーフィックチップ上で動くスパイキングニューラルネットワーク (生物の神経発火を模したネットワーク) は省エネだが、メモリが少ないため重みや膜電位 (ニューロンの内部状態) を低ビットにする必要がある。従来の量子化手法は通常の誤差指標 (平均二乗誤差など) を小さくしようとするが、この研究は同じ誤差量でも発火 (スパイク) が反転するかどうかで精度への影響が全く違うことを見つけ、発火の反転率を直接最小化する量子化手法 SpikeQ を提案した。7 つの画像分類・セグメンテーション・物体検出ベンチマークで、膜電位を 2 ビットにすると既存手法は精度が崩壊する一方 SpikeQ は高精度を保ち、重み・膜電位ともに 4 ビットにしてもフル精度との差は 2.59 ポイント以内に抑えつつ、メモリを 7.8〜7.9 倍、エネルギーを 6.4〜6.9 倍削減した。
papers.why: 通常の誤差指標ではなく「発火が反転するかどうか」を基準に量子化するという着眼点は、低精度化・量子化の設計を考える人に、誤差指標の選び方そのものを見直す視点を与える。
papers.summary_en: On neuromorphic chips, spiking neural networks (SNNs) use far less energy than ANNs, but limited memory forces low-bit weights and membrane potentials. Existing post-training quantization methods minimize numerical error (e.g., MSE) as for ANNs, but the authors find that errors of equal MSE cause very different accuracy losses, whereas errors flipping the same fraction of spikes cause the same loss, motivating SpikeQ, which selects weight levels by minimizing downstream spike errors and builds a reset-aware grid for pre-fire membrane potentials. Across seven benchmarks in image classification, segmentation, and object detection, every existing grid collapses at 2-bit pre-fire membrane potentials while SpikeQ retains most of the full-precision accuracy, and at 4 bits for both weights and potentials the models stay within 2.59 points of full precision while shrinking memory 7.8-7.9x and using 6.4-6.9x less energy.
papers.why_en: Targeting spike-flip fraction rather than raw numerical error as the quantization objective offers a reusable lens for anyone designing low-precision/quantization schemes: the choice of error metric itself matters, not just the bit width.

papers.title: DIFFLET: A Fast Inference Engine for Diffusion Transformer Models on AWS Trainium
papers.abstract: On AWS Trainium2, every component of a diffusion model runs as a program compiled ahead of time for fixed shapes, while pipelines differ across models, prompt lengths across requests, and caching decisions across denoising steps. We present Difflet, a serving engine in which five model pipelines share one compilation backend, joint attention is split across cores by attention head, and a host controller decides at each denoising step whether to run the denoiser or reuse its earlier output. A small probe program computes the caching signal on the device and returns one number per step, and a resident model process keeps every program loaded across requests. Across five image and video model families, fused attention accelerates denoiser steps by 1.2-4.3x over the same framework using PyTorch/XLA attention, and at 32.8k visual tokens it is the only attention that compiles. On four of the five models, resident serving is 1.5-3.4x faster than standalone runs that reload weights from a warm file cache for each generation.
papers.ja_title: AWS Trainium 2 向け拡散モデル推論エンジン Difflet
papers.summary: AWS Trainium 2(トレーニウム 2)では拡散モデルの処理が固定 shape 向けに事前コンパイルされるため、モデルごとに違う処理の流れや可変長の入力、キャッシュ判断の扱いに困っていた。Difflet は 5 系統のモデルを 1 つのコンパイル基盤で動かし、attention(注目機構)をコア間でヘッド単位に分割し、各ステップでデノイザーを実行するか前回出力を再利用するかをホスト側で判断する仕組みを作った。5 つの画像・動画モデル群で、融合 attention は PyTorch/XLA 版より 1.2〜4.3 倍速く、常駐プロセスによるモデル保持は 5 モデル中 4 モデルで毎回の再読み込みより 1.5〜3.4 倍速かった。
papers.why: AWS Trainium(トレーニウム)上で拡散モデルを複数系統同時にサービングする実装例で、固定 shape コンパイルの制約下での attention 分割や推論時キャッシュ判断の作り方が、分散推論・サービング基盤を作る人にそのまま使える。
papers.summary_en: On AWS Trainium2, every diffusion model component is compiled ahead of time for fixed shapes, yet pipelines differ across models, prompt lengths vary across requests, and caching decisions vary across denoising steps. Difflet shares one compilation backend across five model pipelines, splits joint attention across cores by attention head, and uses a host controller to decide at each denoising step whether to run the denoiser or reuse its earlier output. Fused attention accelerates denoiser steps by 1.2-4.3x over PyTorch/XLA attention and is the only attention that compiles at 32.8k visual tokens, and resident serving is 1.5-3.4x faster than reloading weights from a warm file cache on four of five models.
papers.why_en: A concrete serving-engine design for running multiple diffusion model families on AWS Trainium under fixed-shape compilation, showing how to split attention across cores and decide caching on-device - directly reusable for anyone building distributed inference/serving infrastructure.

papers.title: BaGuaLu-2: Taming Dynamic Memory Fluctuation for Efficient MoE Model Training over 10,000 GPUs
papers.abstract: Fine-grained Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) is the de facto architecture for scaling large language models. However, dynamic expert load imbalance causes severe memory fluctuations that degrade training efficiency. Existing systems rely on static memory provisioning: they either over-provision, leaving GPU memory idle during normal execution, or under- provision, inviting out-of-memory crashes and costly manual rollbacks when load spikes occur. To address these challenges, we propose BaGuaLu-2, a large-scale MoE training system that eliminates this dilemma through flexible provisioning. By transforming memory allocation from a static, one-time tuning choice into a continuous and fine-grained control. BaGuaLu-2 grants exact activation memory on demand for each training batch. Furthermore, it offsets any dynamic management overhead through system optimizations. BaGuaLu-2 demonstrates exceptional scalability, training a model with 1040 billion parameters across 12,288 GPUs while sustaining over 2 EFlops at 35% MFU. Compared with state-of-the-art systems, BaGuaLu-2 delivers 1.14x and 1.13x average throughput improvements over Megatron-Kuai and AdaPipe, respectively.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 1万GPU超のMoE学習でメモリの急変動を抑える BaGuaLu-2
papers.summary: 細粒度 MoE(専門家混合)の学習では、どの expert に負荷が偏るかが動的に変わるため GPU メモリの使用量が大きく揺れ、学習効率を落としていた。既存システムはメモリを多めに確保して遊ばせるか、少なめに確保して急な負荷増で OOM(メモリ不足)クラッシュと手動の巻き戻しを招くかの二択だった。BaGuaLu-2 はメモリ確保を一度きりの静的な調整から学習バッチごとの継続的で細かい割り当てに変え、12,288 GPU・1,040 億パラメータのモデルで 2 EFlops 超・MFU 35% を保ちながら、Megatron-Kuai 比で平均 1.14 倍、AdaPipe 比で 1.13 倍のスループット向上を達成した。
papers.why: MoE 学習特有の動的メモリ変動を OOM と手動復旧なしに吸収する実装例で、1 万 GPU 超級の分散学習基盤を運用する人がメモリ確保戦略を見直す際の具体的な比較対象になる。
papers.summary_en: In fine-grained MoE training, dynamic expert load imbalance causes severe memory fluctuations that existing systems handle only by static over- or under-provisioning, the latter inviting OOM crashes and costly manual rollbacks. BaGuaLu-2 turns memory allocation from a static, one-time tuning choice into continuous, fine-grained per-batch control, and while training a 1040-billion-parameter model across 12,288 GPUs it sustains over 2 EFlops at 35% MFU, delivering 1.14x and 1.13x average throughput improvements over Megatron-Kuai and AdaPipe respectively.
papers.why_en: Shows a concrete way to absorb MoE's dynamic memory fluctuation without over-provisioning or OOM rollbacks at >10,000-GPU scale, giving operators of large distributed training systems a specific throughput baseline to compare memory-allocation strategies against.

papers.title: LongForge: Measuring and Improving Long-Context Instruction Data via Evidence-Assertion Reasoning Graphs
papers.abstract: Existing quality control for long-context instruction-tuning data is a one-shot judgment inside the generation pipeline that leaves only a scalar, revealing neither which document parts an answer uses nor how many reasoning steps it writes down; the data can thus be neither audited nor controlled. We formalize data quality as a property of the alignment structure among document, question, and answer, and build LongForge, which pairs an analyzer that measures long-context data with a synthesizer that generates it. The analyzer reverse-reconstructs each sample into an evidence-assertion reasoning graph and programmatically computes four dimensions on it: breadth, depth, correctness, and completeness. Every reading traces back to specific evidence spans and reasoning steps, making data auditable. Measuring seven mainstream datasets reveals two previously unquantified defects: breadth barely grows with document length, and depth is generally low, the two being nearly orthogonal. The synthesizer then embeds the analyzer into generation, gating on correctness and completeness and deferring breadth and depth to a training-time mixture over measured values, which makes the training distribution controllable. On two backbones, its two mixtures, LongForge-1 and LongForge-N, outperform the strongest baseline by 2.2-4.7 points on average over six long-context benchmarks, and in a controlled comparison that holds the gate and the candidate pool fixed, raising breadth and depth alone is worth a further 1.16 points, making the structural distribution of training data a lever on downstream quality rather than only a description of it.

papers.title: Chinese Decision: A Family of Language Models for Single-Pass Probabilistic Decision-Making
papers.abstract: Many language-based applications need a probability distribution over a small set of decisions rather than an open-ended response. We present Chinese Decision, a family of Chinese-language decision models that adapts pretrained causal language models to this interface. Each question is compiled into a shared instruction-and-candidate prompt; a single forward pass reads the final-position logits of the candidate letters and normalizes them over the valid options, without autoregressive answer generation. The interface covers Boolean judgments, categorical choices, and ordinal scores. We report three completed members built on Qwen3.5 0.8B, 2B, and 4B backbones, each trained for one epoch on the same 13.048 million decisions and released with a validation-fitted temperature and a Q8_0 quantization. On the full 307,900-decision CJ-Bench, the 4B model reaches 85.97% overall accuracy, 75.69% general-domain accuracy, and 84.00% average accuracy across medicine, law, and finance with a single checkpoint, above every reported baseline in each domain, at 1.00% expected calibration error. Between the 2B and 4B members, which share data, objective, and minimum batch, parent-clustered paired bootstrap intervals show gains in all four domains, largest in the two low-resource domains (+8.5 and +7.1 points), whereas the 2B gain over 0.8B in law is not statistically resolved. Analyses of the stored predictions further show that a single global temperature lowers pooled calibration error while worsening some domains, that larger members rank their own errors better for selective prediction, and that merging and quantization each change 0.4-1.1% of top-1 predictions while leaving aggregate metrics nearly unchanged. All comparisons rest on single training runs and imported baselines.

papers.title: OfficeTown: Generative Organizations for Evolving Agent Intelligence
papers.abstract: AI agents increasingly use files and software tools to produce professional deliverables. Such work draws on materials, decisions, and feedback accumulated across assignments. We introduce OfficeTown, a generative simulation framework for professional organizations in which tasks and their context arise from continuing organizational work. From a natural-language description of an organization's purpose and activities, OfficeTown initializes an organization whose members coordinate work, delegate bounded assignments to assistant agents, and review their deliverables. Artifacts, decisions, and unresolved matters persist and shape subsequent work, while responsibilities and permissions determine what each member can see and do. We curate work requests, their context, and review feedback into executable resources for evaluation and learning. We construct OfficeTown Bench with 406 tasks and 4,836 evaluation criteria from 23 simulated organizations across eight professional domains, incorporating domain-expert feedback. Frontier-model evaluations reveal substantial remaining headroom. Supervised fine-tuning and on-policy distillation on OfficeTown data substantially improve Qwen3.5-9B on external professional-work benchmarks, including GDPval. Supplementary evaluations show that the principal--assistant harness achieves higher scores than the single- and multi-agent baselines tested. These results highlight the value of organizational simulation in generating work-grounded data and environments for the continued development of generalist agents.

papers.title: Process Reward Modeling with Reliability- and Conservatism-Aware Bayesian Belief
papers.abstract: Process Reward Models (PRMs) play a central role in test-time scaling for large language model (LLM) reasoning. However, PRMs may provide inaccurate process rewards for test-time scaling, which we identify as arising from two sources of uncertainty: (1) \textit{PRM uncertainty} that arises from insufficient supervision data and imperfect PRM training; and (2) \textit{policy uncertainty} that results from the mismatch between the policy to collect supervision data and the policy for test-time scaling, leading to systematic reward overestimation. Previous studies fail to jointly consider both uncertainties. To bridge this gap, we propose BayesianPRM, which treats the process reward as a random variable within a reward hypothesis space and maintains a Bayesian belief over it. Since exact Bayesian inference over the continuous hypothesis space is generally intractable, we discretize the reward hypothesis space with a reward ensemble and introduce two complementary belief updates, each targeting one source of uncertainty: (1) to address PRM uncertainty, we introduce \textit{reliability-aware belief updating} that measures how well each ensemble member explains the supervision data and updates the belief with an amortized belief network optimized by the evidence lower bound (ELBO); and (2) to tackle policy uncertainty, we propose \textit{conservatism-aware belief calibration} which further reweights the belief toward lower rewards to suppress overestimation. These two updates yield a reliability- and conservatism-aware Bayesian belief, whose expectation determines the process reward. Experiments on multimodal reasoning benchmarks indicate that BayesianPRM consistently yields more accurate process reward estimates while enhancing test-time scaling performance.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: PRM(プロセス報酬モデル)の過大評価をベイズ的信念で抑える BayesianPRM
papers.summary: プロセス報酬モデル(PRM)は推論の途中経過に点数をつけてテスト時のスケーリングを支えるが、教師データ不足による PRM 自体の不確実性と、教師データを集めた方策とテスト時に使う方策のずれによる報酬の過大評価という 2 種類の不確実性を同時に扱えていなかった。BayesianPRM は報酬をアンサンブルで離散化した仮説空間上のベイズ的信念として持ち、各メンバーが教師データをどれだけ説明できるかで信念を更新する「信頼性を考慮した更新」と、過大評価を抑えるため低い報酬側へ信念を寄せる「保守性を考慮した補正」を組み合わせる。マルチモーダル推論ベンチマークで、より正確なプロセス報酬の推定とテスト時スケーリング性能の向上を一貫して確認した。
papers.why: テスト時スケーリングで使う検証器(verifier)の信頼度をどう定量化し過大評価を補正するかという、RL 後学習・推論時スケーリング基盤でよく出る課題への具体的な対処法を示す。
papers.summary_en: Process Reward Models (PRMs) support test-time scaling by scoring reasoning steps, but prior work has not jointly handled PRM uncertainty from insufficient supervision data and policy uncertainty from the mismatch between the policy that collected supervision and the policy used at test time, which causes systematic reward overestimation. BayesianPRM discretizes the reward hypothesis space with a reward ensemble and maintains a Bayesian belief via reliability-aware belief updating (how well each ensemble member explains the supervision data, via an ELBO-optimized amortized network) combined with conservatism-aware belief calibration that reweights toward lower rewards. On multimodal reasoning benchmarks, it consistently yields more accurate process reward estimates while enhancing test-time scaling performance.
papers.why_en: Gives a concrete way to quantify and correct for verifier overestimation in test-time scaling, a recurring problem for anyone building RL post-training or inference-time scaling infrastructure.

papers.title: Sample, Mix, or Verify? Allocating Test-Time Compute under Imperfect Verifiers
papers.abstract: A common way to make language models and agents more accurate is to spend more compute at inference time: generate many candidate solutions and submit the one a verifier prefers. Success then requires that some candidate is correct and that the verifier picks it. The first grows predictably with the number of samples; the second does not, because real verifiers (unit tests, majority votes, LLM judges, reward models) accept wrong answers, reject right ones, and make correlated mistakes. With a fixed budget, a practitioner must decide how many samples to draw, which models to draw them from, and how much to spend on verification, and today these choices are made by rules of thumb. We introduce SPLIT, which makes them from a small labelled pilot. It rests on an exact formula for the probability of submitting a correct answer under accept/reject and top-score selection that accounts for varying task difficulty, blind spots shared across models, and correlated repeated verifier calls. SPLIT fits the formula by empirical Bayes and uses it to plan budgets on unseen tasks. Across seven benchmarks spanning math, science QA, code and software-engineering agents, 26 models, 175 agent systems and six kinds of real verifiers, all from public releases, SPLIT lands within 0.02-0.8 percentage points of the best allocation in hindsight, while every fixed rule we test loses at least 2.5 points in some setting. Regret depends only on how well SPLIT ranks configurations, and it stays near-optimal under compute, price and latency costs and online. The formula also explains when asking more LLM judges lowers precision. As a forecaster far beyond the pilot, SPLIT beats power-law fitting when the verifier caps success, and we report where it loses.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 検証器が不完全なときのテスト時計算配分を小さな試験データから決める SPLIT
papers.summary: LLM やエージェントの精度をテスト時に上げる定番の方法は、候補をたくさん作って検証器(verifier)が選んだものを出すことだが、サンプル数をいくつにし、どのモデルから取り、検証にどれだけ費やすかは経験則で決められていた。SPLIT は少量の正解付き試験データから、タスクの難しさのばらつき・モデル間で共有される盲点・検証呼び出しの相関まで考慮した正解提出確率の厳密な式を経験ベイズで当てはめ、未知のタスクでの計算配分を決める。数学・科学 QA・コード・ソフトウェア工程の 7 つのベンチマーク、26 モデル、175 のエージェント系、6 種類の検証器で、SPLIT は事後最適配分とのズレが 0.02〜0.8 ポイントに収まり、試した経験則はどれかの場面で最低 2.5 ポイント以上劣っていた。
papers.why: 検証器(verifier)付きのテスト時スケーリングで、サンプル数・モデル選択・検証予算の配分を経験則任せにせず実測から決める枠組みで、ルーティングやテスト時計算の予算設計をしている人にそのまま効く。
papers.summary_en: Making LLMs and agents more accurate at test time by generating many candidates and submitting the one a verifier prefers requires choosing sample count, model mix, and verification spend, decisions usually made by rules of thumb; real verifiers accept wrong answers, reject right ones, and make correlated mistakes. SPLIT fits an exact formula for the probability of submitting a correct answer, accounting for varying task difficulty, blind spots shared across models, and correlated repeated verifier calls, via empirical Bayes from a small labelled pilot, then plans budgets on unseen tasks. Across seven benchmarks, 26 models, 175 agent systems and six kinds of real verifiers, SPLIT lands within 0.02-0.8 percentage points of the best allocation in hindsight, while every fixed rule tested loses at least 2.5 points in some setting.
papers.why_en: A framework for setting sample count, model choice, and verification budget under test-time scaling from measured data rather than rules of thumb - directly useful for anyone designing routing or test-time compute budgets.

papers.title: ADT: All-Atom Diffusion Tokenizer for 3D Molecular Structures
papers.abstract: Discrete structural tokenization provides a promising route to autoregressive 3D molecular generation. Yet, existing tokenizers face a trade-off between compact representation and all-atom reconstruction: atom-level tokens preserve atomic details but produce long sequences, while compact residue-level protein tokens typically omit side-chain geometry. To overcome this limitation, we propose All-atom Diffusion Tokenizer (ADT), which decouples token granularity from reconstruction resolution. ADT uses one structural token per atom for small molecules and one token per protein residue that jointly represents backbone and side-chain geometry. To mitigate geometric distortion introduced by quantization, we leverage the generative capacity of diffusion models to recover fine-grained atomic geometry beyond deterministic decoding from discrete tokens. Extensive experiments across small molecules and proteins demonstrate that ADT achieves strong reconstruction from compact discrete representations while enabling high-quality autoregressive generation of both small molecules and all-atom protein structures. These results establish compact structural tokens as an effective discrete interface for all-atom molecular reconstruction and generation.

papers.title: Distributed Performance Boosting through Neural Control for Plug-and-Play Networks
papers.abstract: We address the problem of improving the performance of pre-stabilized networked systems subject to plug-and-play (PnP) operations, namely additions or removals of subsystems. While distributed baseline controllers can preserve stability after a PnP transition, augmenting them with expressive neural policies can invalidate the formal stability guarantees. To overcome this issue, we build on recently proposed Performance Boosting controllers based on the Internal Model Control (IMC) principle, which reduce closed-loop stability to a finite $\ell_2$-gain requirement on an auxiliary operator. In the distributed setting, this operator is formed by interconnecting local neural operators that exchange information only between neighboring subsystems. We then derive free parametrizations of this interconnection, namely explicit maps from unconstrained trainable variables to interconnected neural operators satisfying a prescribed network gain bound for every parameter value. The obtained distributed neural controller can therefore be trained by unconstrained gradient-based optimization without stability constraints or projection steps, while retaining the prescribed gain bound at every training iterate. We develop two complementary parametrizations. A neighbor-based compositional parametrization uses local coupling bounds, so that after a PnP event only subsystems whose bounds change need to update their gain parameters. A network-norm parametrization instead uses a bound on the overall coupling matrix and can reduce conservatism, at the price of requiring network-wide information. A PnP DC-microgrid case study shows that the proposed neural layer improves voltage transients under topology changes and load variations while preserving nominal closed-loop stability.

papers.title: SimOPD: Relational Knowledge Transfer for On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract: A key challenge in on-policy distillation (OPD) is extracting effective supervision from teacher knowledge. Supervision from token probabilities may underutilize internal knowledge, while direct hidden-state matching forces the student to shift to the teacher's feature space and complicates cross-architecture transfer. Inspired by contrastive learning's use of relationships between instances, we propose \textbf{SimOPD} to transfer teacher internal knowledge through response similarities. Specifically, SimOPD uses paired memory banks of student-generated responses to extract supervision from the teacher's internal representations as similarity distributions. The student then matches these distributions within its own representation space, retaining representational freedom and removing the need for cross-model projection. Extensive experiments show that SimOPD improves the overall average over the strongest baselines by up to 2.6 and 3.1 percentage points in same- and cross-architecture settings.
papers.ja_title: 応答の類似度で教師の知識を転写する蒸留手法 SimOPD
papers.summary: on-policy 蒸留(distillation、教師モデルの出力を使って生徒モデルを学習させる方法)では、トークンの確率だけでは教師の知識を十分に使えず、隠れ層を直接揃える方法はアーキテクチャが違うと使いにくい。SimOPD は生徒が生成した応答のペアを記憶バンクに貯め、教師の内部表現から求めた応答同士の類似度分布を生徒自身の表現空間内で模倣させる。実験では、同じアーキテクチャの教師生徒で最大 2.6 ポイント、違うアーキテクチャの組でも最大 3.1 ポイント、既存の最強手法より平均精度が上がった。
papers.why: アーキテクチャが異なる教師生徒間でも使える蒸留の手がかりとして、応答間の類似度という新しい信号を示した点が RL 後学習・蒸留基盤の設計に使える。
papers.summary_en: On-policy distillation struggles to extract useful supervision from a teacher: token-probability supervision underuses internal knowledge, while direct hidden-state matching forces the student into the teacher's feature space and complicates cross-architecture transfer. SimOPD instead uses paired memory banks of student-generated responses to turn the teacher's internal representations into similarity distributions, which the student matches within its own representation space. SimOPD improves the overall average over the strongest baselines by up to 2.6 points in same-architecture and 3.1 points in cross-architecture settings.
papers.why_en: Response-similarity supervision offers a projection-free way to transfer teacher knowledge across differing student/teacher architectures, which is directly useful for building distillation and RL post-training pipelines.

papers.title: GUMPIM: Unitary and Malleable Memory for Processing-in-Memory with Guaranteed PIM Pages
papers.abstract: DRAM-based Processing-in-Memory (PIM) addresses the "memory wall" by executing computations directly inside main memory. However, memory interleaving and virtual memory limit contiguous data size visible to PIM units, constraining PIM task granularity. To mitigate this, existing PIM systems drastically isolate PIM memory or disable memory interleaving. These design choices, however, decrease the CPU memory bandwidth and introduce extra data transfer, leading to an additional "system memory wall" that must be resolved to realize PIM's full potential. In this work, we propose GUMPIM, a PIM system that allows interleaved CPU pages and non-interleaved PIM pages to coexist in a Unitary and Malleable memory space with Guaranteed PIM page allocation. GUMPIM enables zero-copy during PIM task offloading and maintains CPU memory bandwidth while ensuring low PIM offloading overhead. First, we propose a dual-track memory management mechanism consisting of independent page allocation and address translation for CPU and PIM pages. Second, we design GUMPIM interface hardware on PIM-enabled DRAMs to provide a dynamic address mapping for the different data layouts of CPU and PIM pages. Third, we propose a PIM-assisted page migration mechanism that transparently migrates pages while preserving CPU access bandwidth, thereby enabling guaranteed and accelerated PIM page allocation. GUMPIM requires no changes to commodity DRAM standards; all hardware modifications are limited to the DRAM side, ensuring full compatibility with existing CPUs and enabling immediate deployment on current HBMx- and LPDDRx-based PIM platforms. Our results show only <0.1% performance degradation for CPU workloads on GUMPIM. For PIM workloads, GUMPIM reduces memory allocation and CPU-part computation times by 2.7x and 4.93x, respectively, yielding an end-to-end 2.3x speedup over a state-of-the-art baseline system.

papers.title: Trajectory-Triggered Sparse Collaborative Decoding
papers.abstract: Dense assistance methods such as speculative decoding repeatedly verify draft tokens with a target model, keeping target computation coupled to generation. We study sparse collaborative decoding, where a draft model generates most tokens and a target model is invoked only for short corrective segments. The key problem is deciding when to call the target. We show that local uncertainty is a weak trigger: entropy, negative log-likelihood, logit margin, top-$k$ mass, and velocity features give near-chance failure prediction, with AUC 0.50-0.53. In contrast, aggregate trajectory-shape features over the draft confidence path reach AUC 0.86 using a lightweight logistic predictor trained only from draft correctness labels. This induces a trigger-timing tradeoff: early calls have more leverage but weaker evidence, while later calls have stronger evidence but less ability to redirect the trajectory. Used online, learned sparse collaborative decoding improves over the best open-loop schedule by +5.3 to +20.0 accuracy points across five GSM8K draft-target pairs. On MATH-500, it gains 7.0-13.5 points when early prediction and target competence align, but loses when either is weak. On StrategyQA, it improves over open-loop by 5.0-8.3 points, showing transfer beyond arithmetics.
papers.ja_title: どこで本物のモデルを呼ぶか軌跡の形で決める疎な協調デコード
papers.summary: speculative decoding(投機的デコード、小さい draft モデルが候補トークンを作り大きい target モデルが検証する手法)は target モデルを毎トークン呼ぶ必要がある。本研究は target を短い訂正区間だけ呼ぶ「疎な協調デコード」を調べ、エントロピーなど局所的な不確実性指標では呼ぶべき場所をほぼ当てられない(AUC 0.50〜0.53、コイン投げ相当)ことを示した。一方、draft の確信度の変化を軌跡としてまとめた特徴なら AUC 0.86 まで当てられ、オンラインで使うと GSM8K で開いた(open-loop)方式より最大 20.0 ポイント精度が上がった。
papers.why: 投機的デコードで「いつ大きいモデルを呼ぶか」を決める指標として、局所的な不確実性ではなく確信度の軌跡を使うべきだという具体的な設計指針を示している。
papers.summary_en: Dense assistance methods like speculative decoding repeatedly verify draft tokens with a target model, keeping target computation tightly coupled to generation. The authors show local uncertainty features (entropy, NLL, logit margin, top-k mass, velocity) are weak triggers for deciding when to call the target (AUC 0.50-0.53, near chance), whereas aggregate trajectory-shape features over the draft confidence path reach AUC 0.86 with a lightweight logistic predictor. Used online, the learned trigger improves over the best open-loop schedule by +5.3 to +20.0 accuracy points across five GSM8K draft-target pairs, with further gains on MATH-500 and StrategyQA.
papers.why_en: It gives a concrete, measured answer to when a draft model should call the expensive target model, showing that naive per-token uncertainty signals fail while trajectory-shape features work, which matters for anyone designing collaborative/speculative decoding triggers.

review.note: 直感的に良さそうな局所指標(エントロピーなど)をまず測って AUC 0.5 程度の弱さを確認し、その上で実際に効く指標(確信度の軌跡の形、AUC 0.86)と比べて示す、という評価設計の進め方。
review.note_en: Measure the intuitively plausible local signals first and show they are near chance (AUC ~0.5), then demonstrate what actually works (trajectory-shape features, AUC 0.86) - a template for evaluating a trigger/predictor design.

papers.title: TUPLE-Bench: Evaluating and Mitigating Privacy-Utility Trade-offs in Typed Decision Models
papers.abstract: Typed decision models often return more than a selected category. They also expose probabilities for each candidate and, sometimes, a separate confidence score. These fields support downstream decisions but may reveal information beyond a recipient's authorization. We introduce TUPLE-Bench (Typed decision models' Utility and Privacy Leakage Evaluation Benchmark), a benchmark of paired synthetic cases in which recipients may learn a coarse operational category but not its fine-grained cause. Across nine models, instructions to withhold the cause fail to protect it: 91.88%-99.93% of responses reveal the cause through direct selection or residual scores. Even when causes are excluded from the candidate set, full outputs enable 62.85%-75.35% recovery on held-out cases, compared with 51.04%-57.64% using only the selected category (50% chance). Full outputs also reduce mean downstream cost in all 27 model-task comparisons. However, confidence fields increase leakage without consistently reducing cost. We further introduce workflow-constrained privacy quantization (WCPQ), which reduces secret recovery while preserving the behavior and cost of specified downstream workflows. Our findings highlight the need to audit decision interfaces field by field and workflow by workflow.

papers.title: Agentic AI for Heterogeneous System Design Across Chip, Scale-Up, and Scale-Out Domains
papers.abstract: The design space of modern AI/HPC systems has expanded rapidly across compute architectures, including GPUs, dataflow processors, and RISC-V accelerators; memory tech- nologies, including HBM, GDDR, and SRAM; and interconnects such as NVLink, UALink, Infinity Fabric, InfiniBand, Slingshot, and Ultra Ethernet. No single architecture is optimal across LLM training, LLM serving, and AI-coupled HPC workloads, while the resulting combinatorial design space is too large for manual exploration. We present ArchAgent, a hierarchical multi- agent framework in which an LLM-based planner decomposes system design into chip, scale-up, and scale-out subproblems, each handled by specialist agents. A deterministic analytical evaluator closes the loop, ensuring that all performance estimates are derived from analytical models rather than generated by the LLM. On a mixed AI+HPC workload under a 1 MW power budget, ArchAgent discovers heterogeneous designs that achieve a 1.93x weighted geometric mean speedup over a homogeneous GPU baseline, while requiring only 18 evaluations compared with 100 evaluations for hill climbing, which achieves 1.65x speedup.
topics: 集団通信・ネットワーク
papers.theme: 集団通信・ネットワーク
papers.ja_title: チップから機器間・機器間ネットワークまでをエージェントで設計する ArchAgent
papers.summary: GPU・データフロー・RISC-V などの計算器、HBM/GDDR/SRAM などのメモリ、NVLink/UALink/InfiniBand などの相互接続(interconnect、機器をつなぐ通信経路)を組み合わせる AI/HPC システムの設計空間は広すぎて人手で探索できない。ArchAgent は LLM の計画役がチップ・scale-up(機器内接続)・scale-out(機器間接続)の 3 つに設計を分け、各担当エージェントの性能評価を決定論的な解析モデルに任せる仕組みを提案した。1 MW の電力制約下の混合 AI+HPC 負荷で、同種 GPU 構成より 1.93 倍の速度向上を 18 回の評価で見つけ、山登り法の 100 回評価・1.65 倍を上回った。
papers.why: LLM の学習・推論基盤を支える計算機・ネットワーク構成の探索を、LLM 自身の憶測ではなく解析モデルで裏付けながら少ない評価回数で進める具体的な枠組みを示している。
papers.summary_en: The design space of modern AI/HPC systems spans compute architectures (GPUs, dataflow processors, RISC-V accelerators), memory technologies (HBM, GDDR, SRAM), and interconnects (NVLink, UALink, Infinity Fabric, InfiniBand, Slingshot, Ultra Ethernet), and is too large to explore manually. ArchAgent is a hierarchical multi-agent framework where an LLM-based planner decomposes system design into chip, scale-up, and scale-out subproblems handled by specialist agents, with a deterministic analytical evaluator ensuring all performance estimates come from analytical models rather than the LLM. On a mixed AI+HPC workload under a 1 MW power budget, ArchAgent finds heterogeneous designs reaching a 1.93x weighted geometric-mean speedup over a homogeneous GPU baseline using only 18 evaluations, versus 100 evaluations for hill climbing's 1.65x.
papers.why_en: It offers a concrete agentic framework for exploring compute/memory/interconnect design choices for AI training and serving infrastructure, with the LLM's role bounded by a deterministic evaluator rather than self-reported numbers.

papers.title: Escaping Parameter Space: Tight Generalization Bounds via Representation Quality
papers.abstract: We derive a tight generalization bound for deterministic neural We derive a tight generalization bound for deterministic neural networks based on their last hidden layer representations. By evaluating representation quality with a parameter-free $k$-nearest-neighbor ($k$-NN) classifier, our certificate avoids traditional parameter-space complexity measures, KL divergences to a posterior, weight norms, and compression. The bound is tight: trained from scratch, it reaches an 8.0 percentage point gap to test error on CIFAR-10 (ResNet-18) and yields the first non-vacuous certificates we are aware of on CIFAR-100; with frozen DINOv2 representations, it certifies at 1.4\% on CIFAR-10 and 23.1\% on 1,000-class ImageNet. It decomposes additively into three empirical, independently measurable quantities: local class geometry ($k$-NN decoder error), decoder-network agreement, and training stability. This allows the bound to act as a diagnostic tool: we demonstrate that actively destroying local class geometry eliminates generalization while leaving dataset memorization intact, identifying class geometry as a causally relevant mechanism for generalization. Finally, we show that learned representations are significantly less sensitive to weight noise than linear readouts, suggesting why parameter-space certificates often struggle to remain tight.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング

papers.title: DLite: History-free Speculative Decoding for Agentic AI
papers.abstract: Speculative decoding has become a mainstream technique for accelerating large language model (LLM) inference by using a lightweight draft model to generate candidate tokens that are subsequently verified by the target model. However, agentic workloads introduce long and continuously evolving contexts and frequent multi-turn interactions. Under such workloads, we observe that existing draft models suffer from up to an 80% degradation in acceptance length, while maintaining their historical KV cache introduces substantial system overhead. In this paper, we identify the growing historical context as a common source of both problems and introduce DLite, a history-free speculative decoding framework for agentic AI. DLite directly reuses contextual hidden states from the target model and performs local speculative prediction without explicitly maintaining the historical context, transforming an increasingly complex modeling problem into local simple prediction problem. A lightweight sequential head further restores intra-block causal dependencies with low overhead. To effectively train this heterogeneous history-free architecture, we introduce a tailored two-stage training strategy. Experiments on general-purpose, long-context and agentic workloads show that DLite achieves 2-6 acceptance length and outperforms the state-of-the-art speculative decoding method, DSpark, up to 70%.
papers.ja_title: 履歴を持たない投機的デコードでエージェント型推論を高速化する DLite
papers.summary: エージェント型(agentic)の利用では文脈が長く続けて変わり続けるため、既存の draft モデルは受理長(一致して採用されるトークン数)が最大 80% 落ち、過去の KV キャッシュを保持すると負荷も増える。DLite は target モデルの文脈に対応した隠れ状態をそのまま使い、過去の履歴を明示的に保持せずに局所的な予測だけを行う手法で、軽量な逐次ヘッドで block 内の因果関係も補う。2 段階の学習により、一般・長文脈・エージェント型の負荷で受理長が 2〜6 倍になり、既存最良手法 DSpark を最大 70% 上回った。
papers.why: 文脈が増え続けるエージェント型の推論で投機的デコードが遅くなる原因を履歴の肥大化と特定し、履歴を持たない設計で解決した点が、エージェント実行基盤の高速化に直結する。
papers.summary_en: Agentic workloads bring long, continuously evolving contexts and frequent multi-turn interactions, under which existing draft models suffer up to an 80% degradation in acceptance length while maintaining their historical KV cache adds substantial overhead. DLite identifies the growing historical context as the common cause of both problems and instead reuses contextual hidden states from the target model to perform local speculative prediction without explicitly maintaining history, with a lightweight sequential head restoring intra-block causal dependencies. On general-purpose, long-context, and agentic workloads, DLite achieves 2-6x acceptance length and outperforms the state-of-the-art method DSpark by up to 70%.
papers.why_en: It pins down context growth as the shared root cause behind both accuracy and overhead problems in speculative decoding for agentic inference, and removes it architecturally rather than patching around it.

papers.title: FuTransformer: FP8 prefill and INT4 decode for Llama-style inference on Hopper
papers.abstract: Transformer prefill reuses weights across tokens and is dominated by matrix multiplication and activation data movement; single-token decode has limited reuse and is dominated by weight and KV-cache reads. We present FUTRANSFORMER, a CUDA implementation of a Llama-style Transformer block for NVIDIA Hopper GPUs. It applies CODA's GEMM-plus-epilogue approach to inference, adding direct KV-cache placement, folding the fixed RMSNorm gain into weights, writing FP8 output directly with delayed scaling, and supporting prefill without padding. Decode uses INT4 projection weights and an INT4 KV-cache copy. Weights and keys follow Tensor Core fragment layouts for direct dequantization into MMA operands without full intermediate tiles. A block-diagonal Hadamard transform reduces cache quantization error from outlier channels. On one H100, prefill is up to 1.48x faster than compiled PyTorch FP8 and reaches 1.29 PFLOP/s. For gate/up projection with SwiGLU at the 8B shape, our BF16 path is 1.13x faster than CODA. Our FP8 path is 2.02-2.18x faster than the evaluated BF16 CODA path. Across 8B and 70B shapes at batches 1-32, INT4 decode is 1.3-2.4x faster than the faster of PyTorch's BF16 and INT4 blocks at each point: 2.1-3.3x faster than compiled, CUDA-graphed BF16 and 1.3-6.3x faster than the same block using PyTorch's INT4 projection kernel, which targets a single query row and loses to BF16 at batch 32. It is also 31-51% faster than our FP8 path. Complete Llama-3.1-8B decode takes 2.8 ms per step at batch one, versus 8.1 ms for the compiled transformers implementation. Decoding every WikiText-2 token through the INT4 weight path raises perplexity from 6.24 to 7.23 with round-to-nearest weights or 6.99 with GPTQ in the same format; the rotated INT4 cache adds 0.20. The kernels match a quantized reference computation within 0.001 perplexity.
papers.ja_title: Hopper 向け prefill は FP8・decode は INT4 で動かす FuTransformer
papers.summary: Transformer の prefill(入力をまとめて処理する段階)は重みを再利用できて行列積中心、decode(1トークンずつ生成する段階)は重みと KV キャッシュの読み出しが中心になる。FuTransformer は H100 向けに、prefill を FP8 で直接書き出し、decode を INT4 の射影重みと INT4 の KV キャッシュで処理する CUDA 実装で、outlier チャネルの誤差を block 単位の Hadamard 変換で抑える。prefill はコンパイル済み PyTorch FP8 より最大 1.48 倍速く 1.29 PFLOP/s に達し、decode は INT4 により PyTorch の最速経路より 1.3〜2.4 倍速く、Llama-3.1-8B の 1 ステップが 2.8 ms(コンパイル済み実装は 8.1 ms)になった。
papers.why: prefill と decode で演算の性質が違う点に合わせて精度(FP8/INT4)とカーネルを別々に最適化する具体的な実装例として、サービング基盤のカーネル設計にそのまま参考になる。
papers.summary_en: Transformer prefill reuses weights across tokens and is dominated by matrix multiplication, while single-token decode has limited reuse and is dominated by weight and KV-cache reads. FuTransformer is a CUDA implementation for Hopper GPUs that writes FP8 output directly with delayed scaling for prefill and uses INT4 projection weights with an INT4 KV-cache for decode, using a block-diagonal Hadamard transform to reduce cache quantization error from outlier channels. On one H100, prefill reaches 1.29 PFLOP/s (up to 1.48x faster than compiled PyTorch FP8), INT4 decode is 1.3-2.4x faster than the faster of PyTorch's BF16/INT4 paths, and complete Llama-3.1-8B decode takes 2.8 ms per step versus 8.1 ms for compiled transformers.
papers.why_en: It is a concrete, measured template for splitting precision and kernel design between prefill and decode according to their different compute/memory characteristics, directly applicable to serving-stack kernel work.

papers.title: PACE: Pareto-Adaptive Compression for Efficient Native MLLMs
papers.abstract: Native multimodal large language models (native MLLMs) jointly encode visual and linguistic sequences within a unified autoregressive Transformer, emerging as a promising paradigm for multimodal understanding. Unlike conventional ViT-based MLLMs relying on external vision encoders, ViT-free native MLLMs tokenize pixel patches directly, potentially suffering severe visual token redundancy. A pilot study confirms this: unlike ViT-based models that degrade under compression, ViT-free MLLMs tolerate aggressive compression with near-lossless or even improved performance. Yet existing compression methods target ViT-based settings, leaving native MLLMs, which stand to gain the most, unexplored. To close this gap, we introduce an analysis pipeline centered on token discriminability and cross-dimensional heterogeneous redundancy, revealing that (i) redundancy is distributed independently and heterogeneously along height and width axes, and (ii) early-layer visual tokens are indiscriminable and uniformly redundant. Guided by these findings, we propose PACE (Pareto-Adaptive Compression for Efficient Native MLLMs), the first visual token compression framework tailored for native MLLMs with Multimodal-RoPE. Leveraging dimensional decoupling of positional encoding, PACE decomposes attention into two orthogonal spatial saliency estimates along height and width, gated by a positional attention signal, yielding direction-aware importance with negligible overhead. It further casts token budget allocation as Pareto optimization over performance preservation, inference efficiency, and spatial coverage, jointly identifying optimal compression depths and retention ratios. Experiments show PACE maintains near-lossless performance at only 25%-50% visual token retention, even improving several benchmarks, while delivering over 2x FLOPs reduction.
papers.ja_title: 位置情報を使って視覚トークンを削る native MLLM 圧縮 PACE
papers.summary: ピクセルを直接トークン化する ViT を使わない native MLLM(マルチモーダル大規模言語モデル)は視覚トークンの重複が多く、既存の圧縮手法は ViT 前提のため使えなかった。PACE は Multimodal-RoPE の位置情報を高さと幅の 2 方向に分けて注目度を計算し、どの層で・どれだけトークンを残すかを性能・速度・空間的な網羅性のパレート最適化として決める。視覚トークンを 25〜50% しか残さなくてもほぼ性能が落ちず(一部ベンチマークでは向上)、FLOPs(計算量)を 2 倍以上削減した。
papers.why: native MLLM 特有の視覚トークンの冗長性の偏りを位置情報の分解で捉え、どこをどれだけ削るかを自動で決める点が、マルチモーダル推論のサービング効率化にそのまま使える。
papers.summary_en: Native MLLMs that tokenize pixel patches directly, without a ViT encoder, suffer from severe visual token redundancy that existing ViT-oriented compression methods do not address. PACE decomposes attention into two orthogonal spatial saliency estimates along height and width using the dimensional decoupling of Multimodal-RoPE, and casts token budget allocation as Pareto optimization over performance preservation, inference efficiency, and spatial coverage. PACE maintains near-lossless performance (sometimes improving benchmarks) at only 25%-50% visual token retention while delivering over 2x FLOPs reduction.
papers.why_en: It shows how to exploit the positional structure specific to native (ViT-free) MLLMs to decide automatically where and how much to compress visual tokens, which is directly applicable to making multimodal inference serving cheaper.

papers.title: Alliance of Stochastic Routing and Reinforcement Fusion for Multi-Model Reasoning
papers.abstract: This paper studies dynamic model routing under uncertainty in multimodal settings, where a system must select and potentially compose multiple models to answer a query. Standard reinforcement learning approaches for routing often suffer from premature convergence to suboptimal models due to noisy rewards and insufficient exploration. We propose a unified vision-language framework (VL-Scout) for efficient multimodal and multi-step reasoning with turn-based reinforcement fusion. First, VL-Scout combines Bayesian priors, policy gradient optimization, and sequential decision-making to enable structured exploration and adaptive inference. A context-dependent Dirichlet belief model allows for epistemic uncertainty over model quality and is updated online based on observed rewards and context-specific evidence, enabling Thompson-style exploration while serving as a prior for regularization. Second, a routing policy is trained via a KL-regularized REINFORCE objective by maximizing a reward-weighted evidence lower bound, where the policy acts as an amortized posterior, and the Dirichlet belief serves as a prior. Third, we introduce a fusion policy trained with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) or Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR), which operates over intermediate model rationales and selects between two actions: CONTINUE or ANSWER, terminating with a generated output. We evaluate VL-Scout on four representative multi-modal benchmarks (MMMU, MMMU-Pro, OKVQA, and RealWorldQA), compared against 11 representative routing and policy optimization baselines. Our method provides consistent performance improvements while reducing premature policy collapse. These results highlight the importance of integrating uncertainty-aware priors with both amortized policy learning and sequential fusion for robust and efficient model selection in discrete action spaces

papers.title: TorchTPU - A Hybrid Eager/Compiled Architecture for Native PyTorch Execution on TPU
papers.abstract: TorchTPU is an open-source collaboration between Google and Meta that introduces a native and principled PyTorch backend for Google TPUs. It enables seamless out-of-the-box model execution and TPU migration while delivering industry-competitive inference and training performance through eager execution optimizations, torch.compile integration, and native hardware acceleration.
papers.ja_title: Google と Meta が作った TPU 向けのネイティブ PyTorch バックエンド TorchTPU
papers.summary: PyTorch のモデルを Google の TPU (専用演算チップ) で動かすには、書き換えや移植の手間がかかるという困りごとがあった。Google と Meta は共同で、即時実行 (eager) と torch.compile によるコンパイル実行を組み合わせたネイティブな PyTorch バックエンド TorchTPU を作り、モデルをそのまま TPU に移植できて業界競争力のある学習・推論性能が出るとしている。
papers.why: 分散学習の基盤を作る人にとって、TPU 上で PyTorch を書き換えずに動かせる公式な経路ができたことが新しい。
papers.summary_en: TorchTPU is an open-source collaboration between Google and Meta that introduces a native and principled PyTorch backend for Google TPUs, enabling seamless out-of-the-box model execution and TPU migration while delivering industry-competitive inference and training performance through eager execution optimizations, torch.compile integration, and native hardware acceleration.
papers.why_en: Gives infra builders an official, unmodified-PyTorch path onto TPUs instead of a separate TPU-specific rewrite.

papers.title: Muon Operates Beyond the Edge of Stability
papers.abstract: We study the Muon optimizer using sharpness and provide the first empirical evidence that the Flat Minima Hypothesis also applies to Muon. Further, we derive Muon's implicit preconditioner to analyze its potential Edge of Stability behavior. Experiments on CIFAR-10 show sharpness strongly correlates with generalization gap within each optimizer (Pearson $r = 0.45$-$0.69$, $p \leq 10^{-4}$), confirming the hypothesis holds for Muon similarly to Adam and SGD. However, Muon operates above the classical sharpness-based Adaptive Edge of Stability threshold that bounds diagonally-preconditioned optimizers like Adam and RMSprop, yet remains stable. Our findings suggest Muon operates in a fundamentally different regime than diagonally-adaptive methods. Defining the exact stability boundary for Muon remains an open question. All code is available at https://github.com/NikoCovic/DL-project.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: Muon は Adam や RMSprop を縛る「安定性の限界」を超えても安定して動く
papers.summary: 最適化手法 (optimizer) Muon が、Adam や SGD のような従来法が従う「安定性の限界 (Edge of Stability)」をどう超えているのかは分かっていなかった。筆者らは CIFAR-10 で実験し、鋭さ (sharpness) と汎化性能の差 (generalization gap) が各手法の中でピアソン相関 r=0.45-0.69 (p≤10^-4) で強く結びつくことを確認し、「平らな最小値仮説 (Flat Minima Hypothesis)」が Muon にも当てはまることを示した。一方で Muon は、Adam や RMSprop など対角成分だけで調整する手法を縛る従来の安定性の境界を超えても安定して動作し、全く別の体制で動いていることを示した。
papers.why: 学習効率・スケーリングの基盤を作る人にとって、新しい最適化手法を大規模学習で使う際の安定性の判断材料になる。
papers.summary_en: The authors study the Muon optimizer using sharpness and provide the first empirical evidence that the Flat Minima Hypothesis also applies to Muon; on CIFAR-10, sharpness strongly correlates with generalization gap within each optimizer (Pearson r = 0.45-0.69, p <= 10^-4), confirming the hypothesis holds for Muon similarly to Adam and SGD.
