However, Muon operates above the classical sharpness-based Adaptive Edge of Stability threshold that bounds diagonally-preconditioned optimizers like Adam and RMSprop, yet remains stable, suggesting Muon operates in a fundamentally different regime.
papers.why_en: Offers a stability lens for deciding whether to trust Muon-style optimizers at scale, beyond the Adam/SGD intuition.

papers.title: VERAS: Verification-Guided Adaptive Search for Reliable Operations Research
papers.abstract: Advances in reasoning, coding, and tool use enable LLM agents to solve operations research (OR) problems through iterative problem modeling, program construction, and verification. Yet passing self-authored verification does not ensure that the solutions satisfy task constraints and meet optimization quality. This gap can arise from correlated specification errors, where the generated program and its checks share omissions or misinterpretations of task requirements, alongside incomplete verification coverage and ineffective optimization strategies. We propose VERAS, a verification-guided adaptive search harness for reliable OR that uses verification evidence to prioritize feasibility repair, constraint-coverage review, and solution-quality improvement. VERAS combines task-specific solution checkers with a separate verification agent to examine candidate solutions against the task requirements. It uses verification feedback to guide feasibility repair, additional constraint checking, and objective improvement, while candidate acceptance criteria screen revisions for deterioration in output validity or constraint satisfaction. On ORAgentBench, VERAS achieves a 42.99% pass rate, exceeding the reported 35.51% of Codex using the same LLM. Across two industrial-scale OR problems, VERAS reduces inter-datacenter peak bandwidth by 10.34% relative to native Codex and lowers annualized distribution network planning costs by 6.28% compared with expert-designed solutions. Code and evidence are available at https://github.com/holimario/VERAS.

papers.title: What Matters for NVFP4 Training? A Comparative Study of Low-Precision Pretraining Recipes
papers.abstract: Training large language models directly in 4-bit floating-point (FP) formats promises substantial improvements in throughput and energy efficiency. While some recipe design choices have been validated at scale, many promising approaches remain untested beyond small models and short token horizons, leaving open the question of which trends will hold. We present a systematic comparison of recent NVFP4 recipes at medium model scale, evaluating dense 8B and 30B-A3B MoE models trained for up to 1T tokens, with a focus on which ingredients are necessary for accuracy recovery. We propose a final recipe grounded in the principles behind established stable NVFP4 training at scale, incorporating state-of-the-art techniques such as unbiased gradient estimation with lower quantization error than stochastic rounding. To the best of our knowledge, this is the strongest FP4 training result demonstrated at this scale to date in loss gap to BF16. Through ablation studies, we find that: (i) each technique in the optimized recipe measurably improves loss trajectory, (ii) selective high-precision layers are necessary for recovering accuracy at scale, (iii) not all tensors in the backward pass benefit equally from de-biasing, leaving room to apply complementary error-reduction techniques to the remaining tensors.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: NVIDIA が中規模で詰めた NVFP4 (4 bit) 事前学習の処方箋比較
papers.summary: 4 bit 浮動小数点 (FP4) で大規模言語モデルを直接学習すると処理速度と電力効率が大きく上がるが、どの工夫が本当に精度の回復に必要かは中規模でまだ確かめられていなかった。NVIDIA は 8B の密なモデルと 30B-A3B の MoE モデルを最大 1T トークンまで学習して NVFP4 の手法を比較し、確率的丸め (stochastic rounding) より量子化誤差の小さい偏りのない勾配推定を含む最終レシピを提案、この規模で BF16 との損失差が過去最強の結果になったとしている。アブレーションでは、選んだレイヤーだけ高精度にすることが精度回復に必要であり、逆伝播のテンソル全部が偏り除去から同じだけ得をするわけではないことも分かった。
papers.why: カーネル・低精度を扱う人にとって、FP4 学習を中規模で実際に成立させる具体的な処方箋とその効き目の内訳が分かる点が新しい。
papers.summary_en: The authors present a systematic comparison of recent NVFP4 recipes at medium model scale (dense 8B and 30B-A3B MoE, up to 1T tokens), proposing a final recipe with unbiased gradient estimation with lower quantization error than stochastic rounding, which they describe as the strongest FP4 training result demonstrated at this scale to date in loss gap to BF16. Ablations show each technique measurably improves loss trajectory, selective high-precision layers are necessary for recovering accuracy at scale, and not all backward-pass tensors benefit equally from de-biasing.
papers.why_en: Gives a concrete, ablated recipe for making FP4 pretraining work at medium scale rather than only small-model demonstrations.

papers.title: FlashRT-PAI: Fast Kernels Are Not Fast Pipelines for Physical AI Inference
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA), video-action (VA), and world action models (WAMs) form the backbone of modern physical AI systems, yet their real-time single-batch inference remains a defining bottleneck. Latency is dominated not by individual kernel computation, but by system-level overhead: thousands of short kernel launches, intermediate data movement across operator boundaries, and redundant recomputation across consecutive decisions. General-purpose graph compilers cannot address these costs, as they optimize individual calls in isolation and lack visibility into cross-call state semantics and global pipeline structure. We present FLASHRT-PAI, a low-latency inference engine built around model-hardware pipeline co-design rather than isolated kernel optimization. FLASHRT-PAI combines three core mechanisms: deep kernel fusion with launch overlap eliminates inter-operator boundaries and launch gaps; an execution contract formalizes the pipeline's stage DAG, update rates, and named buffers to enable cross-decision state reuse and selective refresh; and execution-state capsules enable fast snapshot, restore, and fork of persistent pipeline state. The system also supports drop-in acceleration of unmodified PyTorch models via parity- and latency-gated kernel replacement. Evaluation covers six policies on RTX 5090 and four on Jetson AGX Thor. At matched 16-bit precision, FLASHRT-PAI is 1.3-3.7x faster than official compiled paths. Combining pipeline co-design with reduced precision delivers 3.38-12.66x speedup over official eager implementations. In LIBERO-10, four-bit pi0.5 achieves 94.04% success on Thor and 93.32% on RTX 5090, compared with 92.4% for the measured official FP16 reference. FLASHRT-PAI is open source, distributed via Hugging Face Kernel Hub, and its opt-in pi0.5 kernels have been adopted into the LeRobot framework.
papers.ja_title: FlashRT-PAI: カーネルの速さではなくパイプライン全体の設計で物理 AI 推論を速くする
papers.summary: VLA (vision-language-action) などの物理 AI モデルは、個々の計算カーネルの速さより、何千回も短いカーネルを呼び出すことや演算の間でデータを移動させる無駄といった「システム全体の重さ」が推論を遅くする困りごとを抱えていた。NVIDIA と Hugging Face は、カーネルを深く融合して起動の重なりを無くし、パイプライン全体の構造を契約として明文化し、状態を素早く保存・復元できる推論エンジン FlashRT-PAI を作った。RTX 5090 と Jetson AGX Thor で、16 bit 精度のまま公式のコンパイル済み経路より 1.3-3.7 倍速く、低精度化も組み合わせると公式の eager 実装より 3.38-12.66 倍速くなり、LIBERO-10 というタスクでは 4 bit 版 pi0.5 が公式 FP16 の 92.4% に対し Thor で 94.04%、RTX 5090 で 93.32% の成功率を達成したとしている。
papers.why: 推論・サービングを作る人にとって、カーネル単体の最適化ではなく呼び出し順序全体を契約として設計するという発想と、実機での速度・精度の実測値が参考になる。
papers.summary_en: FLASHRT-PAI is a low-latency inference engine built around model-hardware pipeline co-design rather than isolated kernel optimization, combining deep kernel fusion with launch overlap, an execution contract formalizing the pipeline's stage DAG, and execution-state capsules for fast snapshot/restore. At matched 16-bit precision it is 1.3-3.7x faster than official compiled paths on RTX 5090 and Jetson AGX Thor; combining pipeline co-design with reduced precision delivers 3.38-12.66x speedup over official eager implementations, and on LIBERO-10 four-bit pi0.5 achieves 94.04% success on Thor and 93.32% on RTX 5090, compared with 92.4% for the measured official FP16 reference.
papers.why_en: Shows that fixing cross-call launch and state-reuse overhead, not just kernel speed, is what unlocks real-time physical-AI inference.

papers.title: Koi: Evidence-Guided, Self-Calibrating Planning for Multi-Cloud, Heterogeneous LLM Inference Fleets
papers.abstract: Deploying a large language model (LLM) requires choosing the right accelerator, parallelization strategy, engine configuration, and replica count amongst ~140 other variables across clouds, regions, and markets. These decisions are intertwined, and the best cluster-wide plan continually changes as jobs contend for shared capacity on shifting workloads. We present Koi, a self-calibrating cluster planner for heterogeneous, multi-cloud fleets. Koi uses a Recursive Language Model (RLM) hierarchy to propose hypotheses and reason over deployment while deterministic components predict serving behavior, score candidates, and control placement. It represents inference behavior as a fixed causal graph linking decisions (e.g., accelerator, parallelism), runtime mediators (e.g., KV-cache pressure, communication overhead), and outcomes (e.g., latency, throughput). Each deployment strengthens or weakens scoped causal relationships, building a comprehensive playbook for inference that the planner employs to guide future decisions. Job-wise configurations are composed into cluster-wide plans and evaluated against serving objectives, resource constraints, SLO risks, and cost. Across benchmarks, Koi achieves 1.18x greater goodput than the strongest baseline while reducing $/token by 20% in a real heterogeneous cluster. Ablations isolate the contribution of Koi's architecture: a pure language model attains a composite score of 35.3, the same model equipped with Koi's deterministic tools reaches 51.6, and the full Koi planner reaches 70.8.
papers.ja_title: Koi: 因果グラフを自己学習させて多クラウド・異種 LLM 推論クラスタを計画する
papers.summary: LLM を複数のクラウドや地域にまたがる異種のクラスタで動かすには、アクセラレータの種類や並列化の方法など 140 個近い変数を組み合わせて決める必要があり、しかも最適な配置は負荷の変化で常に変わるという困りごとがある。NVIDIA・UC Berkeley・UIUC・ByteDance は、再帰的言語モデル (Recursive Language Model) で仮説を立てながら決定的な部品が推論性能を予測・採点・配置する自己校正型のクラスタ計画ツール Koi を作った。実際の異種クラスタでの実験で、最良のベースラインより goodput (良いスループット) が 1.18 倍、トークンあたりコストが 20% 下がり、言語モデル単体の複合スコアは 35.3 だったが決定的な道具を組み合わせると 51.6、Koi 全体では 70.8 まで上がったとしている。
papers.why: 推論・サービングの基盤を作る人にとって、配置判断を因果関係のグラフとして明文化し自己学習させる設計が、多クラウド運用にそのまま使える。
papers.summary_en: Koi is a self-calibrating cluster planner for heterogeneous, multi-cloud LLM fleets that uses a Recursive Language Model hierarchy to propose hypotheses while deterministic components predict serving behavior, score candidates, and control placement over a causal graph of decisions, mediators, and outcomes. Across benchmarks Koi achieves 1.18x greater goodput than the strongest baseline while reducing $/token by 20% in a real heterogeneous cluster; ablations show a pure language model attains a composite score of 35.3, the same model with Koi's deterministic tools reaches 51.6, and the full Koi planner reaches 70.8.
papers.why_en: Demonstrates that pairing an LLM planner with deterministic causal scoring, rather than either alone, is what drives the gains in multi-cloud fleet planning.

papers.title: FlashMap: Flow Map Speculative Decoding
papers.abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates large language model (LLM) inference by using a lightweight drafter to propose a block of tokens that the target model verifies in one parallel pass. Autoregressive drafters generate this block one token at a time, whereas block diffusion drafters such as DFlash generate it in one pass, making drafting faster. However, these diffusion drafters predict each token independently, ignoring dependencies between tokens in the block. We introduce FlashMap, a continuous flow drafter that conditions a flow map language model on the target model's hidden states and generates the whole block in one forward pass while capturing inter-token dependencies. On Qwen3-8B, FlashMap is faster than a matched DFlash baseline on every benchmark, with 7% higher average speedup and up to 6.1x lossless acceleration.
papers.ja_title: FlashMap: トークン間の依存関係も捉える投機的デコーディングの下書きモデル
papers.summary: LLM の推論を速くする投機的デコーディング (speculative decoding) では、軽量な下書きモデル (drafter) がブロック単位でトークンを提案するが、DFlash のような拡散 (diffusion) 型の下書きモデルはブロック内のトークンを独立に予測してしまい、トークン同士の依存関係を無視するという困りごとがあった。Princeton は、対象モデルの隠れ状態 (hidden state) を条件にしてブロック全体を 1 回の順伝播で生成しつつトークン間の依存関係も捉える連続フローの下書きモデル FlashMap を提案した。Qwen3-8B での実験では、同条件の DFlash より全てのベンチマークで速く、平均の高速化率が 7% 高く、最大で無損失 6.1 倍の高速化を達成したとしている。
papers.why: 推論・サービングを作る人にとって、拡散型の下書きモデルが抱えていたトークン間依存の弱点を連続フロー (flow map) で埋めるという具体的な改善策が参考になる。
papers.summary_en: FlashMap is a continuous flow drafter that conditions a flow map language model on the target model's hidden states and generates the whole block in one forward pass while capturing inter-token dependencies, addressing the independence assumption of block diffusion drafters like DFlash. On Qwen3-8B, FlashMap is faster than a matched DFlash baseline on every benchmark, with 7% higher average speedup and up to 6.1x lossless acceleration.
papers.why_en: Targets the specific weakness of diffusion drafters (independent per-token prediction) with a flow-map formulation that still drafts in a single forward pass.

papers.title: Generative Retrieval for Reverse Target Fishing with a Proteome-Scale Benchmark
papers.abstract: Reverse target fishing identifies protein targets for a query molecule and is central to drug discovery and repurposing. Discriminative approaches adapted from virtual screening face sparse, long-tailed associations and missing-not-at-random measurements: treating unrecorded pairs as negatives can suppress genuine targets. We reformulate the task as generative retrieval and introduce GenFish. Residual vector quantization converts frozen protein language model features into shared semantic identifiers. Given a molecular fingerprint, GenFish autoregressively models codes conditioned on the query and preceding code, ranking proteins by identifier likelihood without explicitly labeling unrecorded pairs as negatives. We introduce ProTargetBench, the first proteome-scale benchmark for reverse target fishing to jointly support measured-panel discrimination and full-catalogue recovery of experimentally recorded positives. Covering 20,431 UniProt-reviewed human proteins, it integrates curated bioactivity evidence and distinguishes experimental inactivity from unmeasured associations. On 198 held-out molecules, GenFish achieves higher mean performance across all three full-catalogue retrieval metrics than four discriminative neural baselines and three non-neural baselines, including ligand-based methods. A controlled positive-hiding experiment shows that targeted removal of false-negative competition improves contrastive retrieval beyond matched random masking; GenFish remains stronger under the same incomplete supervision. Pfam alignment indicates that the semantic identifiers capture biologically meaningful relationships among proteins. These results establish generative retrieval as a principled paradigm for reverse target fishing under incomplete bioactivity records.

papers.title: Uncovering Semantic Hierarchies in Text-Attributed Graphs via Variational EM-based LLM-GNN Synergy
papers.abstract: While hierarchical structures are intrinsic to organizing human knowledge, current representation learning on text-attributed graphs predominantly operates on flat semantic spaces, overlooking the rich coarse-to-fine granularity inherent in real-world data. To bridge this gap, we propose SHiFT, which synergizes the reasoning power of LLMs with the structural representation capability of GNNs within an Expectation-Maximization (EM) paradigm. In the E-step, we harness LLMs as expert taxonomists to induce an explicit semantic tree, introducing a lightweight Mapping & Diagnosis strategy that reduces inference costs by surgically updating the hierarchy only when anomalies are detected. In the M-step, we align the GNN encoder with this induced hierarchy from complementary perspectives, including clustering partition, topological skeleton, and semantic concepts. Theoretical analysis interprets SHiFT as a generalized Variational EM algorithm. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SHiFT not only achieves state-of-the-art performance but also uncovers high-quality, human-readable taxonomies. Our code can be found at https://github.com/Cloudy1225/SHiFT.

papers.title: Muse Glimmer 30B: An On-Device Agentic Model
papers.abstract: We introduce Muse Glimmer, an open-source 30B parameter causal language model with perception encoder, purpose-built for autonomous agentic tasks on consumer hardware. Muse Glimmer integrates multi-step reasoning, reliable tool use and failure recovery into a single model that runs locally on consumer devices without requiring cloud infrastructure. The model accepts text and image inputs and produces text outputs, was trained on data from over a hundred languages, and is quantized to approximately 4-bit precision for efficient single-GPU inference. Muse Glimmer achieves state-of-the-art performance for its size class on agentic benchmarks, setting a new standard compared to the models of its size: Gemma4-31B and Qwen3.6-27B on tool use, multi-step planning, and agentic task completion. We release the model under the Apache 2.0 license to foster open-source development of capable, safe, local AI agents.

papers.title: PV-Decoding: Progressive Verification Decoding with Decode Gating for Diffusion Language Models
papers.abstract: Discrete diffusion language models (dLLMs) offer an attractive alternative to autoregressive generation by updating multiple tokens in parallel, but their inference efficiency is still limited by the cost of safely committing tentative predictions. In particular, speculative decoding for dLLMs is challenging because speculative tokens within the same diffusion block may depend on one another, making aggressive acceptance prone to error propagation and strict verification computationally expensive. We present PV-Decoding, a confidence-driven speculative decoding framework with progressive verification for block diffusion inference. PV-Decoding partitions masked positions into directly decoded tokens, speculative tokens, and unresolved tokens using two confidence thresholds, and then verifies speculative tokens with progressively stronger policies, including single-batch, dual-batch, and multi-batch verification. This design exposes a practical accuracy--efficiency trade-off: weaker verification minimizes overhead, whereas stronger verification improves acceptance precision and robustness. Experiments on three diffusion language models across GSM8K, MBPP, and HumanEval show that PV-Decoding reduces sequential model forward passes (MFPs) by 8%--37% relative to confidence-based decoding, while keeping the largest observed accuracy drop to 1.3%. On Dream-7B-Instruct/GSM8K, PV-Decoding (1-batch) and PV-Decoding (2-batch) improve throughput by 7.0%--13.6% under the same hardware budget, whereas PV-Decoding (multi-batch) is slower under the current runtime. These results suggest that confidence-guided speculation with structured verification is a practical path toward efficient and reliable dLLM inference.
papers.ja_title: 拡散言語モデル向け投機的デコード PV-Decoding
papers.summary: 拡散言語モデル (dLLM、一度に複数トークンを更新する生成方式) は投機的デコード (draft トークンを先に予測して後でまとめて検証する高速化手法) が難しく、同じブロック内のトークン同士が依存し合うため、雑に受理すると誤りが広がり、厳密な検証は計算が重くなる。PV-Decoding は 2 つの信頼度しきい値でマスク位置を「直接確定」「投機」「未確定」に分け、投機トークンを単一バッチ・2 バッチ・多バッチの順に強くなる検証で確かめる。GSM8K・MBPP・HumanEval で 3 つの拡散言語モデルに試したところ、通常の信頼度ベースの手法に比べ逐次のモデル実行回数を 8〜37% 減らしつつ精度の低下は最大 1.3% に収まり、Dream-7B-Instruct と GSM8K では 1 バッチ・2 バッチ版でスループットが 7.0〜13.6% 向上した (多バッチ版は現状のランタイムでは遅い)。
papers.why: 拡散言語モデルの投機的デコードを実用化する具体的なしきい値設計と検証ポリシーの選び方を示し、サービング基盤を作る人がそのまま参考にできる。
papers.summary_en: Speculative decoding for diffusion language models (dLLMs) is hard because speculative tokens within the same diffusion block can depend on each other, making aggressive acceptance risky and strict verification expensive. PV-Decoding splits masked positions into directly decoded, speculative, and unresolved tokens using two confidence thresholds, then verifies speculative tokens with progressively stronger single-batch, dual-batch, and multi-batch policies. Across three dLLMs on GSM8K, MBPP, and HumanEval, PV-Decoding reduces sequential model forward passes by 8-37% relative to confidence-based decoding while keeping the largest observed accuracy drop to 1.3%; on Dream-7B-Instruct/GSM8K, the 1-batch and 2-batch variants improve throughput by 7.0-13.6% under the same hardware budget, whereas the multi-batch variant is slower under the current runtime.
papers.why_en: Gives dLLM serving builders a concrete confidence-threshold and verification-policy design for speculative decoding, with a measured accuracy-efficiency trade-off across verification strengths.

papers.title: Toward Collective Model Intelligence: Characterizing and Coordinating Models
papers.abstract: Independently developed AI models accumulate diverse and complementary capabilities, but a growing model collection does not automatically realize Collective AI. Addressing this gap requires understanding model capabilities with limited evaluation, organizing complementary models to collaborate on diverse tasks, and executing model calls efficiently under resource constraints. We present a systematic approach to pursuing Collective Model Intelligence through three connected components. First, Model Eval constructs evidence-based capability profiles by combining query-level performance estimation with cross-domain prediction, reducing the need for exhaustive evaluation. Second, Mio (Models in One) organizes complementary model candidates and supports task-conditioned, cost-aware selection and collaboration as task requirements evolve. Third, Mos (Model Serving OS) separates model selection from execution and provides endpoint scheduling and shared model deployment and distribution. Experiments show lower capability-estimation errors under limited evaluation. Across nine public benchmarks, Mio 1.0 Lite achieves the highest average score and lowest average cost among compared methods, with per-request costs 73.7-97.5% lower than those of the best-scoring alternatives. A prewarmed shared cache accelerates model-file retrieval by up to 23.3 times. This work lays a foundation for Collective Model Intelligence by characterizing and coordinating the diverse capabilities of an expanding model universe.
papers.ja_title: 複数モデルを束ねて使う「集合モデル知能」の基盤 Mio/Mos
papers.summary: 別々に作られた AI モデルが集まっても、それだけでは能力を組み合わせた「集合知」にはならない。この研究は能力評価 (Model Eval、少ない評価で性能を見積もる)、モデル選択・協調 (Mio、タスクとコストに応じて複数モデルを組み合わせる)、実行基盤 (Mos、モデルの選択と実行を分離しエンドポイントの割り当てと共有配備をする) の 3 点を組み合わせる。9 つの公開ベンチマークで Mio 1.0 Lite は比較した手法の中で平均スコアが最も高く平均コストが最も低く、1 リクエストあたりのコストは最も成績の良い比較対象より 73.7〜97.5% 低かった。あらかじめ温めておいた共有キャッシュによってモデルファイルの取得が最大 23.3 倍速くなった。
papers.why: モデルの選択と実行を分離し共有キャッシュで配備を速くするサービング OS の具体的な設計で、複数モデルを運用する推論基盤の作り手にそのまま参考になる。
papers.summary_en: A growing collection of independently developed models does not automatically realize Collective AI; the paper addresses this with three connected components: Model Eval (query-level performance estimation plus cross-domain prediction to cut evaluation cost), Mio (task-conditioned, cost-aware model selection and collaboration), and Mos (a model-serving OS separating selection from execution, with endpoint scheduling and shared deployment). Across nine public benchmarks, Mio 1.0 Lite achieves the highest average score and lowest average cost among compared methods, with per-request costs 73.7-97.5% lower than those of the best-scoring alternatives, and a prewarmed shared cache accelerates model-file retrieval by up to 23.3 times.
papers.why_en: Lays out a concrete serving-OS design (selection separated from execution, shared caching) for coordinating many models, directly relevant to anyone building multi-model serving infrastructure.

papers.title: Pattern-Driven Evaluation of LLM Code Optimization: Isolating Compiler-Transcendent Semantic Reasoning
papers.abstract: Existing evaluations of LLM-based code optimization primarily measure end-to-end speedup, obscuring whether a model actually performs the intended optimization. For compiled languages, this is especially problematic: observed gains may reflect transformations already recoverable by modern optimizing compilers rather than optimization behavior attributable to the model itself. We present PatternBench, a benchmark for studying compiler-transcendent optimization, i.e., performance improvements that remain after aggressive compiler optimization. PatternBench targets residual optimization opportunities across seven classes of transformations and pairs runtime evaluation with an AST-based optimization faithfulness analysis that verifies whether the intended optimization is realized in the generated program. Experiments with frontier, open-weight, and fine-tuned models show that runtime speedup alone provides an incomplete account of optimization capability. Optimization faithfulness is strongly associated with realized speedup, and fine-tuning improves both faithfulness and optimization effectiveness. These results suggest that evaluation of LLM-based code optimization should measure not only performance outcomes, but also whether the target transformation was successfully executed.

papers.title: Query-Dependent Reading for Quantized Inner-Product Estimation: A Minimax Separation
papers.abstract: We study quantization for inner-product estimation when storage and reading have separate budgets. In the static bit-probe model [Yao, 1981], an encoder stores $w$ bits about $x$ before seeing a query $y$, and a reader probes at most $r<w$ bits to estimate $x^\top y$. Both vectors lie in the $d$-dimensional Euclidean unit ball. Protocols may be randomized, and computation is unrestricted. Performance is measured by $d$ times the worst-case mean-squared error over $x,y$, averaged over protocol randomness. First, we show that query-independent reading cannot benefit from extra storage. Any such reader is equivalent to fully reading an $r$-bit message, even when later reads depend on previously returned bits. At fixed positive rates $W=w/d$ and $R=r/d$, the normalized minimax error converges to $1/(4^R-1)$, independent of $W$. The upper bound was already known [Ordentlich and Polyanskiy, 2025]. We prove the matching lower bound for arbitrary scalar decoders, extending the result for unbiased compressors [Safaryan et al., 2020]. Then, we show that query-dependent reading makes extra storage useful. We construct a two-batch protocol using Gaussian projections and random thresholds, with asymptotic normalized error at most $(π+o(1))/[4R\log(W/R)]$ as $W/R\to\infty$. At fixed $R$, this error vanishes as storage grows, giving an unbounded advantage over query-independent reading. We also prove a finite-dimensional lower bound for arbitrary encoders, decoders, and fully branching readers. In the doubly sparse regime $W/R\to\infty$ and $R\log(W/R)\to0$, it gives normalized error at least $(1-o(1))/[2R\log(W/R)]$. Thus, our protocol is optimal within a factor of $π/2$ in the leading constant.
papers.ja_title: 内積推定のための量子化、保存と読み出しの予算が別々のときの限界
papers.summary: ベクトルを少ないビット数に圧縮 (量子化) して内積を推定するとき、「何ビット保存するか」と「後で何ビット読み出すか」の予算が別々にある場合の限界はよく分かっていなかった。静的ビットプローブモデルという枠組みで、まずクエリに依存しない読み出し方式は保存ビット数を増やしても誤差が改善せず、正規化した誤差が 1/(4^R−1) に収束すること (読み出しビット数 R だけで決まり保存ビット数 W には無関係) を、既知の上限と一致する下限として証明した。次に、クエリに依存するガウス射影とランダムしきい値を使う 2 バッチ方式を作り、保存ビット数を増やすほど誤差が消えていくことを示した。
papers.why: 低精度 (量子化) 表現でベクトルの内積を検索・推定するときの理論的な限界と、それに迫る具体的な読み出し方法を示し、埋め込み検索や近似最近傍探索の低精度設計の指針になる。
papers.summary_en: The paper studies quantization for inner-product estimation when storage and reading have separate bit budgets, using the static bit-probe model. It shows query-independent readers cannot benefit from extra storage beyond fully reading an r-bit message, with the normalized minimax error converging to 1/(4^R-1) independent of the storage rate W, proving the matching lower bound to a previously known upper bound. It then constructs a query-dependent two-batch protocol using Gaussian projections and random thresholds whose error vanishes as storage grows, and proves this protocol is optimal within a factor of pi/2 against a finite-dimensional lower bound.
papers.why_en: Establishes the theoretical limits and a near-optimal protocol for low-precision (quantized) inner-product estimation under separate storage/read budgets, relevant to designing low-precision embedding and retrieval systems.

papers.title: Arctic-SWE: Revisiting the Long Horizon Agent Training by Modeling-System Co-Design
papers.abstract: Long-horizon agent training, including software engineering, is advancing rapidly, but the recipe and infrastructure needed for a strong reinforcement-learning baseline remain difficult to reproduce. This makes gains from new algorithms or data hard to distinguish from improvements to an under-tuned baseline. We present Arctic-SWE, a fully asynchronous RL framework that establishes such a baseline through model-system co-design, using overfitting on a small task pool as the testbed. This testbed exposes failures that early reward gains conceal and guides the integration of established components: gated reward, importance-weight control, aligned training and inference engines, and consistent state across policy updates. No single component is new, yet together they form the missing foundation. On raw R2E-Gym data, without new algorithms or data work, Arctic-SWE trains Qwen3.5-4B to 62.0% pass@1 on SWE-bench Verified. This is comparable to concurrent FrogNano (61.5%), which relies on online task synthesis, after about one-sixth as many training rollouts. Building on this foundation, we further filter and refine R2E-Gym, SWE-rebench V2, and Scale-SWE. With this curated subset, the 4B model improves from 47.4%/25.0%/37.9% to 65.0%/38.3%/59.7% on SWE-bench Verified/Pro-v1/Pro-v2, and the recipe also improves Qwen3.5-9B from 56.2%/31.9%/48.8% to 65.7%/39.6%/70.2% on Verified/Pro-v1/Pro-v2. Controlled comparisons show that both curation and test strengthening improve held-out performance, although stronger tests reduce apparent training-task mastery. Arctic-SWE provides a documented starting point for studying better algorithms, data and environments for asynchronous agent RL.
papers.ja_title: 長期タスクのエージェント RL 基盤 Arctic-SWE
papers.summary: ソフトウェア工事のような長期タスクのエージェント強化学習は、強いベースラインを再現する手順や基盤が整っておらず、新しい手法の効果なのか単に調整不足のベースラインの改善なのかを見分けにくい。Arctic-SWE は完全に非同期な RL 基盤で、小さなタスク集合に意図的に過学習させる実験を土台にして、見かけの報酬の伸びが隠してしまう失敗を洗い出し、報酬の形 (gated reward)・重要度重みの制御・学習と推論エンジンの整合・ポリシー更新をまたいだ状態の一貫性、という既存の要素をまとめ上げる。R2E-Gym の元データだけで Qwen3.5-4B を SWE-bench Verified の pass@1 62.0% まで学習でき、同時期のオンラインタスク合成を使う FrogNano (61.5%) と同等の結果を約 6 分の 1 の学習ロールアウト数で得た。データを精選すると 4B モデルは Verified/Pro-v1/Pro-v2 で 47.4/25.0/37.9% から 65.0/38.3/59.7% に、9B モデルは 56.2/31.9/48.8% から 65.7/39.6/70.2% に向上した。
papers.why: 長期エージェント RL の「ちゃんと動く」ベースラインのレシピと、小さなタスク集合への過学習で隠れた失敗を見つけるテストベッドの作り方を文書化し、RL 後学習基盤を作る人の比較対象・診断手法になる。
papers.summary_en: Reproducing a strong RL baseline for long-horizon agent training (e.g., software engineering) is difficult, making it hard to tell whether gains come from new algorithms/data or from an under-tuned baseline. Arctic-SWE is a fully asynchronous RL framework built via model-system co-design, using overfitting on a small task pool as a testbed that exposes failures early reward gains conceal, and integrating gated reward, importance-weight control, aligned training/inference engines, and consistent state across policy updates. On raw R2E-Gym data alone it trains Qwen3.5-4B to 62.0% pass@1 on SWE-bench Verified, comparable to concurrent FrogNano (61.5%, which relies on online task synthesis) using about one-sixth as many training rollouts; with curated data, the 4B model improves from 47.4/25.0/37.9% to 65.0/38.3/59.7% (Verified/Pro-v1/Pro-v2), and the 9B model from 56.2/31.9/48.8% to 65.7/39.6/70.2%.
papers.why_en: Documents a reproducible, well-tuned asynchronous RL baseline recipe for long-horizon agent training, giving RL post-training infrastructure builders a concrete reference point and a small-task-pool overfitting testbed for catching hidden baseline failures.

review.note: 新しい RL 手法の効果を主張する前に、小さなタスク集合に意図的に過学習させる実験で「見かけの報酬の伸びが隠す失敗」を洗い出すという、ベースライン検証の観点。
review.note_en: Before claiming a new RL method's gains, deliberately overfit on a small task pool to expose failures that early reward gains conceal — a baseline-validation lens.

papers.title: Certified Sparse Attention via Perturbed Retrieval
papers.abstract: Sparse attention speeds up long-context decoding by reading few keys of the KV cache, but existing methods do not control the error of a query, and on real KV caches their errors have heavy tails. We show that perturbing the score of every key with an independent Exp(1) variable turns threshold retrieval into sampling keys with probability proportional to their attention weights. Lowering the threshold along a geometric grid gives nested samples, a Horvitz--Thompson estimate of the output at every level, and confidence bounds that hold simultaneously over all levels, so each head stops at the first level whose certificate meets the target error $\varepsilon$. With fresh perturbations at every decoding step, each certificate fails with probability at most $δ$ during generation. At a suitable threshold, the estimator reads $O(\varepsilon^{-2}\log(1/δ))$ values regardless of the context length, and no adaptive method reads fewer, up to constants. A 4-bit scan with deterministic bounds, shared across a grouped-query-attention group, generates the candidates exactly but reads every key. On three LLMs and ten settings at 16K--128K tokens, no certificate is violated, and at equal keys read our 90th-percentile error is 4.6--7.9$\times$ lower than that of the best of 15 baseline families. At equal bytes, the best baselines have 0.6--1.6 times our 90th-percentile error and at least 4.9 times our largest. End to end, our method stays within one point of dense attention on tasks and within 0.1\% in PG-19 perplexity, and the strongest baselines at equal bytes score as well. On CPU, decoding steps at 32K--128K tokens run 1.1--1.4$\times$ faster than dense attention on the same 16-bit cache.
papers.ja_title: 誤差を保証付きで抑えるスパースアテンション
papers.summary: スパースアテンション (長い文脈のデコードを速くするため KV キャッシュの一部のキーだけ読む手法) は 1 回ごとのクエリの誤差を制御できず、実際のキャッシュでは大きく外れる場合がある。各キーのスコアに独立なノイズを加えると、しきい値での取得が「アテンションの重みに比例した確率でキーを抜き出す」ことと同じになる。しきい値を段々下げていくことで入れ子になったサンプルが得られ、各段階で推定値と、全段階で同時に成り立つ信頼区間 (証明書) を作り、各ヘッドは目標の誤差 ε を満たした最初の段階で止める。16K〜128K トークンの 3 つの LLM・10 設定で証明書が破られたことは一度もなく、読み出すキー数を揃えたときの 90 パーセンタイル誤差は 15 種のベースライン手法群の最良のものより 4.6〜7.9 倍低く、密なアテンションに対しタスク精度は 1 点以内、PG-19 のパープレキシティは 0.1% 以内に収まり、CPU では 32K〜128K トークンのデコードが密なアテンションより 1.1〜1.4 倍速かった。
papers.why: スパースアテンションに統計的な誤差保証を付ける具体的な方法で、KV キャッシュを圧縮しつつ精度を保証したい推論サービング基盤の設計にそのまま使える。
papers.summary_en: Sparse attention speeds up long-context decoding by reading few KV-cache keys, but existing methods do not control per-query error and show heavy-tailed errors on real caches. Perturbing every key's score with an independent Exp(1) variable turns threshold retrieval into sampling keys with probability proportional to attention weight; lowering the threshold along a geometric grid gives nested samples, a Horvitz-Thompson estimate at every level, and confidence bounds that hold simultaneously over all levels, so each head stops at the first level whose certificate meets a target error epsilon. Across three LLMs and ten settings at 16K-128K tokens, no certificate is violated, and at equal keys read the 90th-percentile error is 4.6-7.9x lower than the best of 15 baseline families; end to end the method stays within one point of dense attention on tasks and within 0.1% in PG-19 perplexity, with CPU decoding at 32K-128K tokens 1.1-1.4x faster than dense attention.
papers.why_en: Gives sparse-attention/KV-cache compression a statistically certified per-query error guarantee with simultaneous validity across stopping levels, directly usable by anyone designing guaranteed-accuracy long-context serving.

papers.title: When Does Better Acceptance Pay? A Controlled Study of Speculative Decoding
papers.abstract: The throughput gains of speculative decoding depend on the trade-off between acceptance length and execution latency. We ask when additional acceptance is worth the cost of obtaining it. We establish a comparison protocol spanning training, inference, and evaluation, remeasuring released checkpoints and retraining six drafter recipes on shared target-generated data across ten benchmarks and two target models. Alignment changes the picture: gaps that appear large in published comparisons shrink substantially under shared training and inference conditions. This narrowing motivates two deeper questions: how is acceptance improved at different costs, and when do these gains improve throughput? We find that acceptance can be improved through nearly free objective and context changes or more expensive token-to-token conditioning, which pays off most clearly under sampled drafting. DCore illustrates the former route as a strong baseline with little additional measured drafting overhead. The payoff is conditional: task uncertainty and serving conditions affect acceptance returns, execution costs, and the preferred drafter and budget. These findings inform future drafter design and deployment choices.
papers.ja_title: 投機的デコードの受理率改善はいつ得になるか
papers.summary: 投機的デコード (ドラフトモデルが提案したトークンをターゲットモデルが検証する高速化手法) のスループットは、提案がどれだけ受理されるかと検証にかかる時間のトレードオフで決まるが、どんな条件で受理率の改善が得になるのかは分かっていなかった。訓練・推論・評価の条件を揃えた比較手順を作り、公開済みのチェックポイントを測り直し、6 種のドラフタを同じターゲットモデル生成データで再学習して 10 のベンチマーク・2 つのターゲットモデルで比較した。条件を揃えると、公開されている比較で大きく見えていた差は大幅に縮まった。受理率はほぼ無料の目的関数・文脈の変更で改善できる場合と、より高コストなトークン間の条件付けが必要な場合があり、後者はサンプリングドラフト時に最も報われる。DCore は追加の計測可能なドラフト負荷をほとんど増やさずに強いベースラインになった。
papers.why: 条件を揃えて測り直すと公開比較の差が縮むという測定上の教訓と、受理率改善のコストと見返りの条件を示し、投機的デコードの高速化手法を比較・採用する人の判断材料になる。
papers.summary_en: The throughput gains of speculative decoding depend on the trade-off between acceptance length and execution latency, and published comparisons of drafters are often measured under inconsistent training, inference, and evaluation conditions. Establishing a shared comparison protocol, remeasuring released checkpoints, and retraining six drafter recipes on shared target-generated data across ten benchmarks and two target models, the authors find that aligning conditions substantially shrinks gaps that appear large in published comparisons. Acceptance can be improved through nearly free objective and context changes or more expensive token-to-token conditioning, which pays off most clearly under sampled drafting; DCore illustrates the former route as a strong baseline with little additional measured drafting overhead, and the payoff is conditional on task uncertainty and serving conditions.
papers.why_en: Shows that published speculative-decoding gains shrink once training, inference, and evaluation conditions are aligned, a measurement-methodology lesson for anyone benchmarking decoding speedups.

review.note: 公開されている速度向上の比較は訓練・推論・評価の条件を揃えないと過大評価されるという、測り方そのものを揃える観点。
review.note_en: Published speedup comparisons overstate gains unless training, inference, and evaluation conditions are explicitly aligned first — a measurement-protocol lens.

papers.title: ReTrace: Visual Backtracking for Efficient Multimodal Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) encode images into dense visual token sequences, creating substantial attention and KV-cache overhead. Existing visual token compression methods reduce this cost by pruning low-saliency tokens in shallow layers, but this practice couples temporary computational deactivation with irreversible information deletion. We show that this coupling breaks an intrinsic inference pattern in MLLMs. Through layer-wise attention analysis, we identify \textbf{Visual Backtracking}: visual pivots remain spatially stable, yet in middle layers they actively retrieve context from tokens that appeared unimportant earlier. Thus, early low-saliency tokens can be inactive for computation while still being useful for later reasoning. Motivated by this finding, we propose \textbf{ReTrace}, a backtracking-aware compression framework that introduces a dormant token state. ReTrace caches non-pivot tokens outside expensive layer-wise computation, restores them during the backtracking window, and prunes only after their information has been absorbed. Experiments on Qwen2.5-VL and InternVL3 demonstrate nearly 90\% reductions in FLOPs and KV cache, a 2.83$\times$ prefilling speedup, and strong performance retention across complex vision-language benchmarks.
papers.ja_title: 視覚トークンを消す前に休ませる MLLM 圧縮 ReTrace
papers.summary: マルチモーダル大規模言語モデル (MLLM) は画像を密な視覚トークン列に変換するためアテンションと KV キャッシュの負荷が大きい。既存の視覚トークン圧縮は浅い層で重要度の低いトークンを刈り込むが、これは「一時的に計算を止める」ことと「情報を完全に消す」ことを一緒にしてしまう。層ごとのアテンション分析から、視覚的な要となるトークンは空間的には安定しているが中間層で以前は重要に見えなかったトークンから文脈を取り戻す「Visual Backtracking」現象を見つけ、休眠トークン状態を導入する ReTrace を提案した。要でないトークンを高コストな層計算の外にキャッシュし、バックトラッキングの窓の間だけ復元し、情報が吸収された後に初めて刈り込む。Qwen2.5-VL と InternVL3 で FLOPs と KV キャッシュをほぼ 90% 削減し、プリフィルを 2.83 倍高速化しつつ、複雑な視覚言語ベンチマークでの性能を強く維持した。
papers.why: 視覚トークンを「消す」前に「休ませる」という KV キャッシュ圧縮の新しい段階を示し、マルチモーダル推論サービングのキャッシュ設計にそのまま使える。
papers.summary_en: Multimodal LLMs (MLLMs) encode images into dense visual token sequences, creating substantial attention and KV-cache overhead; existing visual token compression prunes low-saliency tokens in shallow layers, coupling temporary computational deactivation with irreversible information deletion. Layer-wise attention analysis identifies Visual Backtracking: visual pivots remain spatially stable, yet in middle layers they actively retrieve context from tokens that appeared unimportant earlier. ReTrace, a backtracking-aware compression framework with a dormant token state, caches non-pivot tokens outside expensive layer-wise computation, restores them during the backtracking window, and prunes only after their information has been absorbed. On Qwen2.5-VL and InternVL3 it achieves nearly 90% reductions in FLOPs and KV cache, a 2.83x prefilling speedup, and strong performance retention across complex vision-language benchmarks.
papers.why_en: Introduces a new compression stage for visual tokens — dormant before deleted — directly usable for KV-cache design in multimodal serving.

papers.title: Conjugate Compilation: Self-Improving Agentic Co-Compilation for Speculative Decoding
papers.abstract: As LLM adoption surges, scaling model serving requires unlocking stranded GPU capacity alongside deploying more GPUs. Speculative decoding brings two models into the serving process: a small draft model proposes tokens that a larger target model verifies. Yet compiling these models individually leaves their shared execution outside the compiler's optimization boundary. We introduce CONJUGATE COMPILATION, which reframes speculative decoding as a cross-model compilation problem and jointly optimizes the draft and target models within their shared execution rather than treating each in isolation. Our key insight is that cross-model compilation should be informed by the measured performance of the co-located shared execution it produces: an optimization that improves a kernel in isolation need not improve the models when they execute together. To expand cross-model opportunities, we devise operand layouts that interleave blocks from both models within common tiles, co-locating GEMM and non-GEMM work while preserving their mathematics. We realize CONJUGATE COMPILATION through a self-improving agentic search system in which an LLM edits cross-model optimization plans using the compiler and GPU execution as its environment. Each proposed plan is compiled and evaluated through its co-located shared execution, whose measured score, together with kernel-level verdicts and compiler feedback, informs subsequent proposals, while Monte Carlo tree search accumulates rewards to guide exploration. Across six single-GPU speculative-decoding configurations on NVIDIA B300 and RTX 5090 GPUs, CONJUGATE COMPILATION achieves a geometric-mean per-round speedup of 1.37x over conventional execution. Interleaved kernels raise this speedup to 1.45x, reaching 1.59x in the best case. CONJUGATE COMPILATION also improves GPU utilization on average by 1.46x on RTX 5090 and 1.50x on B300.
papers.ja_title: ドラフトとターゲットを一緒にコンパイルする Conjugate Compilation
papers.summary: 投機的デコードはドラフトモデルとターゲットモデルの 2 つを使うが、それぞれを別々にコンパイルすると共有実行がコンパイラの最適化範囲の外に置かれ、使われていない GPU 容量を引き出しにくい。Conjugate Compilation は投機的デコードをモデル横断のコンパイル問題として再構成し、両モデルを共有実行の中で一緒に最適化する。両モデルのブロックを同じタイルに織り込む演算配置を考案して GEMM と非 GEMM の作業を共存させつつ数学的な正しさを保ち、LLM がコンパイラと GPU 実行を環境として最適化案を編集する自己改善型のエージェント探索(モンテカルロ木探索で誘導)で実現した。NVIDIA B300 と RTX 5090 上の 6 つの単一 GPU 投機的デコード構成で、従来実行に対し幾何平均で 1 ラウンドあたり 1.37 倍の高速化、ブロックを織り込んだカーネルでは 1.45 倍(最良で 1.59 倍)に達し、GPU 利用率は RTX 5090 で平均 1.46 倍、B300 で 1.50 倍向上した。
papers.why: 投機的デコードの 2 モデルを別々にではなく 1 つの共有実行として最適化するという発想を LLM 駆動のカーネル探索で実現し、サービング基盤のコンパイラ・カーネル設計に新しい軸を与える。
papers.summary_en: Speculative decoding brings a draft and a target model into the serving process, but compiling them individually leaves their shared execution outside the compiler's optimization boundary, hindering use of stranded GPU capacity. Conjugate Compilation reframes speculative decoding as a cross-model compilation problem, jointly optimizing the draft and target within their shared execution, using operand layouts that interleave blocks from both models within common tiles to co-locate GEMM and non-GEMM work while preserving correctness, realized through a self-improving agentic search in which an LLM edits cross-model optimization plans guided by Monte Carlo tree search. Across six single-GPU speculative-decoding configurations on NVIDIA B300 and RTX 5090 GPUs, it achieves a geometric-mean per-round speedup of 1.37x over conventional execution, rising to 1.45x with interleaved kernels (1.59x best case), and improves GPU utilization by 1.46x on RTX 5090 and 1.50x on B300.
papers.why_en: Realizes cross-model (draft+target) joint compilation for speculative decoding via LLM-driven kernel search, opening a new axis for serving-stack compiler and kernel design.

papers.title: Beyond the Teacher: Understanding and Preserving Distillation Overshoot in Agentic On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains agents on their own trajectories using supervision from a stronger teacher. We uncover a counterintuitive phenomenon in multi-turn agentic tasks: a smaller, initially weaker student can substantially outperform its teacher during training, only to regress as distillation continues. We term this phenomenon distillation overshoot. Through decision- and task-level analyses, we trace overshoot to two competing effects of OPD: repairing weak student decisions and eroding successful student choices that the teacher disfavors. Early in training, repair outpaces erosion, allowing the student to combine the teacher's corrections with its own strengths and surpass the teacher. As training continues, erosion overtakes repair, causing these gains to vanish. Motivated by this finding, we propose Success-Preserving On-Policy Distillation (SPOD), which selectively masks conflicting teacher supervision on successful student choices and introduces a soft probability floor to counteract their erosion, while retaining teacher guidance elsewhere. SPOD requires only binary episode success and model probabilities already available during OPD. Across two model families and three agentic benchmarks, SPOD consistently outperforms ordinary OPD and evaluated variants, improving final success by up to 15.2 percentage points and surpassing the teacher by up to 20.0 points. Moreover, SPOD's final checkpoints outperform even ordinary OPD's best intermediate checkpoints in all six settings, demonstrating that beyond-teacher gains can be not only preserved but further extended. Code: https://github.com/Jike338/SPOD
papers.ja_title: 蒸留で教師を超えた生徒がその後劣化する「蒸留の行き過ぎ」
papers.summary: オンポリシー蒸留 (生徒が自分の行動軌跡の上で教師の指導を受けて学習する手法) のマルチターンエージェントタスクで、最初は教師より弱かった生徒が学習中に教師を大きく上回るのに、学習を続けると性能が下がる「distillation overshoot (蒸留の行き過ぎ)」という現象を見つけた。決定レベル・タスクレベルの分析から、オンポリシー蒸留には「生徒の弱い判断を修復する」効果と「教師が好まない生徒自身の成功した選択を侵食する」効果という競合する 2 つの働きがあり、学習初期は修復が侵食を上回るが、学習が進むと侵食が逆転することが原因だと示した。これを踏まえ、教師と矛盾する指導のうち生徒が成功させた選択への部分だけを選択的に隠し、侵食を抑える確率の下限を加える Success-Preserving On-Policy Distillation (SPOD) を提案した。2 つのモデル系列・3 つのエージェントベンチマークで SPOD は通常のオンポリシー蒸留や比較手法を一貫して上回り、最終的な成功率を最大 15.2 ポイント改善し教師を最大 20.0 ポイント上回った。SPOD の最終チェックポイントは、通常のオンポリシー蒸留の最良の中間チェックポイントさえも 6 設定全てで上回った。
papers.why: 蒸留が「教師を超えた後に逆に劣化する」現象を初めて定量化し、成功した生徒の判断を守る具体的な修正法を示す、蒸留による後学習基盤の作り手に直接役立つ知見。
papers.summary_en: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains agents on their own trajectories using supervision from a stronger teacher; in multi-turn agentic tasks, a smaller, initially weaker student can substantially outperform its teacher during training, only to regress as distillation continues — a phenomenon termed distillation overshoot. Decision- and task-level analyses trace this to two competing effects of OPD: repairing weak student decisions and eroding successful student choices the teacher disfavors, with repair outpacing erosion early in training before erosion overtakes it. Success-Preserving On-Policy Distillation (SPOD) selectively masks conflicting teacher supervision on successful student choices and introduces a soft probability floor to counteract erosion, needing only binary episode success and already-available model probabilities. Across two model families and three agentic benchmarks, SPOD consistently outperforms ordinary OPD and evaluated variants, improving final success by up to 15.2 percentage points and surpassing the teacher by up to 20.0 points, with SPOD's final checkpoints outperforming even ordinary OPD's best intermediate checkpoints in all six settings.
papers.why_en: Quantifies for the first time a teacher-overshoot-then-regress failure mode in on-policy distillation and gives a concrete fix for protecting a student's successful choices, directly relevant to anyone building distillation-based post-training infrastructure.

papers.title: P2N: Reusing Deep Representations for Greater Effective Depth
papers.abstract: Mathematical problem solving and autonomous agents are increasingly important applications of language models, demanding stronger reasoning capabilities. Computational depth is a key resource for such reasoning, but adding model layers increases both training and inference costs, while test-time scaling incurs substantial additional inference computation. We introduce P2N (Previous to Next), which reuses the previous token's deep representations, already available during generation, to increase effective computational depth with negligible decoding overhead. Specifically, P2N adds the previous token's deep hidden state to the current token's shallow representation, allowing subsequent layers to build on previously completed deep computation. This recurrence extends effective computational depth across tokens, while introducing only a single vector addition per decoding step. We train the recurrence using parallel Jacobi updates restricted to a middle-layer core. Experiments with Qwen-style models show that, at 1.5B parameters, P2N improves GSM8K accuracy by over 10 percentage points under both zero-shot and few-shot prompting, with nearly unchanged decoding latency. The benefits also extend to language modeling and average performance on general downstream benchmarks. on general downstream benchmarks.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 前のトークンの深い表現を再利用して実効的な深さを増やす P2N
papers.summary: 数学的な問題解決や自律エージェントには強い推論能力が必要で、計算の「深さ」が鍵になる資源だが、層を増やすと学習・推論コストが増え、テスト時のスケーリング (何度も試行する) も推論計算を大きく増やす。P2N (Previous to Next) は、生成中にすでに手に入っている「前のトークンの深い層の表現」を今のトークンの浅い表現に加えることで、デコードのオーバーヘッドをほとんど増やさずに実効的な計算の深さを増やす。中間層のコアに限定した並列 Jacobi 更新でこの再帰を学習する。Qwen 系モデルで、1.5B パラメータのとき GSM8K の精度がゼロショット・フューショットの両方で 10 ポイント以上改善し、デコードの遅さはほぼ変わらなかった。この効果は言語モデリングや一般的な下流タスクの平均性能にも及んだ。
papers.why: 層を増やさずに前のトークンの深い表現を使い回すだけで実効的な計算の深さを増やすという低コストな構造上の工夫で、推論効率とモデル構造の両方に関わる具体例。
papers.summary_en: Mathematical problem solving and autonomous agents demand stronger reasoning, for which computational depth is a key resource, but adding layers increases training and inference costs while test-time scaling incurs substantial additional inference computation. P2N (Previous to Next) reuses the previous token's deep representations, already available during generation, adding them to the current token's shallow representation so subsequent layers build on previously completed deep computation, extending effective computational depth across tokens with only a single vector addition per decoding step; the recurrence is trained using parallel Jacobi updates restricted to a middle-layer core. On Qwen-style models at 1.5B parameters, P2N improves GSM8K accuracy by over 10 percentage points under both zero-shot and few-shot prompting, with nearly unchanged decoding latency, and the benefits extend to language modeling and average downstream performance.
papers.why_en: A low-cost architectural trick — reusing the previous token's deep representation instead of adding layers — that increases effective computational depth, relevant to both inference efficiency and model architecture.

papers.title: Dual-Slot: From Serial Loops to Parallel Slots in Language Models
papers.abstract: Looped language models increase computational depth by repeatedly applying shared layers, offering a way to improve model quality without adding parameters. However, sequential dependencies between loop iterations increase autoregressive decoding latency. We introduce Dual-Slot, an architecture that reorganizes serial looped computation into parallel latent and prediction slots. Rather than waiting for the current token's latent computation to finish, the prediction slot combines the previous token's deep latent state with the current representation, while the latent slot produces a state for the next decoding step. This shifts the latent dependency across adjacent tokens, replacing two sequential module invocations with a single paired invocation while preserving standard autoregressive generation. To preserve token-level parallelism during training, we use a small number of Jacobi iterations to refine latent states across the sequence in parallel. Experiments on Qwen-style dense and mixture-of-experts (MoE) models show consistent improvements in language modeling and average downstream accuracy. On the 1B dense model, Dual-Slot reduces Pile validation perplexity from 7.25 to 7.00 and improves average five-shot accuracy across nine task configurations by 2.26 percentage points. After supervised fine-tuning, it improves zero-shot GSM8K accuracy by 5.83 and 3.49 percentage points for the 1B dense and A0.6B MoE models, respectively. Across the evaluated batch sizes, Dual-Slot retains 93.1-96.5% of vanilla decoding throughput for the dense model and 98.1-99.6% for the MoE model.
papers.ja_title: ループ型モデルの直列依存を並列スロットにずらす Dual-Slot
papers.summary: ループ型言語モデル (同じ層を繰り返し使って計算の深さを増やす) はパラメータを増やさずに品質を上げられるが、ループの各反復が順番に依存するため自己回帰デコードが遅くなる。Dual-Slot は、直列のループ計算を並列の「潜在スロット」と「予測スロット」に再構成する。現在のトークンの潜在計算が終わるのを待たず、予測スロットが前のトークンの深い潜在状態と現在の表現を組み合わせ、潜在スロットは次のデコードステップのための状態を作ることで、隣接トークン間で潜在の依存をずらし、2 回の逐次モジュール呼び出しを 1 回のペア呼び出しに置き換えつつ通常の自己回帰生成を保つ。学習時は少数の Jacobi 反復で系列全体の潜在状態を並列に精緻化する。Qwen 系の密モデルと MoE (専門家混合) モデルで一貫した改善が見られ、1B の密モデルでは Pile の検証パープレキシティが 7.25 から 7.00 に下がり、9 タスク設定の平均 5-shot 精度が 2.26 ポイント改善した。教師あり微調整後は、1B 密モデルと A0.6B MoE モデルでゼロショット GSM8K 精度がそれぞれ 5.83 ポイント・3.49 ポイント改善した。評価したバッチサイズ全体で、Dual-Slot は密モデルで通常デコードのスループットの 93.1〜96.5%、MoE モデルで 98.1〜99.6% を維持した。
papers.why: ループ型モデルの「順番に待つ」依存を並列スロットにずらすという具体的な構造上の工夫で、品質とデコード速度を両立させるモデル構造の設計に直接使える。
papers.summary_en: Looped language models increase computational depth by repeatedly applying shared layers, improving quality without adding parameters, but sequential dependencies between loop iterations increase autoregressive decoding latency. Dual-Slot reorganizes serial looped computation into parallel latent and prediction slots: rather than waiting for the current token's latent computation to finish, the prediction slot combines the previous token's deep latent state with the current representation while the latent slot produces a state for the next decoding step, shifting the latent dependency across adjacent tokens and replacing two sequential module invocations with a single paired invocation while preserving standard autoregressive generation; training uses a small number of Jacobi iterations to refine latent states across the sequence in parallel. On Qwen-style dense and mixture-of-experts (MoE) models, Dual-Slot shows consistent improvements: on the 1B dense model it reduces Pile validation perplexity from 7.25 to 7.00 and improves average five-shot accuracy across nine task configurations by 2.26 percentage points, and after supervised fine-tuning it improves zero-shot GSM8K accuracy by 5.83 and 3.49 percentage points for the 1B dense and A0.6B MoE models respectively, while retaining 93.1-96.5% of vanilla decoding throughput for the dense model and 98.1-99.6% for the MoE model across evaluated batch sizes.
papers.why_en: A concrete architectural trick that shifts looped models' sequential-wait dependency into parallel slots, usable directly for architectures that want both quality gains and decoding speed.

papers.title: Toward Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Enterprise Retail Workflows over Heterogeneous Data Sources
papers.abstract: Enterprise retail workflows require agents to chain evidence across heterogeneous sources, from structured product and order records to unstructured inquiries and reviews, yet existing agentic RAG benchmarks rarely capture this challenge. To enable controlled evaluation of such workflows, we introduce RetailBridge, a compositional retail benchmark built from persona-driven simulations. Its questions are constructed by linking entities and intermediate answers across heterogeneous sources, requiring agents to identify the relevant sources, carry evidence between them, and produce a grounded answer. To systematically evaluate LLMs on these retail workflows, we develop RetailRAG, a retail-aware framework equipped with auto-schema briefing, source-routed plan chaining, and diagnostic plan revision. RetailRAG consistently outperforms existing agentic RAG baselines across all evaluation axes, serving as a strong reference system for assessing LLM agents on retail workflows. On RetailBridge, evaluating ten LLM backbones with RetailRAG reveals multi-source chaining as the dominant bottleneck across providers and model scales, suggesting that reliable retail agents require explicit cross-source orchestration rather than scaling alone. Code and data are publicly available at \url{https://github.com/DISL-Lab/RetailBridge}.

papers.title: Calibration-Free Early Stopping for Chain-of-Thought Reasoning via E-processes
papers.abstract: Reasoning large language models (LLMs) benefit from test-time scaling, motivating adaptive policies that spend tokens when they help and stop early otherwise. Existing rules halt when a confidence or stability signal crosses a threshold, but such thresholds rarely transfer across models and datasets, and validation-calibrated rules lose their guarantee under shifts in test-time horizon or signal dynamics. We reframe adaptive stopping as sequential evidence accumulation along the reasoning trajectory rather than threshold calibration on held-out data. Our framework runs two e-processes on a shared per-chunk signal: a commit stream tracks the signal's position relative to its slow trend, and an abstain stream tracks its signed velocity, making the two anti-correlated by construction. Under signal-level nulls on the per-chunk increments, Ville's inequality yields an anytime-valid signal-level false-alarm bound at user-specified significance levels, with no held-out calibration. Across various model--dataset combinations, the framework matches or exceeds calibration-based stopping on the token--accuracy Pareto front using zero calibration data, and the same significance level transfers unchanged across cells where calibration becomes infeasible.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 較正データなしで CoT 推論を早めに止める E-process
papers.summary: 推論する LLM (chain-of-thought で考える) はテスト時にトークンを使うほど良くなるが、どこで止めるかを決める既存のルールは確信度や安定性の信号がしきい値を超えたら止めるというもので、しきい値がモデルやデータセットをまたいで通用せず、ホールドアウトデータで較正したルールもテスト時の長さや信号の変化が起こると保証を失う。この研究は停止判断を「ホールドアウトでのしきい値較正」ではなく「推論の経路上で証拠を逐次積み重ねる」問題として再定義し、共有するチャンクごとの信号に対して 2 つの e-process (逐次検定の枠組み) を走らせる。一方は信号の位置を緩やかな傾向と比べる「commit」ストリーム、他方は符号付きの速度を追う「abstain」ストリームとし、構造的に互いに負の相関を持たせる。チャンクごとの増分にシグナルレベルの帰無仮説を置くと、Ville の不等式により、ホールドアウトでの較正なしに、指定した有意水準でいつでも成り立つ誤報率の上限が得られる。さまざまなモデル・データセットの組み合わせで、この枠組みはホールドアウトの較正データをゼロにしても較正ベースの停止とトークン対精度のパレートフロンティア上で同等以上の性能を示し、較正が実行不可能な設定でも同じ有意水準がそのまま通用した。
papers.why: テスト時スケーリングの「いつ止めるか」を較正データなしで理論的に保証する停止ルールを与え、推論コストを制御したい人の判断にそのまま使える。
papers.summary_en: Reasoning LLMs benefit from test-time scaling, motivating adaptive policies that stop spending tokens when they stop helping, but existing rules halt when a confidence or stability signal crosses a threshold, and such thresholds rarely transfer across models and datasets while validation-calibrated rules lose their guarantee under shifts in test-time horizon or signal dynamics. The paper reframes adaptive stopping as sequential evidence accumulation along the reasoning trajectory rather than threshold calibration on held-out data, running two e-processes on a shared per-chunk signal — a commit stream tracking the signal's position relative to its slow trend, and an abstain stream tracking its signed velocity, anti-correlated by construction. Under signal-level nulls on the per-chunk increments, Ville's inequality yields an anytime-valid signal-level false-alarm bound at user-specified significance levels, with no held-out calibration. Across various model-dataset combinations, the framework matches or exceeds calibration-based stopping on the token-accuracy Pareto front using zero calibration data, and the same significance level transfers unchanged across cells where calibration becomes infeasible.
papers.why_en: Gives a theoretically-guaranteed, calibration-free early-stopping rule for test-time scaling, directly usable by anyone who needs to control reasoning token cost.

papers.title: Improving the Expressive Power of Hybrid Sequence Models via Multi-Hop Retrieval
papers.abstract: Hybrid architectures offer a promising approach to efficient language modeling by combining a small number of full-attention layers with a larger number of efficient sequence layers, such as sparse attention and recurrent layers. While full-attention layers maintain a KV cache that grows linearly with sequence length, efficient layers typically rely on separate, fixed-size states rather than accessing this richer existing memory. Recent work has begun exploring ways to allow efficient layers access to the KV cache, but the theoretical benefits of such access, and the extent to which existing approaches can realize them remain poorly understood. We investigate these questions by analyzing the expressive power of individual hybrid blocks on function composition, a well-studied task in sequence-model expressivity associated with multi-hop reasoning. We first establish that both conventional hybrid blocks and those with top-$κ$ KV-cache access require $Ω(\sqrt{n})$ capacity to compute even two-function composition over a domain of size $n$. To overcome this limitation, we introduce the \emph{Multi-hop Retrieval Attention} (MuRA) hybrid block, a simple architecture that enables multi-hop retrieval from a shared KV cache while preserving asymptotic computational and memory efficiency. We prove that a single fixed size $m$-hop MuRA block can compute $m$-function composition, whereas computing $(m+1)$-function composition with the same retrieval depth requires polynomial model size, establishing a strict expressivity hierarchy in retrieval depth. Synthetic experiments support this hierarchy, showing that increasing retrieval depth enables learning progressively deeper compositions, substantially outperforming existing hybrid architectures. Together, our results identify multi-hop retrieval as a promising mechanism for improving the expressive power of efficient hybrid architectures.
papers.ja_title: ハイブリッドモデルに KV キャッシュへのマルチホップ検索を与える MuRA
papers.summary: ハイブリッドアーキテクチャ(少数のフルアテンション層と、スパースアテンションや再帰層など多数の効率的な層を組み合わせる)は効率的な言語モデリングに有望だが、フルアテンション層は系列長に線形に増える KV キャッシュを持つ一方、効率的な層は別の固定サイズの状態しか使わず、この豊富な既存メモリにアクセスしない。既存研究は効率的な層に KV キャッシュへのアクセスを与え始めているが、その理論的な利点や既存手法が実現できる範囲は分かっていなかった。関数合成 (マルチホップ推論に関連するタスク) に対する個々のハイブリッドブロックの表現力を分析し、通常のハイブリッドブロックと top-k の KV キャッシュアクセスを持つブロックの両方が、サイズ n の領域での 2 関数合成でさえ Ω(√n) の容量を必要とすることを示した。これを超えるため、共有 KV キャッシュからのマルチホップ検索を可能にしつつ漸近的な計算・メモリ効率を保つ Multi-hop Retrieval Attention (MuRA) ブロックを導入し、固定サイズ m-hop の MuRA ブロック 1 つで m 関数合成を計算できる一方、同じ検索深さで (m+1) 関数合成を計算するには多項式サイズのモデルが必要であることを証明した。合成実験でもこの階層が裏付けられ、検索深さを増やすほど段々深い合成を学習できるようになり、既存のハイブリッドアーキテクチャを大きく上回った。
papers.why: 効率的なハイブリッド層に KV キャッシュへのマルチホップアクセスを与えるという理論的に裏付けられた具体的な設計を示し、長文脈を扱うモデル構造の設計に新しい道具を与える。
papers.summary_en: Hybrid architectures combine a small number of full-attention layers with a larger number of efficient sequence layers (sparse attention, recurrent layers) for efficient language modeling, but while full-attention layers maintain a KV cache growing linearly with sequence length, efficient layers typically rely on separate fixed-size states rather than accessing this richer memory, and the theoretical benefits of giving them such access were poorly understood. Analyzing the expressive power of individual hybrid blocks on function composition (a task tied to multi-hop reasoning), the paper establishes that both conventional hybrid blocks and those with top-k KV-cache access require Omega(sqrt(n)) capacity to compute even two-function composition over a domain of size n. The Multi-hop Retrieval Attention (MuRA) block is introduced to overcome this, enabling multi-hop retrieval from a shared KV cache while preserving asymptotic computational and memory efficiency; a single fixed-size m-hop MuRA block can compute m-function composition, whereas computing (m+1)-function composition at the same retrieval depth requires polynomial model size, establishing a strict expressivity hierarchy. Synthetic experiments support this hierarchy, with increasing retrieval depth enabling progressively deeper compositions and substantially outperforming existing hybrid architectures.
papers.why_en: Provides a theoretically grounded design (MuRA) for giving efficient hybrid layers multi-hop access to the KV cache, a new tool for architectures handling long context.

papers.title: CD-OPD: Contextual Digest for On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract: Teacher takeover in on-policy distillation (OPD) can produce incorrect responses even when the student and teacher independently answer the same problem correctly, a failure we quantify using Collaboration Failure Rate (CFR). To address it, we propose Contextual Digest for On-Policy Distillation (CD-OPD). CD-OPD structures the earlier context of teacher guidance through a teacher-generated dependency graph, curating the required problem conditions and preceding reasoning as node summaries alongside the unchanged guidance in a Contextual Digest before student continuation. We further develop online meta-reweighting, which compares Digest segment gradients with a task gradient from independent student responses to improve student-only performance, favoring updates predicted to reduce task loss. Across eight benchmarks, CD-OPD improves average accuracy by 1.32--7.05 percentage points over representative existing OPD methods. It also reduces CFR by 27.4\%--56.4\% relative to existing takeover-based OPD methods.
papers.ja_title: 教師の指導を整理して「乗っ取り」を防ぐ CD-OPD
papers.summary: オンポリシー蒸留 (OPD) では、生徒と教師が同じ問題に独立に正解できる場合でも、教師が指導を「乗っ取る」ことで誤った応答を生み出す失敗が起き、これを Collaboration Failure Rate (CFR) として定量化した。CD-OPD (Contextual Digest for On-Policy Distillation) は、教師が生成した依存関係グラフを使って以前の文脈を構造化し、必要な問題の条件と先行する推論をノードの要約として整理し、変更していない指導と合わせて「Contextual Digest」として生徒の継続前に提示する。さらに、Digest のセグメントごとの勾配を生徒単独の応答から得たタスクの勾配と比較し、タスク損失を減らすと予測される更新を優先する「オンラインメタ再重み付け」を開発した。8 つのベンチマークで、CD-OPD は代表的な既存の OPD 手法に対し平均精度を 1.32〜7.05 ポイント改善し、既存の乗っ取り型 OPD 手法に対し CFR を 27.4〜56.4% 減らした。
papers.why: 教師による指導の「乗っ取り」が生徒の正しい判断を壊すという失敗を定量化し、文脈の整理と勾配比較による具体的な修正法を示す、蒸留による後学習基盤の作り手に役立つ知見。
papers.summary_en: Teacher takeover in on-policy distillation (OPD) can produce incorrect responses even when the student and teacher independently answer the same problem correctly, a failure quantified using Collaboration Failure Rate (CFR). Contextual Digest for On-Policy Distillation (CD-OPD) structures the earlier context of teacher guidance through a teacher-generated dependency graph, curating the required problem conditions and preceding reasoning as node summaries alongside the unchanged guidance in a Contextual Digest before student continuation, and further develops online meta-reweighting, which compares Digest segment gradients with a task gradient from independent student responses to favor updates predicted to reduce task loss. Across eight benchmarks, CD-OPD improves average accuracy by 1.32-7.05 percentage points over representative existing OPD methods and reduces CFR by 27.4-56.4% relative to existing takeover-based OPD methods.
papers.why_en: Quantifies how teacher takeover in on-policy distillation can corrupt a student's correct judgment and offers a concrete fix via context curation and gradient comparison, useful for anyone building distillation-based post-training infrastructure.

papers.title: MOSAIC: Multi-Objective Search for Allocating Inference Cache Across LLM Decoder Layers
papers.abstract: The Key-Value (KV) cache is the main memory bottleneck of long-context LLM inference. Token eviction methods such as SnapKV, H2O, AdaKV and L2Norm shrink it, but they give every transformer layer the same budget, although layers differ in which tokens they need. We present MOSAIC, a multi-objective neural architecture search that learns per-layer KV-cache budgets for any eviction method. One search maps the trade-off between average budget and task score; its best allocation transfers to every target budget without further search, and an optional budget-constrained search refines it. Across four eviction methods on Llama-3-8B-Instruct and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2, MOSAIC beats uniform allocation in 146 of 154 (task, method, budget) settings, by up to +48 points on RULER and +11.9 on LongBench (LCC). On both models, it reaches the score of uniform allocation with up to 4x less KV cache (75% smaller). Against EvolKV, MOSAIC explores a ~10^40 x larger search space with 4x fewer evaluations and 18% fewer GPU-hours per budget, and scores higher in 5 of 6 settings. The learned allocations consistently favour a small set of middle layers.
papers.ja_title: KV キャッシュの予算を層ごとに自動配分する MOSAIC
papers.summary: KV キャッシュは長文脈 LLM 推論の主なメモリの壁。SnapKV・H2O・AdaKV・L2Norm などのトークン削減 (eviction) 手法はキャッシュを縮めるが、層ごとに必要なトークンが違うのに全ての層に同じ予算を与えてしまう。MOSAIC は、任意の eviction 手法に対して層ごとの KV キャッシュ予算を学習する多目的ニューラルアーキテクチャ探索で、1 回の探索で平均予算とタスク性能のトレードオフの全体像を描き、その最良の配分は追加探索なしでどの目標予算にも転用でき、予算を指定した探索でさらに精緻化できる。Llama-3-8B-Instruct と Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 上で 4 つの eviction 手法を試した 154 の (タスク・手法・予算) 設定のうち 146 で均一配分を上回り、RULER で最大 48 ポイント、LongBench (LCC) で 11.9 ポイント改善した。両モデルで、均一配分と同じ性能を最大 4 倍少ない KV キャッシュ (75% 削減) で達成した。既存の探索手法 EvolKV に対しては約 10^40 倍広い探索空間を、4 倍少ない評価回数・予算ごと 18% 少ない GPU 時間で探索し、6 設定中 5 設定で高い性能を示した。学習された配分は一貫して少数の中間層を優先した。
papers.why: KV キャッシュの予算を層ごとに自動で決めるという、既存の eviction 手法にそのまま重ねられる具体的な改善で、長文脈推論サービングのメモリ最適化に直接使える。
papers.summary_en: The KV cache is the main memory bottleneck of long-context LLM inference; token eviction methods such as SnapKV, H2O, AdaKV, and L2Norm shrink it but give every transformer layer the same budget even though layers differ in which tokens they need. MOSAIC is a multi-objective neural architecture search that learns per-layer KV-cache budgets for any eviction method: one search maps the trade-off between average budget and task score, its best allocation transfers to every target budget without further search, and an optional budget-constrained search refines it. Across four eviction methods on Llama-3-8B-Instruct and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2, MOSAIC beats uniform allocation in 146 of 154 (task, method, budget) settings, by up to 48 points on RULER and 11.9 on LongBench (LCC), and reaches the score of uniform allocation with up to 4x less KV cache (75% smaller) on both models; against EvolKV it explores a ~10^40x larger search space with 4x fewer evaluations and 18% fewer GPU-hours per budget, scoring higher in 5 of 6 settings, and the learned allocations consistently favor a small set of middle layers.
papers.why_en: A concrete, drop-in improvement over existing KV-cache eviction methods — automatically learning per-layer budgets — directly usable for memory optimization in long-context inference serving.

papers.title: System X: An LLM Decision Model That Replies from Its Own KV Cache
papers.abstract: Decision models return probabilities over supplied options, but a deployed agent may also need to reply in words. The present study introduces System X, a large language model (LLM) decision model that adds a text-reply option to the LLM-as-Jev readout. When this option wins, or confidence is low, the same model continues from the decision's key-value (KV) cache, avoiding a repeated prompt prefill. Qwen3-0.6B has been fine-tuned with LoRA on Reason-9k and Bitext reply rows. JevBench accuracy shows no statistically significant change (55.4% to 54.5%, p=0.87), while expected calibration error falls from 0.292 to 0.169. Held-out Bitext routing accuracy reaches 98.3%. Cache reuse saves 15-37% of latency on an Apple M4 Pro, with token-identical replies in the FP32 demonstration cases. Scoring options on copies of the prompt cache matches full-sequence scoring to within 1.4e-6 in probability. Adding dialogue, industry and complaint data (System X+) improves support-task results but lowers IFEval accuracy from 55.5% to 45.0%. System X v4 uses Qwen3-1.7B, rebalanced data and teacher-rewritten reply targets. Against its base LLM, JevBench accuracy rises from 55.0% to 61.0% (p=0.04), with no statistically significant IFEval change (p=0.71). A matched latency test on unadapted Qwen3-1.7B saves 17-39%. One LLM judge prefers v4 replies to an unadapted 1.7B second call (31 to 11 pairs, p=0.003); the other's preference is not significant. These reply comparisons also differ in prompts and generation limits. State conflicts and unsupported reply details remain failure modes. Further studies with several seeds, human raters and real support data are recommended.
papers.ja_title: 自分の KV キャッシュから続けて答える決定モデル System X
papers.summary: 判断モデル(選択肢に対する確率を返すモデル)は実際にデプロイされたエージェントでは言葉で返答する場面もあるが、判断と返答を別々に行うとプロンプトを再び読み込む(prefill)コストがかかる。System X は決定モデルに「文章で答える」選択肢を追加し、この選択肢が選ばれたり確信度が低い場合は、同じ決定の KV キャッシュから続けて生成してプロンプトの再読み込みを避ける。Qwen3-0.6B を Reason-9k と Bitext の返答データで LoRA 微調整すると、JevBench 精度は統計的に有意な変化なし(55.4%→54.5%, p=0.87)だが期待キャリブレーション誤差は 0.292 から 0.169 に下がり、保留にした Bitext のルーティング精度は 98.3% に達した。キャッシュ再利用は Apple M4 Pro で遅延を 15〜37% 節約し、プロンプトキャッシュのコピー上でのスコアリングはフルシーケンスでのスコアリングと確率で 1.4e-6 以内に一致した。Qwen3-1.7B・リバランスしたデータ・教師による返答の書き換えを使う System X v4 では、ベース LLM に対し JevBench 精度が 55.0% から 61.0% に上がり(p=0.04)、調整していない Qwen3-1.7B との遅延を揃えた比較では 17〜39% を節約した。
papers.why: 判断と自然文返答を同じ KV キャッシュから続けて生成することでプロンプトの再読み込みコストを避ける具体的な設計で、判断と返答の両方を行うエージェントの推論サービングに使える。
papers.summary_en: Decision models return probabilities over supplied options, but a deployed agent may also need to reply in words, and handling decision and reply separately costs a repeated prompt prefill. System X adds a text-reply option to the LLM-as-judge readout, and when this option wins or confidence is low, the same model continues from the decision's KV cache, avoiding a repeated prefill. Qwen3-0.6B fine-tuned with LoRA on Reason-9k and Bitext reply rows shows JevBench accuracy with no statistically significant change (55.4% to 54.5%, p=0.87) while expected calibration error falls from 0.292 to 0.169, with held-out Bitext routing accuracy reaching 98.3%; cache reuse saves 15-37% of latency on an Apple M4 Pro, and scoring options on copies of the prompt cache matches full-sequence scoring to within 1.4e-6 in probability. System X v4, using Qwen3-1.7B with rebalanced data and teacher-rewritten reply targets, raises JevBench accuracy from 55.0% to 61.0% against its base LLM (p=0.04), with a matched latency test on unadapted Qwen3-1.7B saving 17-39%.
papers.why_en: A concrete design that lets a decision model continue into a natural-language reply from its own KV cache, avoiding a repeated prefill, useful for agent serving that must both decide and reply.

papers.title: Clean Forcing: Drift-Resistant Autoregressive Video Diffusion with a Frozen Base
papers.abstract: Autoregressive (AR) video diffusion models generate streaming video of arbitrary length by conditioning each new chunk of frames on those already generated. However, they suffer from exposure bias, where a model trained on clean context must continue from its own imperfect outputs, and errors compound until quality collapses within seconds (drift). Existing methods either require cluster-scale base retraining, apply training-free inference corrections with inconsistent results, or train frozen-base correctors for sampling and cache errors. We instead find that drift is largely deterministic and therefore learnable, as holding the noisy state fixed while varying only the history reveals a counterfactual velocity gap that is ~95% systematic across noise seeds. Based on this observation, we introduce Clean Forcing, which trains a 5.9M-parameter LoRA corrector on the frozen base model to regress this gap, with a closed-loop stage that adds DAgger-style aggregation and a drift-contraction objective to expose the corrector to its own rollouts. Because the clean histories can be the base model's own single-shot generations, training needs no real videos, and the merged corrector adds no inference cost. In 50 s text-to-video generation, Clean Forcing reduces Δ-drift from +11.3 to +1.65 without real video and to -0.16 with 40 real clips, improving on the best published result of +3.57 with over 150x less data. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Clean Forcing outperforms prior methods in aesthetic quality and data efficiency with reduced drift for long-horizon video generation.

papers.title: Spherical Fixed-Point Reasoners: Adaptive Loop Halting on the Hypersphere
papers.abstract: Looped (weight-tied) transformers enable adaptive computation by allocating more iterations to harder inputs. Fixed-Point Reasoners (FPRM) achieve this with a damped fixed-point solver, but operate in an unbounded Euclidean residual space with coupled rescaling and relative-norm halting. We introduce Spherical Fixed-Point Reasoners (SFPRM), which perform the same computation on the unit hypersphere of normalized transformers (nGPT). Input injection, damping, and halting become geodesic operations, yielding boundedness by construction and eliminating coefficient coupling. We prove fixed-point existence, local convergence under an explicit step-size condition, and global convergence under strong injection.
