On Sudoku-Extreme, Maze-Hard, and Mini-ARC, SFPRM achieves 96.6%, 87.9%, and 59.1% test accuracy, respectively, outperforming FPRM and other baselines while allocating test-time compute more effectively. Its converged geometry is also interpretable: token-input angles capture puzzle structure and predict correctness.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 球面上で止まり方を安定させる Spherical Fixed-Point Reasoners
papers.summary: ループ型(重みを共有する)トランスフォーマーは難しい入力に多くの反復を割り当てて適応的に計算できる。Fixed-Point Reasoners (FPRM) は減衰付きの不動点ソルバーでこれを実現するが、無限に広がるユークリッド残差空間で動くため係数が結合し、相対ノルムでの停止判断も不安定になる。Spherical Fixed-Point Reasoners (SFPRM) は、正規化されたトランスフォーマー (nGPT) の単位超球面の上で同じ計算を行い、入力注入・減衰・停止判断をすべて測地線上の操作にすることで構造的に値を有界にし係数の結合を解消する。不動点の存在、明示的なステップサイズ条件のもとでの局所収束、強い注入のもとでの大域収束を証明した。Sudoku-Extreme・Maze-Hard・Mini-ARC でそれぞれ 96.6%、87.9%、59.1% のテスト精度を達成し、FPRM や他のベースラインを上回り、テスト時の計算をより効果的に割り振った。収束後の幾何も解釈可能で、トークンと入力の角度がパズルの構造を捉え正しさを予測した。
papers.why: 適応的な計算割り当てを行うループ型推論モデルの不安定さ(係数の結合・停止判断の不安定さ)を球面上の幾何に移すことで理論的に解消する具体例で、テスト時スケーリングの設計に使える。
papers.summary_en: Looped (weight-tied) transformers enable adaptive computation by allocating more iterations to harder inputs; Fixed-Point Reasoners (FPRM) achieve this with a damped fixed-point solver but operate in an unbounded Euclidean residual space with coupled rescaling and relative-norm halting. Spherical Fixed-Point Reasoners (SFPRM) perform the same computation on the unit hypersphere of normalized transformers (nGPT), making input injection, damping, and halting geodesic operations, yielding boundedness by construction and eliminating coefficient coupling; the paper proves fixed-point existence, local convergence under an explicit step-size condition, and global convergence under strong injection. On Sudoku-Extreme, Maze-Hard, and Mini-ARC, SFPRM achieves 96.6%, 87.9%, and 59.1% test accuracy respectively, outperforming FPRM and other baselines while allocating test-time compute more effectively, and its converged geometry is interpretable, with token-input angles capturing puzzle structure and predicting correctness.
papers.why_en: Resolves instability (coefficient coupling, unstable halting) in adaptive-compute looped reasoning models by moving the computation onto spherical geometry, a concrete tool for test-time-scaling design.

papers.title: OPDArena: Understanding Learning and Forgetting in On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) is increasingly used for language model post-training, yet how teacher supervision shapes learning and forgetting remains unclear. We present OPDArena, a framework comparing supervised fine-tuning (SFT), reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR), and OPD across five pretrained models and diverse teacher sources. It jointly evaluates mathematical learning, general capability retention, and predictive distribution changes. Teacher choice strongly shapes retention: students of RLVR-trained teachers improve on the target task while retaining prior capabilities, whereas students of SFT-trained teachers incur greater capability loss. Across post-training methods, out-of-domain (OOD) distribution change shows a more consistent positive association with forgetting than in-domain change. To understand how teacher choice affects these changes, we examine the additional information teachers provide relative to the student's pretrained model. Controlled teacher comparisons show that the task-specific preferences teachers acquire through post-training make student updates more concentrated in-domain.
papers.ja_title: 教師の選び方が蒸留の忘却を左右する OPDArena
papers.summary: オンポリシー蒸留 (OPD) は言語モデルの後学習に使われるようになっているが、教師の指導が学習と忘却をどう形作るかは分かっていなかった。OPDArena は、5 つの事前学習済みモデルと多様な教師の組み合わせで教師あり微調整 (SFT)・検証可能な報酬を使う強化学習 (RLVR)・OPD を比較し、数学の学習・一般的な能力の保持・予測分布の変化を同時に評価する枠組み。教師の選び方は保持を強く左右し、RLVR で学習した教師の生徒は対象タスクを改善しつつ以前の能力を保持するが、SFT で学習した教師の生徒はより大きな能力の損失を受ける。後学習の手法をまたいで見ると、ドメイン外 (OOD) の分布変化の方がドメイン内の変化より忘却との関連が一貫して強く、教師が後学習を通じて獲得した「タスク特有の好み」が生徒の更新をよりドメイン内に集中させることが分かった。
papers.why: 蒸留の教師選びが生徒の忘却をどう左右するかを RLVR 対 SFT 教師で定量的に示した知見で、RL・蒸留による後学習基盤の教師選定に直接役立つ。
papers.summary_en: On-policy distillation (OPD) is increasingly used for language model post-training, yet how teacher supervision shapes learning and forgetting remains unclear. OPDArena compares supervised fine-tuning (SFT), reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR), and OPD across five pretrained models and diverse teacher sources, jointly evaluating mathematical learning, general capability retention, and predictive distribution changes. Teacher choice strongly shapes retention: students of RLVR-trained teachers improve on the target task while retaining prior capabilities, whereas students of SFT-trained teachers incur greater capability loss; across post-training methods, out-of-domain (OOD) distribution change shows a more consistent positive association with forgetting than in-domain change, and controlled teacher comparisons show that task-specific preferences teachers acquire through post-training make student updates more concentrated in-domain.
papers.why_en: A quantitative account of how teacher choice (RLVR vs SFT) drives forgetting in distillation, directly useful for teacher selection in RL/distillation post-training infrastructure.

papers.title: Whose Credential Is It? How Owner Attribution in Agent MemoryShapes Cross-User Account Misuse
papers.abstract: Shared long-term memory lets an LLM agent serving one user inadvertently retrieve another user's credentials, but it is unclear when such exposure leads to actual harm. We introduce a three-stage audit that separates three events: a foreign credential reaches the prompt (exposure), the agent acts with it (behavior), and the other user's account changes (state). In AppWorld, a store that mixes 763 past logins from all users retrieves another user's credential for 84.7 percent of required apps, yet agents rarely act on it. Misuse appears in a stress test where memory lacks the user's own credential and presents a single foreign one as the user's record: seven agents then use it in 80 to 94 percent of runs and change the victim's account in up to 43 percent, sometimes passing the official check. Naming the owner before or inside each credential line prevents most of this: with all else fixed, misuse falls from 92 to 1 of 305 paired runs, also with name-free usernames, though owner-bound notes cost 3 to 5 successful tasks per model on clean memory. A wrongly written owner largely restores misuse; trailing owner tags and added safety instructions help only some models. Agent memory should consistently record whose credential it stores, and evaluations should measure behavior, not only exposure.

papers.title: Not Every Rollout Needs Distillation: Correctness-Filtered On-Policy Self-Distillation
papers.abstract: On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) supervises student-generated trajectories with a reference-conditioned version of the same base model. We ask whether every trajectory supplies distinct supervision that warrants its distillation cost. Gradient measurements on Qwen3-1.7B at initialization reveal that correct and incorrect responses have similar individual gradient magnitudes, but incorrect responses have approximately three times the coherent gradient share. Their estimated population-mean directions also largely overlap. A signal--noise model fitted at a small group size tracks alignment at larger group sizes without refitting. Motivated by these measurements, we introduce correctness-filtered OPSD (C-OPSD), which generates one response per problem and distills only a subset of incorrect responses. Removing unselected rows before both distillation forwards avoids their teacher/student forward and student backward work. Across Qwen3-1.7B, 4B, and 8B on AIME24, AIME25, and HMMT25, C-OPSD achieves on-par performance with full OPSD. In a measured micro-batch-size-four implementation, executed rows decrease by approximately 68%, and with retained rows packed into full micro-batches, training takes about 40% less time while rollout generation remains unchanged. Together, the measurements and training results connect outcome-conditioned supervision redundancy to more compute-efficient distillation.
papers.ja_title: 誤答の一部だけ蒸留すればよい Correctness-Filtered OPSD
papers.summary: オンポリシー自己蒸留 (OPSD、生徒自身が生成した軌跡を同じベースモデルの参照条件付き版で指導する) では、全ての軌跡が蒸留コストに見合う独自の教示を与えているのかは分かっていなかった。Qwen3-1.7B の初期化時点での勾配測定から、正解と誤答の応答は個々の勾配の大きさは似ているが、誤答の応答は整合した勾配の割合がおよそ 3 倍大きく、推定された母平均の方向もおおむね重なることが分かった。小さいグループサイズで当てはめた信号対雑音モデルは、再フィッティングなしで大きいグループサイズでの整合性を追跡できた。これに基づき、問題ごとに 1 つの応答だけ生成し誤答の応答の一部のみを蒸留する correctness-filtered OPSD (C-OPSD) を提案し、選ばれなかった行を蒸留と生徒のバックワード計算の両方の前に取り除くことで計算を省く。Qwen3-1.7B・4B・8B で AIME24・AIME25・HMMT25 において、C-OPSD は通常の OPSD と同等の性能を達成した。マイクロバッチサイズ 4 の実装で計測したところ、実行される行はおよそ 68% 減少し、残った行をフルのマイクロバッチに詰め込むことで、ロールアウト生成の時間は変わらないまま学習時間が約 40% 短縮された。
papers.why: 蒸留する必要のないロールアウトを勾配の整合性から見分けて計算を削るという具体的な効率化で、RL・蒸留の計算コストを減らしたい後学習基盤の作り手に直接使える。
papers.summary_en: On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) supervises student-generated trajectories with a reference-conditioned version of the same base model, but whether every trajectory supplies supervision that warrants its distillation cost was unclear. Gradient measurements on Qwen3-1.7B at initialization reveal that correct and incorrect responses have similar individual gradient magnitudes, but incorrect responses have approximately three times the coherent gradient share, with their estimated population-mean directions largely overlapping; a signal-noise model fitted at a small group size tracks alignment at larger group sizes without refitting. Correctness-filtered OPSD (C-OPSD) generates one response per problem and distills only a subset of incorrect responses, removing unselected rows before both distillation forwards and student backward work. Across Qwen3-1.7B, 4B, and 8B on AIME24, AIME25, and HMMT25, C-OPSD achieves on-par performance with full OPSD; in a measured micro-batch-size-four implementation, executed rows decrease by approximately 68%, and with retained rows packed into full micro-batches, training takes about 40% less time while rollout generation remains unchanged.
papers.why_en: A concrete efficiency gain — identifying redundant rollouts via gradient coherence and skipping their compute — directly useful for cutting the training cost of RL/distillation post-training infrastructure.

papers.title: LEAPS: Long-context Evaluation of Adaptive Pattern Learning and State Tracking
papers.abstract: Long-context language models (LCLMs) power agents that act over long trajectories, from improving a codebase to running research experiments to forecasters that condition on lengthy histories. These applications draw on three distinct long-context capabilities: recall, where the answer is a fact present in the context; state tracking, where the outcome can be computed by performing a series of transformations to a specified state; and pattern learning, where the goal is to make a prediction by sampling from a distribution inferred from many observations. Existing benchmarks primarily focus on the first capability. In this work, we introduce LEAPS (Long-context Evaluation of Adaptive Pattern learning and State tracking), a collection of 12 novel datasets, spanning agentic workflows, behavioral modeling, and forecasting of market and world events. By construction, LEAPS is resistant to data contamination, extends to millions of input tokens, and uses reliable metrics. We evaluate 30 API and open models from 8K to 512K input tokens. LEAPS distinguishes models that perform near perfectly on recall tasks, finding that such models' state tracking and pattern learning abilities can vary significantly and degrade much more dramatically with increasing input lengths--even for pattern learning, where more observations should make learning a theoretically easier task. Moreover, thinking models often underperform their base counterparts, exhausting their generation budget or oversimplifying the task. We hope LEAPS can guide the development of the next generation of LCLMs.

papers.title: PaceVLA: Adaptive Temporal Action Quantization in Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.abstract: Fast and reliable manipulation is crucial for practical robot deployment. Although Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have recently shown remarkable progress as generalist robot policies, their execution often remains temporally inefficient. A key source of this inefficiency is that policies learn fine-grained temporal patterns from teleoperated demonstrations, requiring many low-level action steps. Temporal action quantization offers a simple way to accelerate execution by aggregating consecutive low-level actions into temporally coarser actions. However, applying action quantization without considering when fine-grained control is required introduces a speed-accuracy trade-off: accelerated actions may efficiently reduce redundant steps in some phases, while discarding critical motion details in precision-sensitive interactions. To address this, we propose PaceVLA, a unified framework for adaptive temporal execution in VLAs that integrates two coupled components: (1) mode-specific action decoders built on a shared action expert, supporting multiple temporal granularities and prediction horizons, and (2) a quantizability-guided mode selection scheme which decides whether coarse execution is appropriate, and a context-conditioned router that selects an execution mode at each inference step. Experiments across three multi-task simulation benchmarks and six real-world tasks show that PaceVLA improves execution efficiency while maintaining task success rate across multiple embodiments, including long-horizon and dexterous manipulation.

papers.title: TempoMoE: Identifying and Steering Fast-Slow Thinking Experts for Efficient Multimodal Reasoning
papers.abstract: Multimodal Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) reasoning models rely on long chain-of-thought (CoT) for complex tasks, yet often overthink easy inputs, increasing token cost and latency, and sometimes degrading accuracy. Existing methods optimize reasoning length during training or impose external control at inference, but leave the underlying reasoning mechanism a black box. We find that fast and slow thinking exhibit distinct expert-routing patterns: holding the input fixed and varying only the prompted reasoning tempo produces stable routing shifts. Suppressing slow-thinking experts shortens the reasoning chain, whereas suppressing fast-thinking experts lengthens it, providing causal evidence that these experts influence reasoning depth. Based on this finding, we propose TempoMoE, a training-free, two-stage framework. It identifies fast- and slow-thinking experts via tempo-contrastive routing analysis and redistributes routing weights within the original top-k set according to sample difficulty. It amplifies fast-thinking experts and suppresses slow-thinking experts on easy inputs and reverses this adjustment on hard ones, enabling difficulty-adaptive control over reasoning depth. We evaluate TempoMoE on Kimi-VL, Qwen3-VL, and ERNIE-4.5-VL across six benchmarks. Compared with Vanilla, TempoMoE consistently improves accuracy while reducing output tokens, with accuracy gains of up to 2.6 points and token reductions of up to 35.4%.
papers.ja_title: MoE 推論モデルの「速い思考・遅い思考」担当エキスパートを見つけて操る手法
papers.summary: マルチモーダル MoE(専門家が分担するモデル)推論モデルは簡単な問題でも長く考えすぎてトークン数が増える。本研究は、推論の速さ(テンポ)を変えるだけでルーティング(どの専門家を使うか)が安定して変わることを見つけ、遅い思考を担う専門家と速い思考を担う専門家を特定して問題の難しさに応じて重みを調整する学習不要の手法 TempoMoE を提案した。Kimi-VL など 3 モデル・6 ベンチマークで、何もしない場合と比べて精度を最大 2.6 ポイント上げつつ出力トークンを最大 35.4% 減らした。
papers.why: 学習や追加データを使わずルーティングの重み付けだけで推論コストを削れるため、既存の MoE 推論サービスにそのまま組み込みやすい。
papers.summary_en: Multimodal MoE reasoning models often overthink easy inputs, burning tokens and latency. The authors find that prompting only the reasoning tempo (fast vs. slow) produces stable, causal shifts in expert routing, and build TempoMoE, a training-free method that identifies fast-/slow-thinking experts and reweights them by sample difficulty. Across Kimi-VL, Qwen3-VL, and ERNIE-4.5-VL on six benchmarks, it improves accuracy by up to 2.6 points while cutting output tokens by up to 35.4% versus vanilla.
papers.why_en: A training-free routing-weight intervention that cuts inference cost on deployed MoE reasoning models without retraining is directly usable in serving pipelines.

papers.title: Nash-MOPD: Optimizing Task Trade-offs in Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract: Multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) aggregates the capabilities of multiple domain-expert teachers into a single student model. However, all domains in MOPD share the student's finite budget of optimization steps and rollouts. Fixed uses constant domain sampling ratios based on corpus sizes; by contrast, D$^3$-MOPD adjusts the ratios using the teacher-student reverse-KL divergence and its recent decrease. However, favoring large recent decreases can direct more training toward domains that already improve quickly, while domains that improve more slowly may receive too few examples. To address inflexible allocation and the risk of giving insufficient training to domains that improve more slowly, we propose Nash-MOPD, an adaptive domain scheduler based on a local minimax game using existing reverse-KL statistics. The equilibrium maximizes the smallest predicted proportional reduction under the local model and gives more prompts to domains that need more examples for comparable improvement. Consequently, Nash-MOPD responds to changing learning progress and supports domains that improve more slowly without extra teacher queries or rollouts. At step 100, Nash-MOPD exceeds both baselines' final mathematics and code checkpoint scores on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B and reaches Fixed's on Qwen3-8B-Base. Furthermore, it leads eight of nine reported metrics and is best or tied best on all six mathematics and code accuracy metrics, respectively.
papers.ja_title: 複数の専門教師から生徒モデルへ蒸留するとき、どの分野にどれだけ練習させるか
papers.summary: 複数の分野専門の教師モデルから 1 つの生徒モデルへオンポリシー蒸留(生徒自身の出力を教師に評価させて学習する方式)をする際、学習の予算(ステップ数)は全分野で共有される。既存手法は教師と生徒の KL ダイバージェンス(分布のずれ)の最近の下がり方で配分を決めるが、これだと伸びが速い分野にばかり練習が集中してしまう。本研究は、各分野が同じだけ改善するために必要な練習量をミニマックスゲーム(最悪の場合を最大化する考え方)で均衡点として求める Nash-MOPD を提案し、DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B の数学・コードの最終スコアを既存 2 手法より上回った。
papers.why: 複数教師からの蒸留で分野間の練習配分を自動調整する一般的な仕組みであり、RL 後学習の基盤設計で分野バランスを取る際の参考になる。
papers.summary_en: Multi-teacher on-policy distillation shares a finite training budget across domains, and prior schedulers that chase the fastest-improving domain starve slower ones. Nash-MOPD reframes allocation as a local minimax game over reverse-KL statistics, giving more prompts to domains needing more examples for comparable gains. At step 100 it exceeds both baselines' final math/code scores on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B and matches Fixed on Qwen3-8B-Base, leading on eight of nine reported metrics.
papers.why_en: A general, teacher-query-free scheduler for balancing domains in multi-teacher distillation is a reusable building block for RL post-training pipelines.

papers.title: RECAP: Reciprocal Sparse Attention and Hierarchical Caching for Efficient Video Diffusion
papers.abstract: Diffusion transformers generate high-quality videos but remain computationally expensive. Sparse attention and temporal caching reduce computation within and across denoising steps, respectively, offering a natural composition. However, predictions produced with sparse attention become sources for temporal reuse, coupling their errors along the sampling trajectory. We observe that improving the accuracy of these sources recovers fidelity without changing the reuse schedule, and that sparsification errors remain directionally aligned across nearby steps, suggesting that correction information can be shared rather than recomputed. These observations motivate RECAP, a training-free method that couples sparse attention with hierarchical caching through reciprocal correction, adaptively coordinated by online error feedback. Cached dense refinement corrects omitted interactions in current sparse estimates, while fresh sparse statistics track input changes and regulate the aging correction. The resulting predictions then renew the sources for whole-step prediction reuse, allowing prediction history to advance between dense refreshes. We evaluate RECAP on multiple video diffusion models against sparse-attention methods, caching methods, and their direct compositions. On HunyuanVideo at 720p 5-second generation, RECAP achieves a 3.05x speedup and outperforms all tested direct compositions in both fidelity and inference speed.
papers.ja_title: 動画生成モデルの高速化: 疎な注意とキャッシュの誤差を互いに補正し合う
papers.summary: 動画を作る拡散トランスフォーマー(diffusion transformer)は高品質だが計算が重い。注意機構を疎(スパース、一部だけ計算)にする手法とステップ間で結果を再利用するキャッシュ手法は両立できるが、疎な注意で出た誤差がキャッシュによって後のステップまで持ち越されてしまう問題があった。RECAP は学習なしで、キャッシュされた密な(全部計算した)結果で疎な注意の誤差を補正し、逆に疎な注意の統計で古いキャッシュの補正量を調整する仕組みを作り、HunyuanVideo の 720p・5 秒生成で 3.05 倍の高速化を達成し、他の組み合わせ手法より画質も速度も上回った。
papers.why: 疎な注意とキャッシュという 2 つの高速化手法を安全に組み合わせる考え方は、動画生成サービングのレイテンシ削減にそのまま使える。
papers.summary_en: Diffusion transformers generate high-quality video but remain costly; sparse attention and temporal caching each cut compute, but composing them lets sparsification errors propagate through cached reuse across steps. RECAP, a training-free method, uses cached dense refinement to correct sparse-attention errors and fresh sparse statistics to regulate cache aging, achieving a 3.05x speedup on HunyuanVideo 720p 5-second generation while outperforming all tested direct compositions in fidelity and speed.
papers.why_en: A principled way to compose sparse attention with caching without compounding their errors is directly applicable to reducing video-generation serving latency.

papers.title: An Empirical Study of Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for Mixture-of-Experts LLMs
papers.abstract: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods are critical for adapting large models under resource-constrained settings. However, as mixture-of-experts (MoE) architectures, which offer efficient inference at massive parameter scales, gain increasing prevalence in the community, a critical gap arising from the lack of systematic recipes for applying PEFT to MoE models. To narrow this gap, we conduct a large-scale systematic study that investigates a set of essential design recipes, including which modules should be adapted, which granularity should be used to adapt MoE modules, which PEFT method to use, and to what extent should the load-balancing objective be used, across three MoE backbones on downstream tasks and general knowledge tasks. Our experiments yield several key insights. First, adapting MoE experts alone achieves the highest downstream performance with competitive general capability retention under a comparable parameter budget. Second, native expert-weight updates offer a better downstream--retention trade-off than adapters that bypass experts or entire MoE modules. Third, LoRA and DoRA together define the strongest operating region for high downstream accuracy among the evaluated PEFT methods. Fourth, no nonzero load-balancing coefficient Pareto-dominates the zero baseline. We finally evaluate a weight-level redesign of MoE$^2$-LoRA on Qwen3. Moving its module-level bypass pool into native expert weights improves all four upstream endpoints by 2.4 to 17.9 points with 17% fewer trainable parameters and a 3.2-point average downstream cost.
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: MoE(専門家混合)モデルの効率的な微調整、どこをどう調整すれば良いかを総点検
papers.summary: 専門家混合(Mixture-of-Experts, MoE)構造の大規模モデルを少ないパラメータで微調整する方法(PEFT)には、どの部分を・どの粒度で・どの手法で調整すべきかの定まったやり方がなかった。本研究は 3 種類の MoE モデルで体系的に比較し、専門家そのものを直接調整するのが下流タスクの性能と元の知識の保持を両立しやすく、LoRA と DoRA が最も強い手法であり、負荷分散の正則化項を追加しても 0(なし)を上回る設定は見つからないと報告した。さらに既存手法 MoE2-LoRA を専門家の重みを直接使う形に作り直すと、学習可能パラメータを 17% 減らしながら 4 つの評価指標を 2.4〜17.9 ポイント改善した。
papers.why: MoE モデルを安く微調整する際の設計選択(調整箇所・粒度・手法・正則化)について実測に基づく指針を与え、再現可能な比較の作法も示している。
papers.summary_en: There was no systematic recipe for parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) of mixture-of-experts (MoE) LLMs -- which modules, what granularity, which method, how much load-balancing. A large-scale study across three MoE backbones finds adapting the experts directly gives the best downstream/retention trade-off, LoRA and DoRA define the strongest operating region, and no nonzero load-balancing coefficient Pareto-dominates the zero baseline; redesigning MoE2-LoRA to update native expert weights improves four upstream metrics by 2.4-17.9 points with 17% fewer trainable parameters.
papers.why_en: Gives empirically grounded design guidance (what to adapt, at what granularity, with which method) for cheaply fine-tuning MoE LLMs, plus a reusable comparison methodology.

papers.title: ReAnchor: Reusing Rejected Verifier States for Diffusion Drafting
papers.abstract: Block diffusion drafters accelerate speculative decoding by generating multiple draft tokens in a single forward pass. However, each pass produces only a fixed-length block from a single target-generated anchor, limiting how far the draft can extend. Meanwhile, target verification computes hidden states even at positions beyond the first rejection, but these states are typically discarded rather than reused. We propose ReAnchor, a training-free method that reanchors a pretrained drafter at shifted positions using discarded verifier states to generate parallel draft blocks. These blocks improve predictions within the original block and extend coverage beyond its endpoint. At sampling temperature of T=0, ReAnchor achieves its largest average gains on Gemma 4-12B, improving acceptance length by 19.4% and decoding speed by 17.9% across eight benchmarks. Averaged equally over four target models and eight benchmarks, it improves acceptance length by 15.2% and decoding speed by 13.4% with pretrained DFlash drafters.
papers.ja_title: 投機的デコーディングを速くする: 検証側が捨てていた『不合格』の内部状態を再利用
papers.summary: ブロック拡散ドラフター(複数の下書きトークンを 1 回の計算でまとめて作る手法)を使った投機的デコーディング(speculative decoding、下書きを作って本体モデルが検証する高速化手法)は、1 回のアンカー(基準点)から固定長の下書きしか作れない。一方、本体モデルの検証は不合格になった先の位置まで内部状態(hidden states)を計算しているのに、それは普通捨てられている。ReAnchor は学習なしで、その捨てられた内部状態を使って下書き生成の基準点をずらし、並行して追加の下書きブロックを作ることで、温度 0 の設定で Gemma 4-12B では受理される下書きの長さを 19.4%、デコード速度を 17.9% 改善した(8 ベンチマーク平均)。
papers.why: 既存の投機的デコーディングの仕組みの中で捨てられていた計算結果を無駄なく使い回す発想で、学習や追加計算なしにサービングの速度を上げられる。
papers.summary_en: Block diffusion drafters accelerate speculative decoding by producing multiple draft tokens per forward pass, but each pass is limited to a fixed-length block anchored at one target-generated token, while hidden states the target computes beyond the first rejection point are normally discarded. ReAnchor is a training-free method that reuses those discarded verifier states to reanchor the drafter at shifted positions and generate parallel draft blocks. At temperature T=0, it gives its largest average gains on Gemma 4-12B -- 19.4% longer acceptance length and 17.9% faster decoding across eight benchmarks -- and 15.2%/13.4% averaged over four target models with pretrained DFlash drafters.
papers.why_en: Reusing verifier compute that speculative decoding pipelines normally throw away is a free, training-free latency win applicable to existing serving stacks.

papers.title: WhatIf-Bench: Benchmarking Intervention-Aware Time Series Forecasting
papers.abstract: Recent time series foundation models (TSFMs) can consume covariates in-context, extending zero-shot forecasting to problems driven by external factors. This enables scenario analysis: forecasting how a target responds to events that set covariates to chosen future values. Whether they can do this reliably is an open question. We introduce WhatIf-Bench, a benchmark measuring how well forecasters use covariates to forecast a target's response to future events. WhatIf-Bench is semi-synthetic: time series come from mechanistic simulators of data centers, power grids, road traffic, and water networks, with controlled covariate-target relationships grounded in each system. Each task presents a history of events intervening on covariates, then asks to forecast a future event that either replays seen values (Replay) or sets them to unseen ones (Novel). Varying the number of covariates, historical events, and event length yields 37,665 tasks. Evaluating TSFMs, frontier LLMs, and simple regression baselines, we find the LLMs reach the highest skill (improvement over a naive baseline), ahead of the best TSFMs. Every model forecasts well on Replay futures (48 to 85% skill) but drops to -7 to 50% on Novel futures, with the regression baselines falling the most. Skill on Novel futures also falls as events set more covariates jointly. More historical events raise skill on Novel futures across the board, but large differences remain. WhatIf-Bench reveals generalization to Novel futures as the core challenge, and offers a testbed toward arbitrary scenario analysis.

papers.title: A Type System for Communication-Safe Hardware Design
papers.abstract: Hardware components communicate through clock-cycle-sensitive protocols. Hardware Description Languages (HDLs), however, provide limited support for expressing these protocols or for checking that independently developed components agree on them. When components disagree, the composed design can perform unsynchronized exchanges or stop making progress. We call these failures communication-safety violations. Communication safety is thus a global property, determined by interactions between components. This makes it difficult to check modularly. This paper presents Pact, a typed extension of Anvil for modular verification of communication safety in synchronous hardware. Pact types describe message-passing, control-flow, and clock-cycle behaviour. Each component is checked against its type. Compatible types guarantee that the components compose into a communication-safe system. Pact also supports incremental design. It can check a subsystem before the rest of the system exists. The check produces a summary type that captures the communication behaviour left for future compositions. To reduce annotation burden, Pact infers types by abstracting payload values while preserving communication, timing, control, and fairness. These inferred types are optimal for the checker: whenever some checker-accepted types can prove compatibility, the inferred types can prove it as well. Type inference and type checking are decidable, and compatibility is decided by a sound and complete algorithm. We implement Pact by extending the Anvil compiler and evaluate it along five dimensions: detecting communication errors in incremental design, expressiveness on ten clock-cycle-accurate translations of open-source hardware IPs, compatibility-checking time, generated hardware overhead, and annotation burden. Pact expresses realistic protocols and verifies all ten benchmarks in reasonable time.

papers.title: VaDar: Implicit Goal Conditioning via Value Disaggregation
papers.abstract: Long-horizon tasks are important for modern AI and robotics, yet pose a challenge for reinforcement learning. Historically, a popular approach has been to decompose a task into subgoals, and learn a subgoal-conditioned policy to execute each subtask in sequence. We introduce an alternative called Value Disaggregation (VaDar), which trains a single subgoal-independent policy to maximize a linear combination of per-subgoal critic values. Because subgoal information is needed only at training-time, VaDar removes the need for possibly costly or cumbersome subgoal-selection during policy deployment. Moreover, through careful experiments, we show that VaDar (1) is always competitive with, and frequently outperforms, natural baselines like goal-conditioning and (2) succeeds on tasks with non-sequential goal structure and multiple optimization objectives. In particular, VaDar is the first algorithm to solve challenging, long-horizon tasks in the RoboCasa suite, even when starting from a policy pretrained from behavior cloning with near-zero initial task success. Taken together, VaDar's successes suggest that subgoal information benefits actor-critic reinforcement learning by enhancing the efficacy of critic learning, whereas policy goal-conditioning is often unnecessary.

papers.title: Parallel Language Models via Variational Decoding
papers.abstract: Autoregressive language models emit one token per forward pass. This causes high inference latency, in particular as models are scaled up for quality. In this paper, we introduce Parallel Language Models (PLMs), which generate mutually consistent tokens in one forward pass by routing dependencies through latent auxiliary variables. PLMs are trained using a variational bound that reduces to an autoregressive loss plus a parallel decoding loss. Empirically, PLMs are on a faster and better Pareto frontier than autoregressive and discrete diffusion baselines. Pretrained PLMs achieve near-autoregressive pretraining loss on model scales of 80M to 3B parameters, and speedup follows a power law in model size. When post-trained, our 1.3B model matches or exceeds an identically trained autoregressive model on math, coding, and instruction-following benchmarks, speeding up inference $2.3\text{-}5.7\times$. Together, we show that parallel generation can be trained from a single training objective at autoregressive quality. We will make our code available at https://github.com/mandt-lab/plm.
papers.ja_title: 並列言語モデル(PLM) - 潜在変数で複数トークンを一度に生成
papers.summary: 自己回帰的な言語モデルは 1 回の計算で 1 トークンしか出せず、モデルを大きくするほど生成が遅くなるという困りごとがある。この研究は潜在的な補助変数を介してトークン間の依存関係をやり取りする並列言語モデル(PLM)を提案し、1 回の計算で互いに整合した複数トークンを生成できるようにした。80M から 3B パラメータの規模で事前学習の損失を自己回帰モデルとほぼ同じ水準に保ちながら、1.3B モデルは数学・コーディング・指示追従のベンチマークで自己回帰モデルと同等以上の性能を保ち、推論を 2.3〜5.7 倍高速化した。
papers.why: 自己回帰の品質を保ったまま推論を大幅に高速化できる学習目的を 1 つに統一して示した点が、推論高速化を狙うサービング基盤の設計者に参考になる。
papers.summary_en: Autoregressive language models emit one token per forward pass, causing high inference latency that worsens as models scale. The authors introduce Parallel Language Models (PLMs), trained with a variational bound that reduces to an autoregressive loss plus a parallel decoding loss, routing token dependencies through latent auxiliary variables so multiple mutually consistent tokens can be generated in one forward pass. PLMs sit on a faster and better Pareto frontier than autoregressive and diffusion baselines, reach near-autoregressive pretraining loss from 80M to 3B parameters, and a post-trained 1.3B model matches or exceeds an identically trained autoregressive model on math, coding and instruction-following while speeding up inference 2.3-5.7x.
papers.why_en: It shows that near-autoregressive quality and large inference speedups can come from a single unified training objective, which matters for anyone designing fast serving stacks.

papers.title: recAMPLIFY: Large-Scale Pretraining of Recursive Protein Language Models
papers.abstract: Protein language models (pLMs) are powerful tools for protein annotation and mutation-effect prediction, but progress has largely depended on scaling model size and data, making them expensive and prone to memorization. Test-time scaling offers a complementary path, but methods developed for autoregressive LLMs do not transfer directly: masked encoders lack a generation loop, and amino acids do not verbalize in a reasoning language. Instead, we adapt recursive pretraining to masked pLMs, where a weight-tied Transformer core refines residue-aligned hidden states over an adjustable number of cycles. We instantiate this recipe as recAMPLIFY, a pLM with 155M unique parameters trained on the same 2T tokens as AMPLIFY-350M. Despite 56% fewer parameters, it improves CASP contact recovery and three out of four supervised tasks, notably raising fold accuracy by 22.5%. Because optimal depth for recAMPLIFY varies across tasks and assays, we then introduce Gated Mixture Recurrence (GMR), a framework that decodes each protein from a probability-weighted mixture of hidden states visited during recursion. GMR employs a learned residual gate at scalar, low-rank, or per-dimension resolution to control how much of each cycle's proposed update is accepted into the state. This unifies halting and gating into a single adaptive computation objective while recovering PonderNet-style halting as a special case without gates. Layered on top of recAMPLIFY, GMR further reduces expected layer depth by up to 37%, although the accuracy trade-off varies by task. Mechanistic analyses show that residual gating controls recurrence stability beyond the trained depth and that halt depth tracks biological properties.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング

papers.title: TokenGate: Adapting LLMs for Fast and Memory-Efficient Prefill with Learned Token Pruning
papers.abstract: Expert human readers process large inputs (e.g., code repositories and long documents) by skimming to closely read only what matters. On the other hand, language models process all input tokens through each model layer, resulting in significant processing costs for long-context inputs. We introduce TokenGate, a small, drop-in component that extends existing trained models to enable end-to-end learnable token pruning over long-context inputs for fast and memory-efficient prefill. To enable end-to-end learning despite the non-differentiable top-K operator for token pruning, we introduce token-gated attention, a mechanism inspired by Mixture-of-Experts that re-weights attention logits using token importance scores. Across diverse tasks, TokenGate achieves $1.4$-$11.3\times$ faster time-to-first token (TTFT) and $1.5$-$3.4\times$ lower peak memory at no accuracy degradation for prefill in transformers. Compared to the best-performing prior methods for token-pruning, TokenGate gives up to $6.4\times$ faster prefill and $2\times$ lower peak memory. TokenGate natively extends both standard transformers (e.g., Qwen3) and hybrid-attention models (e.g., Qwen3.5) with simple lightweight adaptation comparable to standard parameter-efficient fine-tuning. We make our code available at: https://github.com/tokengate-models/TokenGate.
papers.ja_title: TokenGate - 学習で選ぶトークン刈り込みで長文脈の prefill を高速化
papers.summary: 長い入力(コードリポジトリや長文書など)を扱う言語モデルは、すべてのトークンを毎層処理するため計算コストが大きいという困りごとがある。TokenGate は既存の学習済みモデルに追加できる小さな部品で、トークンの重要度でアテンションの重みを再調整する token-gated attention という仕組みにより、微分できない上位 K 個選択の操作を回避してトークン刈り込みを end-to-end で学習する。多様なタスクで prefill の初回トークン生成時間(TTFT)を 1.4〜11.3 倍、ピークメモリを 1.5〜3.4 倍改善し、精度の劣化なしに、既存最良のトークン刈り込み手法と比べても最大 6.4 倍速い prefill と半分のピークメモリを達成した。
papers.why: 通常のトランスフォーマーとハイブリッドアテンションモデルの両方に軽量な追加学習だけで適用できるため、長文脈 serving のコスト削減策として基盤設計者がすぐ検討できる。
papers.summary_en: Language models process every input token through every layer, making long-context inputs such as code repositories or long documents costly to prefill. TokenGate is a small, drop-in component that adds token-gated attention, inspired by Mixture-of-Experts, to re-weight attention logits by learned token importance, enabling end-to-end learnable token pruning despite the non-differentiable top-K operator. Across diverse tasks it achieves 1.4-11.3x faster time-to-first-token and 1.5-3.4x lower peak memory with no accuracy degradation, and up to 6.4x faster prefill and 2x lower peak memory than the best prior token-pruning methods, extending both standard transformers (Qwen3) and hybrid-attention models (Qwen3.5) via lightweight adaptation.
papers.why_en: Because it bolts onto existing standard and hybrid-attention models with lightweight fine-tuning, it is a practical lever for infra builders trying to cut long-context prefill cost.

papers.title: Simulation Priors for Rapid Adaptation in Model-Based RL for Autonomous Racing
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning enables learning high-performance control policies, but its reliance on extensive interaction limits deployment on physical systems where data collection is costly, and failures are unsafe. We introduce Prior-Informed Adaptation (PIA), an offline-to-online model-based RL framework that uses structured simulation priors for rapid adaptation. PIA pretrains a world model on heterogeneous low- and high-fidelity simulated trajectories, then adapts it with limited target-domain interaction using uncertainty-regularized planning. Rather than requiring an accurate simulator for policy transfer, PIA treats simulated trajectories as biased priors whose residual mismatch is corrected during online adaptation. We evaluate PIA in autonomous racing using high-fidelity simulation and on a real full-size autonomous race car. In simulation, PIA adapts faster across track and surface shifts than strong baselines, achieving lower lap times and fewer failures. On hardware, PIA achieves reliable few-shot adaptation with less than one hour of on-vehicle interaction.

papers.title: LG-Bench: A Graph-Structured Evaluation Benchmark for Life Sciences
papers.abstract: Traditional evaluation benchmarks reduce inherently interconnected scientific knowledge in life sciences into flat lists of questions, disregarding the underlying topological structure of the knowledge. We introduce, the first graph-structured benchmark for life sciences, featuring over 10,000 high-quality multiple-choice questions across medicine, biology, and chemistry. Our approach constructs a weighted evaluation graph using bidirectional matching and semantic similarity algorithms, where nodes represent questions and edge weights capture their semantic relationships. Leveraging this graph topology, we design two novel evaluation metrics. The Global Coherence Score (GCS) measures a model's consistency within semantically related neighborhoods, while Knowledge Balance Score (KBS) analyzes how model errors are distributed across the graph to reveal conceptual blind spots. LG-Bench facilitates fine-grained comparison of LLMs by surfacing differences in conceptual coherence and patterns of knowledge organization across models. Our framework shifts the evaluation paradigm from flat accuracy metrics to structure-aware analysis, offering a new lens for diagnosing and improving LLM performance in the life sciences domain.
topics: 集団通信・ネットワーク

papers.title: Competing Learning in Hybrid Architectures
papers.abstract: Many modern language models have adopted hybrid architectures that incorporate both linear-time recurrence and softmax attention. Modern recurrence layers provide a highly expressive mixing mechanism while ensuring high throughput by compressing contextual information into a fixed-size state, but underperform softmax attention in contextual information retrieval. In this paper, we reveal a Competing Learning phenomenon where different kinds of mixers compete to learn the same function, and when any layer learns a function, it suppresses the corresponding learning signal for other layers. Layer attribution analysis reveals that under typical data distributions, modern recurrence learns retrieval functions faster than softmax attention, causing attention to fail to learn retrieval in most cases. Stopping weight updates in recurrence in the middle of training helps attention learn retrieval. Based on these results, we propose a staged training procedure for pre-training hybrid architectures on natural language. Empirical results on models up to 1B parameters show that our method results in substantial improvement in language modeling loss, common-sense reasoning, as well as a wide range of retrieval-related tasks across different context lengths.
papers.ja_title: 競合学習 - ハイブリッドアーキテクチャで線形再帰がアテンションの学習を妨げる現象
papers.summary: 線形時間の再帰(recurrence)層と softmax アテンションを組み合わせたハイブリッドなモデルでは、再帰層の方が検索(retrieval)に関する機能を速く学んでしまい、その分アテンション層が同じ機能を学ぶための学習信号が抑えられてしまう「競合学習」という現象が起きることを示した。学習の途中で再帰層の重み更新を止めるとアテンション層が検索を学べるようになることを確認し、この知見に基づいて段階的な事前学習の手順を提案した。最大 1B パラメータのモデルで、言語モデリングの損失・常識推論・さまざまな文脈長での検索系タスクが大きく改善した。
papers.why: 既存のハイブリッドアーキテクチャの事前学習が実は層同士の学習信号を奪い合っていたことを示し、段階的学習という具体的な改善策まで提示した点が、ハイブリッドモデルの事前学習パイプラインを設計する人に直結する。
papers.summary_en: In hybrid architectures that combine linear-time recurrence layers with softmax attention, the authors reveal a "Competing Learning" phenomenon: modern recurrence learns retrieval functions faster than softmax attention under typical data distributions, which suppresses attention's own learning signal for the same function, so attention mostly fails to learn retrieval. Stopping weight updates in the recurrence layers partway through training lets attention learn retrieval instead, motivating a staged pretraining procedure for hybrid architectures. On models up to 1B parameters, this staged procedure yields substantial improvements in language modeling loss, common-sense reasoning, and retrieval-related tasks across context lengths.
papers.why_en: It diagnoses a concrete failure mode in how hybrid attention-recurrence models are pretrained today and ships a staged-training fix, which is directly actionable for anyone building hybrid-architecture pretraining pipelines.

papers.title: Text-to-Image Generative Modeling Without Language Pretraining
papers.abstract: Modern text-to-image (T2I) systems use internet-scale language pretraining for text-conditioned image generation. We ask whether language pretraining is necessary for strong T2I generation. We introduce Halcyon, a family of early-fusion multimodal autoregressive models pretrained entirely from scratch on GPIC, a dataset of 100M image-text pairs. Halcyon-0.52B outperforms LlamaGen-XL/8 (48.0 vs. 63.3 gFD) with 18.2$\times$ less pretraining compute. Further, Halcyon-1.6B outperforms JiT-T2I-XXL/8++ (35.3 vs. 41.0 gFD) with 275$\times$ less pretraining compute. Controlled experiments show that text-only pretraining does not improve T2I generation. Halcyon also learns image captioning by replacing caption dropout with I2T supervision, maintaining competitive T2I generation quality under the same pretraining budget. We show that strong T2I systems can be trained from scratch without internet-scale language pretraining. Code and models are available at https://cs.stanford.edu/~keshik/halcyon
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング

papers.title: Beyond Policy Discrepancy: Capability-Aware Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract: Multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) integrates domain specialists into a shared student, but determining how strongly each teacher should supervise remains challenging. Existing discrepancy-based allocation can assign strong supervision even when the student already matches or exceeds the teacher's task performance, since behavioral mismatch does not necessarily imply a remaining capability deficit. We propose Capability-Aware Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation (CA-MOPD), which combines specialist merging with capability-guided allocation to account for what the student has already learned. CA-MOPD first merges reinforcement-learning specialists into a strong student initialization, then uses verifier-estimated teacher--student capability gaps to adjust domain-level distillation strength. Supervision decreases as capability gaps close and increases when estimated student capability regresses, while dense token-level guidance remains provided by the teachers. Across six benchmarks spanning mathematics, code generation, and instruction following, CA-MOPD achieves an average score of 32.22, outperforming naive MOPD, Open-MOPD, and the merged initialization by 0.86, 0.83, and 0.74 points, respectively. Controlled comparisons further support the benefits of merged initialization and capability-gap guidance under matched training budgets.
papers.ja_title: CA-MOPD - 生徒の実力に応じて教師ごとの指導の強さを変える多教師オンポリシー蒸留
papers.summary: 複数の専門分野の教師モデルを 1 つの生徒モデルに蒸留する多教師オンポリシー蒸留(MOPD)では、各教師にどれだけ強く教わらせるかの決め方が課題で、教師と生徒の行動の違いだけに基づく既存の割り当てでは、生徒がすでに教師と同等以上の実力を持つ場面でも強く教え続けてしまう。CA-MOPD は強化学習で育てた専門家モデルたちを統合した生徒の初期状態を作ったうえで、検証器(verifier)で推定した教師と生徒の実力差に応じて分野ごとの蒸留の強さを調整する(実力差が縮めば指導を弱め、生徒の実力が落ちたと分かれば指導を強める)。数学・コード生成・指示追従など 6 つのベンチマークで平均 32.22 点を達成し、素朴な MOPD より 0.86 点、Open-MOPD より 0.83 点、専門家統合だけの初期化より 0.74 点それぞれ上回った。
papers.why: 教師の指導強度を固定の行動差でなく実力差の推定で動かすという設計は、複数の RL 専門家モデルを 1 つに集約する後学習パイプラインを作る人にとって、蒸留の効かせ方の具体的な改善案になる。
papers.summary_en: In multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD), deciding how strongly each domain-specialist teacher should supervise a shared student is hard, and existing discrepancy-based allocation keeps supervising strongly even where the student already matches or exceeds the teacher, since behavioral mismatch does not necessarily mean a remaining capability deficit. CA-MOPD first merges reinforcement-learning specialists into a strong student initialization, then uses verifier-estimated teacher-student capability gaps to adjust domain-level distillation strength, decreasing supervision as gaps close and increasing it if estimated student capability regresses. Across six benchmarks spanning math, code generation, and instruction following, CA-MOPD reaches an average score of 32.22, beating naive MOPD, Open-MOPD, and the merged initialization alone by 0.86, 0.83, and 0.74 points respectively.
papers.why_en: Driving teacher supervision strength from an estimated capability gap rather than a fixed behavioral discrepancy is a concrete lever for anyone building post-training pipelines that merge multiple RL specialist models.

papers.title: VS-Flash: Harnessing Vector Search with Computational Memory-Semantic Flash
papers.abstract: As generative AI continues to evolve, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems are driving rapid growth in vector database capacity requirements. As datasets outgrow host DRAM, vector databases rely on MMap-based serving over SSDs to extend capacity. However, high-fan-out ANN searches generate concurrent irregular accesses that contend for host memory and storage resources, degrading bulk throughput and inflating tail latency under mixed workloads. In this paper, we address these challenges through memory-semantic capacity and workload-aware compute placement. VS-Flash exposes flash as a large-capacity memory-semantic space and dynamically selects the execution engine according to runtime query and workload characteristics. It offloads throughput-oriented large-batch queries to a Computational Memory-Semantic Flash (CMS-Flash) device, while executing latency-sensitive small-batch queries on the host CPU. Both paths access the same resident segments, avoiding a separate host-DRAM replica. Across three billion-scale datasets, VS-Flash improves bulk-search throughput over vanilla Milvus by 36.8X on average, with up to a 57.4X improvement. Under mixed workloads, VS-Flash reduces the p99 latency of latency-sensitive requests by up to 24.8X while sustaining device-side bulk search. These results show that VS-Flash delivers scalable vector search beyond host DRAM capacity while jointly improving bulk throughput and small-request tail latency.
papers.ja_title: SSD 上のフラッシュをメモリのように使うベクトル検索サービングの高速化
papers.summary: ベクトル検索データベースは RAG (検索で補強した生成) の普及でデータ量がホストの DRAM を超え、SSD 上の MMap 読み込みに頼ると、大量クエリの混在でスループットが落ち、尾部レイテンシ (p99 など遅い方の応答時間) が悪化する。VS-Flash はフラッシュをメモリのように直接扱える CMS-Flash デバイスを使い、大量バッチのクエリはデバイス側に、少量・低レイテンシのクエリはホスト CPU 側に振り分けて同じデータ領域を共有させる。30 億件規模のデータセットで、素の Milvus に比べ一括検索のスループットを平均 36.8 倍 (最大 57.4 倍) に上げ、混在負荷での p99 レイテンシを最大 24.8 倍短縮した。
papers.why: ホストメモリを超える規模でも、負荷の性質 (大量バッチか低遅延要求か) に応じて実行場所を振り分ける設計は、RAG サービング基盤のスケールアウト設計に直接使える知見。
papers.summary_en: As vector databases outgrow host DRAM, SSD-backed MMap serving under high-fan-out ANN search suffers contention that degrades bulk throughput and inflates tail latency under mixed workloads. VS-Flash exposes flash as a memory-semantic space and routes large-batch queries to a Computational Memory-Semantic Flash (CMS-Flash) device while running latency-sensitive small-batch queries on the host CPU, with both paths sharing the same resident segments. Across three billion-scale datasets, VS-Flash improves bulk-search throughput over vanilla Milvus by 36.8X on average (up to 57.4X) and reduces p99 latency under mixed workloads by up to 24.8X.
papers.why_en: The workload-aware split between a throughput-oriented device path and a latency-oriented host path, without duplicating data, is a directly reusable pattern for scaling RAG serving infrastructure beyond host memory.

papers.title: Discrete Neural Interlingua for Ontology-Agnostic EHR Modeling
papers.abstract: EHR foundation models promise scalable clinical prediction across health systems, yet their deployment is constrained by a tokenization bottleneck. The same clinical concept can appear as different ontology codes, local identifiers, synonyms, or free-text descriptions, which standard EHR tokenizers treat as unrelated symbols. A model trained on MIMIC-III with a closed-vocabulary tokenizer can use only 13% of eICU events. We introduce MEDIATOR, a discrete ontology-agnostic tokenizer that maps any clinical concept expressed as text into a shared vector-quantized codebook, turning EHR harmonization into open-vocabulary tokenization without manual mappings or a fixed vocabulary. Trained with synonym supervision and guided by enriched concept descriptions, code co-occurrence, and relation graphs, MEDIATOR collapses equivalent expressions while organizing distinct concepts in a medically meaningful discrete space. Used as the token interface of an EHR Transformer, MEDIATOR improves mean AUPRC over the strongest prior tokenizer by 4.0 points (8% relative) on 20 MIMIC-III tasks and by 8.6 points (29% relative) in zero-shot transfer to 14 eICU tasks, where it uses all events. The transfer gain combines coverage and representation, as MEDIATOR remains the best tokenizer under identical inputs (+1.0 and +1.9 points on operational and subcohort-mortality tasks). Same-encoder controls show that the text encoder drives in-domain accuracy, while the learned objectives of MEDIATOR drive transfer robustness and entity-linking quality. MEDIATOR also enables transferable attribution across hospitals.

papers.title: Reconstruction-Optimized Expert Pruning for Mixture-of-Experts Language Models
papers.abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models reduce computation through sparse expert activation, but deployment still requires storing a large number of expert parameters. We study post-training expert pruning using task-domain calibration data as a subset-selection problem: given a pretrained MoE layer, select a fixed number of experts that best reconstruct its original output. Exact subset search is combinatorial and becomes intractable for modern MoE models with many experts per layer. We develop OptEP, a scalable continuous relaxation that directly optimizes differentiable expert-selection variables, followed by a lightweight reconstruction-based update of the retained expert weights. Across multiple MoE architectures and tasks spanning mathematical reasoning and code generation, our approach improves over the strongest existing expert-pruning baselines, with absolute accuracy gains of up to 15.05% on Qwen3-30B-A3B, 14.55% on Qwen3-235B-A22B, 11.06% on GLM-4.5-Air, and 16.20% on Mixtral-8x7B. The improvements are particularly pronounced under aggressive pruning, demonstrating that reconstruction-driven expert selection and weight adaptation can preserve substantially more of the original model's performance while reducing the number of retained experts.
papers.ja_title: 出力の再現度で選ぶ MoE の専門家 (エキスパート) 枝刈り
papers.summary: 専門家混合 (MoE) モデルは一部の専門家だけを使うことで計算量を減らせるが、デプロイ時には全ての専門家パラメータを保存する必要があり、容量を圧迫する。OptEP は学習後に、元の MoE 層の出力を最もよく再現できる専門家の組み合わせを、しらみつぶしでなく連続緩和 (選択変数を微分可能にして最適化する手法) で選び、残した専門家の重みも軽く調整し直す。数学的推論とコード生成のタスクで、Qwen3-30B-A3B で最大 15.05 ポイント、Qwen3-235B-A22B で 14.55 ポイント、GLM-4.5-Air で 11.06 ポイント、Mixtral-8x7B で 16.20 ポイントの絶対精度向上を、既存の最強の専門家枝刈り手法に対して達成した。
papers.why: 専門家を減らす枝刈りの選び方を組合せ最適化として連続緩和で解く手法は、MoE モデルのデプロイ容量を減らす際の精度劣化を抑える具体的な改善として使える。
papers.summary_en: MoE models cut computation via sparse expert activation, but deployment still requires storing a large number of expert parameters. OptEP frames post-training expert pruning as subset selection that best reconstructs a pretrained MoE layer's original output, using a scalable continuous relaxation over differentiable expert-selection variables followed by a lightweight reconstruction-based weight update. Across MoE architectures on math reasoning and code generation, it improves over the strongest existing expert-pruning baselines with absolute accuracy gains of up to 15.05% on Qwen3-30B-A3B, 14.55% on Qwen3-235B-A22B, 11.06% on GLM-4.5-Air, and 16.20% on Mixtral-8x7B, with gains most pronounced under aggressive pruning.
papers.why_en: A continuous-relaxation approach to the combinatorial expert-selection problem, paired with reconstruction-based weight adaptation, is a concrete lever for shrinking MoE deployment footprint while limiting accuracy loss.

papers.title: A Combined Streaming FPGA Architecture for Client-Side CKKS Encoding and Encryption
papers.abstract: Homomorphic encryption allows a computing service to process encrypted data, but the client must first encode and encrypt its inputs. Sharing hardware between floating-point encoding and modular encryption reduces area but requires those transform roles to execute at different times. We present a streaming FPGA architecture for CKKS encoding and encryption that computes the shared floating-point encoding transform once and performs the integer transforms for six residue moduli in parallel. Dedicated transform pipelines exchange intermediate results on chip rather than through off-chip memory. DSP Builder generates the transform RTL, and Altera HLS IP Gen compiler compiles the surrounding SYCL pipeline into IP integrated with DMA and control logic in an accelerator functional unit. At polynomial degree N = 8192, the Altera Agilex 7 implementation delivers 5,143 complete ciphertexts per second at 471 MHz. One SEAL-Embedded CPU worker on the same workstation delivers 113 ciphertexts per second for real-valued inputs using all 4,096 slots. Measurements cover prepared-input computation through complete ciphertext construction, including FPGA submission and output delivery.

papers.title: Which Agent's Skill Should Change? Group-Relative Credit Assignment for Evolving Multi-Agent Teams
papers.abstract: Cooperative language-model agents can improve without weight updates by revising reusable skills, but only if a shared team reward is traced to the responsible agent and skill. Existing methods credit the skills present in each trajectory, yet presence is not responsibility: a harmful skill active in successful runs still earns positive credit. We present \textbf{GRSE}, \textbf{G}roup-\textbf{R}elative \textbf{S}kill \textbf{E}volution, which assigns behavioral credit by comparison: inspired by GRPO, it executes each question several times under the same skill libraries and contrasts the executions to credit agent--skill pairs, with structured diagnosis of failures. On HotpotQA and LoCoMo with two open-weight actors, GRSE outperforms MASkills, the closest prior method, on HotpotQA and every LoCoMo category except open-domain, with the largest gains on multi-hop questions ($+6.7$ and $+3.2$ F1). Its gains rest on better-grounded retrieval rather than answers given without evidence, and its learned skills transfer between the multi-hop tasks. GRSE is robust to corrupted libraries: starting from planted harmful skills, it credits every planted skill with the correct sign and recovers the score of a clean library ($+6.3$ points), whereas MASkills misattributes two and falls below its starting point.

papers.title: TEX: Test-Time Scaling Testing Agents via Execution-based Cross-Validation
papers.abstract: Test-case generation is critical but remains challenging for language models. Existing test-time scaling methods either isolate candidates or aggregate traces, which do not scale to long-horizon tasks. We present TEX, a collaborative test-time scaling framework based on execution-driven cross-validation. TEX parallelizes agents to generate tests and patches, cross-executing each test against every patch to form a $K \times K$ feedback matrix. Agents use their matrix slices for refinement, enabling objective validation without verbose trace sharing. On SWT-Bench Verified, TEX achieves 86.4%, establishing a new state-of-the-art and improving +9.0% over single-agent baselines. Moreover, even random selection from TEX outputs (84.4%) surpasses the previous SOTA (84.0%), showing collaborative execution feedback improves solution quality, not just best-case samples. Our results highlight execution-grounded feedback as an effective scaling mechanism for long-horizon agentic tasks.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング

papers.title: Ask to Distill: Learning to Synthesize Data for On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) can succeed with surprisingly few training questions, motivating a view of questions as carriers of distributional knowledge transfer. How can we assess whether a newly generated question is valuable for distillation, and learn to generate better questions---without access to its correct answer? We introduce Ask-to-Distill (\method), a framework that treats synthetic questions as distribution elicitors and optimizes the teacher supervision they expose along student-generated trajectories. A student-initialized synthesizer is optimized using a distributional surrogate for question value, computed from a frozen student--teacher pair without reference answers, correctness rewards, or per-candidate student updates. The reward combines teacher--student disagreement with teacher probability mass on the student's candidate support, together with length and diversity controls. The generated questions are filtered and deduplicated into a prompt-only bank for standard OPD. Across mathematical reasoning, code generation, and agentic tasks, our method improves average performance and teacher-gap recovery over unoptimized student-generated prompts and KL-filtered real questions, while matching or exceeding real-bank OPD in the evaluated settings. Signal analyses further show that optimized questions can elicit denser supervision and more total signal from shorter student responses, supporting elicited distributional supervision as an objective for synthetic distillation data. Our code, data and models are publicly available at https://github.com/GasolSun36/Ask_to_Distill.
papers.ja_title: 正解を見ずに良い問題を作る、オンポリシー蒸留のための問題合成
papers.summary: オンポリシー蒸留 (生成モデル自身の出力列に対して教師モデルから学ぶ蒸留) は少ない問題数でも効果が出ることが知られているが、新しく作った問題が蒸留に役立つかどうかを正解を使わずに判定し、より良い問題を作れるようにする方法はこれまでなかった。Ask-to-Distill は、固定した生徒・教師モデルの組だけから計算できる指標 (教師と生徒の不一致度や、生徒が出しそうな答えに対する教師の確信度など) を使って問題の価値を評価し、それを使って問題合成器を最適化する。数学推論・コード生成・エージェント的タスクで、最適化前の生徒生成プロンプトや既存の KL フィルタ済み実問題集より性能が上回り、実問題集を使ったオンポリシー蒸留と同等以上の結果になった。
papers.why: 正解ラベルなしで「蒸留に効く問題」を見分ける指標を作り、それを合成データ生成の最適化目標に使う発想は、合成データで事後学習する際のデータ選別・合成の設計に使える。
papers.summary_en: On-policy distillation (OPD) can succeed with surprisingly few training questions, but there was no way to assess whether a newly generated question is valuable for distillation, or to learn to generate better ones, without access to the correct answer. Ask-to-Distill optimizes a synthesizer using a distributional surrogate for question value, computed from a frozen student-teacher pair via teacher-student disagreement and teacher probability mass on the student's candidate support, with length and diversity controls, requiring no reference answers or correctness rewards. Across math reasoning, code generation, and agentic tasks, it improves average performance and teacher-gap recovery over unoptimized student-generated prompts and KL-filtered real questions, while matching or exceeding real-bank OPD in the evaluated settings.
papers.why_en: A reference-answer-free signal for how much a synthetic question is worth to distillation, used directly as an optimization target for the question generator, is a reusable design for synthetic post-training data pipelines.

papers.title: Projected Distillation: On Learning to Solve Hard Problems from Close, Correct Targets
papers.abstract: On-policy learning is central to post-training: training on a model's own generations limits distribution shift and helps preserve existing capabilities. On hard problems, however, on-policy RL provides no reward-based learning signal when all attempts fail. On-policy distillation provides next-token supervision from a teacher, but on hard problems, if a rollout goes wrong early, subsequent supervision is conditioned on prefixes that already contain the mistake. Correct behavior can instead come from a gold or teacher solution, but such off-policy targets can differ substantially from the model's generations and, as we show, may erode existing capabilities. We therefore treat on-policyness as a continuum and propose projected distillation, which minimally edits the student's failed attempts into correct targets. The method uses contrastive updates to favor corrections over failed attempts and refreshes these corrections as the student evolves, enabling near-on-policy learning even when all student attempts fail. Theoretically, we prove that the student's learning regret grows with the edit size: it scales linearly with the horizon under minimal correction, as in DAgger, and quadratically under full-answer replacement, as in behavior cloning. Empirically, across two students (Qwen3-8B and OLMo-2-7B) and five domains spanning math, code, science, and tool use, projected distillation gives the highest area under the specialization-retention frontier (best on 8 of 9 cells against GRPO and OPD, and 7 of 9 against SPOT and SODA). Our ablations highlight the importance of online corrections, the contrastive loss, and on-policyness: moving targets farther off-policy steadily worsens the specialization-retention trade-off, with retention falling from 0.916 to 0.744 when minimal corrections are replaced by student-agnostic gold solutions.
papers.ja_title: 失敗した自分の回答を最小限だけ直して学ぶ、オンポリシー蒸留の改良
papers.summary: 事後学習では、モデル自身の出力から学ぶオンポリシー学習がよいとされるが、難しい問題では全ての挑戦が失敗すると強化学習 (RL) は学習信号を全く出せず、教師モデルの正解をそのまま使う蒸留は生徒自身の出力とかけ離れていて既存の能力を損なうことがある。Projected Distillation は、生徒が失敗した回答を正解に変えるための最小限の編集だけを教師から取り、生徒の変化に合わせてその修正を更新し続けることで、どの問題でもオンポリシーに近い学習を可能にする手法で、理論的には編集量が小さいほど学習の後悔 (regret) が horizon に対して線形にしか増えないことを示した (全文置き換えだと horizon の2乗で増える)。数学・コード・科学・ツール使用の5領域で Qwen3-8B と OLMo-2-7B の2つの生徒モデルに対し、専門性と既存能力維持の両立 (9マスのうち8マスで GRPO と OPD に対し最良、7マスで SPOT と SODA に対し最良) で最も良い結果を示し、最小限の修正を生徒に依存しない正解に置き換えると既存能力の維持率が 0.916 から 0.744 まで下がった。
papers.why: 失敗した自己生成を正解に向けて最小限だけ寄せる修正という手段は、難問で RL の信号が消える場面でも既存能力を壊さずに事後学習を続ける具体的な代替手段になる。
papers.summary_en: On-policy learning is central to post-training, but on hard problems on-policy RL gives no learning signal when all attempts fail, while on-policy distillation from a teacher stays conditioned on an already-mistaken prefix once a rollout goes wrong, and fully off-policy teacher/gold targets can erode existing capabilities. Projected distillation minimally edits the student's failed attempts into correct targets with contrastive updates that favor corrections over failed attempts, refreshing the corrections as the student evolves; the authors prove that learning regret scales linearly with horizon under minimal correction (as in DAgger) versus quadratically under full-answer replacement (as in behavior cloning). Across two students (Qwen3-8B and OLMo-2-7B) and five domains, projected distillation gives the best area under the specialization-retention frontier on 8 of 9 cells against GRPO and OPD and 7 of 9 against SPOT and SODA, with retention falling from 0.916 to 0.744 when minimal corrections are replaced by student-agnostic gold solutions.
papers.why_en: Treating on-policyness as a continuum and editing failed rollouts just enough to be correct, rather than replacing them outright, is a concrete fallback for continuing post-training on hard problems where RL gives no signal, without sacrificing retained capability.

papers.title: Can Native Safety Travel? Reusing Safety Pretraining Across Models via On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract: Safety pretraining has emerged as a promising paradigm for embedding safety deeply into a model during pretraining, yielding robustness to subsequent fine-tuning that conventional safety post-training often lacks. We refer to this safety acquired during model pretraining as native safety. Yet native safety is expensive to acquire, confined to the model in which it was pretrained, and often accompanied by lower general utility. In this work, we rethink the practical value of safety-pretrained models and introduce, for the first time, the native safety reuse problem: Can native safety be transferred from a specialized, potentially smaller, safety-pretrained "teacher" to standard-pretrained "students," enabling them to inherit its robustness while preserving their general utility? We show that native safety can "travel" through on-policy distillation. A standard-pretrained student generates responses to safety-pretraining prompts, while a small safety-pretrained teacher supervises the student's token-level predictions along its own generated trajectories; cross-tokenizer alignment further enables transfer across model families. The resulting students exhibit substantially greater safety robustness than their safety-post-trained counterparts while retaining higher general utility than the teacher: subsequent fine-tuning raises the average attack success rate (ASR) of the 1.7B student by only 5.00%, compared with 11.58% for safety post-training, and its average utility of 48.20% far exceeds the aligned teacher's 27.42%. Unlike conventional large-to-small knowledge distillation, our framework enables selective, small-to-large safety transfer: it reuses the robust safety expertise of a smaller pretrained teacher without inheriting its utility limitations. These findings establish native safety as a reusable model property rather than one permanently tied to the originally pretrained model.
papers.ja_title: 安全性を教師から生徒へ移すオンポリシー蒸留
papers.summary: 事前学習で安全性を組み込んだ「素の安全性」モデルは、そのモデル専用になってしまい他のモデルに使い回せないという課題があった。この研究はオンポリシー蒸留(生徒が自分で出した回答を教師が採点して学ぶ手法)を使い、小さな安全教師の知識を標準的な生徒モデルに移す方法を示した。1.7B の生徒モデルでは、追加学習後の攻撃成功率の上昇が従来の安全性後学習の 11.58% に対して 5.00% に抑えられ、汎用性能も教師の 27.42% を大きく超える 48.20% になった。
papers.why: 安全性の後学習より壊れにくい安全性を、モデル間で持ち運べる資産として扱える発想が、大規模モデルの運用で使える。
papers.summary_en: Native safety pretraining is expensive and tied to one model. This work shows native safety can travel via on-policy distillation from a small safety-pretrained teacher to a standard-pretrained student: subsequent fine-tuning raises the average attack success rate of the 1.7B student by only 5.00%, compared with 11.58% for safety post-training, while its average utility of 48.20% far exceeds the aligned teacher's 27.42%.
papers.why_en: Establishes native safety as a reusable, transferable model property rather than one permanently tied to the model it was pretrained in, useful for teams maintaining many model sizes.

papers.title: Meta Expert: Cross-Layer Expert Sharing for Storage- and Retrieval-Efficient MoE
papers.abstract: As model parameters scale up, sparsely activated Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) approaches have become essential for model scaling. However, mainstream models currently adopt hierarchical architectures, where experts in different layers, although topologically independent, exhibit substantial similarity and redundancy in their stored content. Compared to the hierarchically arranged \textbf{Local Expert} in existing mainstream models, we hypothesize that inter-layer shared \textbf{Meta Expert} hold greater potential. To this end, we conduct a multi-dimensional empirical comparison between Local and Meta Experts, and find that models incorporating Meta Experts exhibit lower parameter redundancy, together with lower cross-entropy loss and higher downstream task accuracy. With the activated quantity and the expert granularity held fixed, \textbf{our model matches the performance of Vanilla MoE using only 70--80\% of the experts}, substantially improving the model's scaling potential. Beyond removing inter-layer redundancy among experts and improving information storage efficiency, our theoretical analysis further shows that, compared with Local Experts, Meta Experts provide hidden states with more flexible residual pathways, thereby improving information retrieval efficiency.
papers.ja_title: 層をまたいで専門家(エキスパート)を共有する MoE
papers.summary: MoE(複数の専門家ネットワークを切り替えて使うモデル)は層ごとに別々の専門家を持つのが主流だが、実は層をまたいで似た内容を重複して覚えていることが多い。この研究は層を越えて専門家を共有する「メタ専門家」を導入し、パラメータの重複を減らしつつ損失と下流タスクの精度を改善した。活性化する専門家の数と粒度を揃えた条件で、通常の MoE と同じ性能を専門家数の 70〜80% だけで達成した。
papers.why: 専門家の重複を削るだけでモデルの保存効率と拡張性を上げられるという、MoE 設計の新しい軸を示す。
papers.summary_en: Mainstream hierarchical MoE models keep topologically independent experts per layer that nonetheless show substantial similarity and redundancy. This work introduces inter-layer shared Meta Experts, finding lower parameter redundancy, lower cross-entropy loss, and higher downstream accuracy; with activated quantity and expert granularity held fixed, the model matches Vanilla MoE performance using only 70-80% of the experts.
papers.why_en: Shows a storage- and retrieval-efficiency axis for MoE design orthogonal to routing or sparsity choices.

papers.title: A Radiation-Hardened, Fault-Aware Quantized Neural Network That Self-Heals
papers.abstract: Deep learning (DL) models are increasingly being deployed into radiation-challenging environments in spacecraft, particle accelerators, and, soon, space-based data centers. Instantiated as a learned orchestration of numbers stored in persistent memory, models are susceptible to continual degradation as high-energy particles corrupt data. At inference time, new data passed through the network fundamentally break the off-line assumptions and guarantees of a static model determined during training. To preserve the quality and efficacy of the models, fault tolerance against bit flips is a clear objective. In this work we developed a runtime method for repairing the quantized weights of neural networks (NNs) after bit flips on commodity, commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) hardware, without storing extra replicas. Our work extends the well-established Fault-Aware Training (FAT) paradigm by adding an alignment penalty to concentrate undamaged activations and weights into a low-rank subspace, and we then reconstruct flagged corrupted coordinates from the uncorrupted survivors. We call this method {\it Projection Healing} and apply it to six regression benchmarks on quantized NNs. Holding a FAT checkpoint fixed and toggling only the runtime heal gives a further ${\sim}23\%$ reduction in the native-unit excess integral. Across those datasets the method extends the operational scrub interval by a median of $2.04\times$ at a $+5\%$ RMSE degradation and $1.96\times$ at $+50\%$, compared with $1.62\times$ and $1.07\times$ for classical Single Error Correction, Double Error Detection (SECDED). This introduces a new path towards designing resilient data-driven models, complementing established hardware redundancy, ECC, and FAT-based techniques.

papers.title: From Outcomes to Steps: Reliable Success-Aware Critic Learning for Long-Horizon Language Agents
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning for long-horizon language agents requires identifying whether intermediate actions make eventual task success more or less likely when supervision is available only at trajectory level. The main difficulty is that a critic with aggregate return-prediction accuracy may still fail to resolve the local value differences needed to assign credit to actions, especially under sparse feedback and function approximation. Conventional critics estimate future return, but policy improvement also depends on knowing whether each intermediate decision makes task success more or less likely. We introduce SCALE, an actor-critic framework that augments conventional return estimation with explicit prediction of eventual task success. At each interaction prefix, the critic predicts a return value and a Success Value, defined as the probability that the task will eventually be completed from that prefix. SCALE converts changes in Success Value into multi-step action credit through Success-GAE and modulates its contribution according to the estimated reliability of the predictor, while retaining the token-level PPO objective. Across five agent benchmarks and three model backbones, SCALE improves task performance over the compared RL baselines in most settings, with gains of up to 4.1 percentage points in success rate. Separate critic-learning analyses show that SCALE also improves critic estimation and training stability.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 最終結果だけでなく途中の一手も評価する RL 批評家
papers.summary: 長い手順を踏むエージェントの強化学習では、成功か失敗かは最後にしか分からないため、途中の行動が良かったか悪かったかを判断するのが難しい。この研究は、将来の報酬(リターン)に加えて「このまま進めたら最終的に成功する確率」(Success Value)も予測する批評家 SCALE を提案し、その変化を行動への評価に変換する仕組みを作った。5 つのエージェント向けベンチマークと 3 つのモデルで、成功率が既存手法より最大 4.1 ポイント改善した。
papers.why: 成果だけでなく途中経過の確率推定を学習信号にする設計は、長期タスクの RL 基盤を作る人に直接使える発想。
papers.summary_en: RL for long-horizon language agents must assign credit to intermediate actions from trajectory-level supervision alone. SCALE augments return estimation with an explicit Success Value (the probability the task will eventually be completed from a prefix) and converts its changes into multi-step action credit via Success-GAE; across five agent benchmarks and three model backbones, SCALE improves task performance over RL baselines in most settings, with gains of up to 4.1 percentage points in success rate.
papers.why_en: Gives builders of long-horizon RL post-training pipelines a concrete, measured credit-assignment signal beyond return prediction.

papers.title: Hybrid Momentum Methods for Optimizing Deep Learning Models
papers.abstract: Momentum is central to stochastic optimization in deep learning, including the training of large language models. Classical momentum methods typically rely on a fast exponential moving average (EMA) scheme, which discounts past gradients on a fixed timescale and may underweight older gradients that remain informative. This creates a trade-off between retaining long-term history and adapting to recent changes. We introduce Hybrid Momentum (HyM), which combines a linearly weighted average of past gradients with a geometrically discounted fast momentum. The former assigns weights proportional to the gradients' iteration indices and retains a growing span of history, while the latter emphasizes recent gradients. This hybrid construction is modular and can be combined with adaptive preconditioning and other update transformations. In particular, we propose HyMUON, which applies Newton--Schulz orthogonalization to the hybrid direction. Illustrative examples and controlled experiments demonstrate the benefits of combining gradient information across these two timescales. Across image classification, machine translation, and language modeling, HyM and HyMUON match or improve upon strong baselines. HyMUON improves over Muon on IWSLT14, and in both the 100k- and 600k-step GPT-2 124M OpenWebText regimes. For LLaMA-1.3B pretraining on C4, HyMUON achieves a final validation loss of 2.777, compared with 2.903 for Muon.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 直近と過去の勾配を両方活かすハイブリッド momentum
papers.summary: 深層学習の最適化で使う momentum(勾配の移動平均)は、指数移動平均だと古い勾配の重みが急に小さくなり長期の情報を捨ててしまう。この研究は、反復回数に比例した重みを持つ線形平均と、直近を強く見る指数移動平均を組み合わせた Hybrid Momentum(HyM)を提案し、直交化と組み合わせた HyMUON も作った。LLaMA-1.3B を C4 で事前学習した場合、HyMUON は検証損失 2.777 を達成し、既存の Muon の 2.903 より小さくなった。
papers.why: 既存の最適化手法に後付けできる設計のため、学習効率を上げる手段として既存の学習基盤に組み込みやすい。
papers.summary_en: Classical momentum relies on a fast exponential moving average that may underweight older, still-informative gradients.
