Hybrid Momentum (HyM) combines a linearly weighted average of past gradients with geometrically discounted fast momentum, and HyMUON applies Newton-Schulz orthogonalization to this hybrid direction; for LLaMA-1.3B pretraining on C4, HyMUON achieves a final validation loss of 2.777, compared with 2.903 for Muon.
papers.why_en: A modular addition compatible with adaptive preconditioning, usable as a drop-in optimizer improvement in existing pretraining stacks.

papers.title: E8-QAT: Efficient 2-Bit Quantization-Aware Training with Implicit Lattice Codebooks
papers.abstract: Low-bit quantization reduces the memory footprint of large language models, but preserving accuracy with efficient training remains challenging. Scalar quantization encodes weights independently, while explicit-codebook vector quantization introduces costly search during training. We propose E8-QAT, a 2-bit quantization-aware training framework that uses the $E_8$ lattice as an implicit eight-dimensional codebook. It jointly quantizes weight groups through arithmetic projection without storing or searching an explicit codebook during the training forward pass. A 2-bit core encoding and sparse extension preserve the selected lattice points exactly, adding less than 0.1\% to core index storage. On Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, E8-QAT matches the performance of the full-precision model in terms of the average score across the four tasks. E8-QAT improves over the state-of-the-art baseline by 2.03\% on IFEval and by 1.51\% on LiveCodeBench, under the same data, schedule, and bit width. The 2-bit representation reduces peak memory by 80\% and supports a $4\times$ larger batch. At each representation's largest feasible batch, E8-QAT reaches $1.97\times$ the decoding throughput of BF16.
papers.ja_title: 格子を使った暗黙のコードブックで 2 bit 学習時量子化
papers.summary: 大規模言語モデルを 2 bit まで量子化すると精度が落ちやすく、明示的なコードブック(値の対応表)を使う方式は学習中の探索コストが高かった。この研究は E8 格子という 8 次元の構造を暗黙のコードブックとして使い、探索なしで重みをまとめて量子化する E8-QAT を提案した。Qwen3.6-35B-A3B では、IFEval で既存手法より 2.03%、LiveCodeBench で 1.51% 改善し、ピークメモリを 80% 減らしつつ BF16 の 1.97 倍のデコード速度を達成した。
papers.why: 探索コストなしで 2 bit 品質を出す設計は、量子化カーネルを作る人にそのまま使える手法。
papers.summary_en: Low-bit quantization reduces memory footprint but preserving accuracy with efficient training remains hard; explicit-codebook vector quantization adds costly search during training. E8-QAT uses the E8 lattice as an implicit eight-dimensional codebook, quantizing weight groups via arithmetic projection without storing or searching an explicit codebook; on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B it improves over the state-of-the-art baseline by 2.03% on IFEval and 1.51% on LiveCodeBench, reduces peak memory by 80%, and reaches 1.97x the decoding throughput of BF16.
papers.why_en: A training-time quantization scheme that avoids codebook search cost, directly applicable to low-bit kernel and training pipeline design.

papers.title: RLSplat: Resource-Linear Budget Control for Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting
papers.abstract: Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting (FF3DGS) reconstructs 3D scenes from images in a single forward pass, making it well-suited to applications that must operate within limited resource budgets. To further improve its practicality, recent budget-controllable FF3DGS methods allow the number of Gaussians to be adjusted at inference, so that the output meets a given storage limit or rendering-latency constraint. However, these methods overlook the cost of inference itself: to produce a representation with the target number of Gaussians, they first predict a dense set of Gaussians and then prune or select from it, requiring nearly constant latency and peak memory regardless of the budget. We therefore propose RLSplat, a resource-linear budget-controllable FF3DGS framework whose representation size, inference latency, and peak memory all decrease linearly as the Gaussian budget is reduced. Instead of pruning or selection, RLSplat learns a Gaussian allocation policy that distributes the budget across local scene regions, so that exactly the requested number of Gaussians is generated. These Gaussians are then refined through resource-linear Gaussian decoding, in which each Gaussian attends only to nearby Gaussians found via an efficient hierarchical neighbor search, so that the decoding cost decreases linearly with fewer Gaussians. In zero-shot evaluation, RLSplat outperforms prior budget-controllable methods at every budget, surpassing the strongest baseline even with 4$\times$ fewer Gaussians, while running up to 4.1$\times$ faster with 9.6$\times$ less peak memory at low budgets.

papers.title: On-Policy Transition Distillation
papers.abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) consolidates expert capabilities into a single student by matching teacher and student final-layer distributions on student-generated rollouts. We investigate whether depthwise prediction transitions, the changes in predictions between layers, can provide additional task-relevant supervision. Our diagnostic study finds that stronger teacher--student agreement in intermediate transitions is associated with higher answer correctness within questions, with correct responses exhibiting lower mean transition KL across all measured intermediate layer pairs. These observations motivate On-Policy Transition Distillation (OPTD), which augments final-layer distribution matching by aligning teacher and student layer-to-layer log-probability increments on student-generated rollouts. Evaluations across three backbones and eight benchmarks spanning mathematics, coding, and instruction following show that OPTD achieves the best or tied-best overall performance in both dual- and three-domain distillation. In the three-domain setting, OPTD recovers $\approx 90\%$ of the overall teacher--student capability gap, compared with $\approx 75\%$ for OPD.
papers.ja_title: 層と層の変化も真似させるオンポリシー蒸留
papers.summary: オンポリシー蒸留は最後の層の出力分布だけを教師と生徒で揃える手法だが、この研究は層から層への予測の変化(遷移)にも正解かどうかに関わる情報があることを確かめた。これを踏まえ、層ごとの対数確率の変化も教師に合わせる On-Policy Transition Distillation(OPTD)を提案した。3 つのモデルと 8 つのベンチマークで、OPTD は教師と生徒の性能差の約 90% を取り戻し、従来のオンポリシー蒸留の約 75% を上回った。
papers.why: 最終層だけでなく中間層の変化も蒸留の学習信号に使うという、蒸留手法の設計に直接効く知見。
papers.summary_en: On-policy distillation matches only final-layer teacher-student distributions on student rollouts. A diagnostic study finds stronger teacher-student agreement in intermediate layer-to-layer prediction transitions is associated with higher answer correctness. On-Policy Transition Distillation (OPTD) augments final-layer matching with alignment of layer-to-layer log-probability increments; in a three-domain distillation setting, OPTD recovers approximately 90% of the teacher-student capability gap, compared with approximately 75% for OPD.
papers.why_en: Identifies an additional, measurable supervision signal (intermediate-layer transitions) usable in any on-policy distillation pipeline.

papers.title: KPage: Cross-Block Page Compaction for Hardware-Efficient Sparse Attention
papers.abstract: Sparse attention reduces the computational cost of long-sequence video Transformers, but three-dimensional token layouts often leave selected blocks partially occupied, wasting physical tile capacity. We present KPage, a block-sparse attention scheme that packs valid 16-row K/V pages across logical-block boundaries into large tiles directly during loading, without materializing compacted tensors in high-bandwidth memory. KPage also routes Q blocks between 64x256 and 128x128 tiles to reduce query-side padding. Exact masking and K/V-owned page packing preserve the original sparse graph in forward and backward execution. Across five representative workloads, KPage achieves 1.35x-2.06x bare forward-kernel speedup over NVIDIA Block-Sparse Attention (BSA), with a geometric mean of 1.77x. It is near parity for fully occupied blocks (1.03x) but achieves 2.29x geometric-mean speedup on 3D layouts with partial blocks. KPage reduces physical query-key pair capacity from 334.1G to 177.5G while preserving 160.6G useful interactions. Across eight layouts from open-source SSTA, STA, and VSA systems, KPage achieves 1.13x-4.25x forward and 1.02x-2.71x forward-plus-backward speedup over the strongest exact sparse baselines. With independent Q/K partitions, KPage also achieves 1.49x speedup over the strongest exact sparse baseline and 1.57x over BSA on the SVG2 Wan 14B/720p configuration. After compliance review, we will open-source KPage and submit a pull request to NVIDIA cuDNN Frontend.
papers.ja_title: ブロックをまたいで詰め直すスパースアテンション高速化
papers.summary: 長い動画を扱う Transformer のスパースアテンション(注意を一部のトークンだけに絞る手法)は、選んだブロックが半分しか埋まっていないことが多く、ハードウェアのタイル容量を無駄にしていた。この研究は K/V のページをブロックの境界をまたいで大きなタイルに詰め直す KPage を提案し、メモリに展開せずにロード中に詰め替える。KPage は NVIDIA の Block-Sparse Attention 比で 1.35〜2.06 倍(幾何平均 1.77 倍)速く、部分的に埋まったブロックでは幾何平均 2.29 倍の高速化を達成した。
papers.why: タイル充填率というハードウェア視点の無駄を直接削る設計で、スパースアテンションカーネルを書く人にそのまま参考になる。
papers.summary_en: Sparse attention reduces cost for long-sequence video Transformers, but 3D token layouts often leave selected blocks partially occupied, wasting physical tile capacity. KPage packs valid 16-row K/V pages across logical-block boundaries into large tiles directly during loading, without materializing compacted tensors in HBM; across five workloads it achieves 1.35x-2.06x (geometric mean 1.77x) speedup over NVIDIA Block-Sparse Attention, and 2.29x geometric-mean speedup on 3D layouts with partial blocks.
papers.why_en: A concrete hardware-tiling-efficiency technique for sparse-attention kernel authors, with a stated plan to open-source into cuDNN Frontend.

papers.title: Adaptive Pullback: Reweighting Supervision at Penalty Jumps in On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) supervises student-generated responses using sampled-token student-teacher log-ratios. A positive log-ratio penalizes a token that the student assigns higher probability to than the teacher, but its current value does not distinguish sustained high penalties from abrupt increases along a response. We examine these local changes by comparing consecutive blocks of tokens within the same response. Our diagnostic identifies penalty jumps, abrupt increases in average penalty that persist on held-out tokens. Across these jumps, penalties rise while teacher confidence decreases. We call this pattern penalty-confidence tension. Boundaries into high-penalty blocks do not exhibit comparable confidence changes, showing that local changes provide information beyond the current penalty value. Motivated by this observation, we propose Adaptive Pullback OPD (AP-OPD). At each detected jump, AP-OPD uses the preceding block as a local reference and uniformly scales all supervision coefficients in the following block so that its weighted average penalty matches the preceding block's original mean. This reference determines the scaling factor without an additional strength constant. AP-OPD improves performance on both mathematical reasoning and code generation.
papers.ja_title: 罰則が急に跳ねた箇所だけ重みを調整するオンポリシー蒸留
papers.summary: オンポリシー蒸留では生徒が教師より自信過剰なトークンに罰則(ログ比)を課すが、罰則の値だけでは罰則が長く続いているのか急に跳ねたのかを区別できない。この研究は連続するブロックを比べて「罰則の急な跳ね(ペナルティジャンプ)」を見つけ、その箇所で直前のブロックの平均罰則に合わせて以降の重みを一律に調整する AP-OPD を提案した。数学推論とコード生成の両方で性能が改善した。
papers.why: 罰則の値そのものではなく変化のパターンに着目する診断手法は、蒸留の学習信号を設計する際の観点として使える。
papers.summary_en: On-policy distillation supervises student rollouts using sampled-token student-teacher log-ratios, but a positive log-ratio's value alone does not distinguish sustained high penalties from abrupt increases. The diagnostic identifies penalty jumps where penalties rise while teacher confidence decreases. Adaptive Pullback OPD (AP-OPD) uses the preceding block as a local reference to uniformly scale supervision coefficients in the following block, and improves performance on both mathematical reasoning and code generation.
papers.why_en: Offers a block-local diagnostic pattern (penalty-confidence tension) as a design lens for weighting distillation supervision.

papers.title: Adaptive Replay Refinement: Allocating Test-Time Compute Between Revision and Resampling
papers.abstract: Test-time scaling allocates additional inference compute to refining existing solutions or generating new ones. This raises a fundamental question: Should I keep improving this solution, or stop working on it and try a completely new solution? Existing methods make this decision using fixed refinement schedules, self-verification judgments, or learned controllers, which can waste compute or rely on signals that may be incorrect or require additional training. We introduce Adaptive Replay Refinement (ARR), a training-free method that detects when a stationary revision reaches a fixed point and reallocates the released compute to a new independent sample; replay decoding treats the current solution as a draft and verifies unchanged tokens in parallel, enabling efficient fixed-point detection. Across seven models from five families and seven benchmarks, ARR matches majority voting on three of five mathematical reasoning benchmarks at equal compute, while reducing critical-path serial passes by up to 2.4 times. On MATH500, ARR achieves 84.6% accuracy with only 41% of the serial passes required by majority voting. These results demonstrate that detecting refinement exhaustion enables adaptive reallocation from revision to independent sampling, improving inference efficiency while highlighting the limits of self-revision. Code is available at https://github.com/AhsanBilal7/adaptive_refine.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 直し続けるか新しくやり直すかを自動判定するテスト時計算
papers.summary: テスト時に計算を追加して答えを良くする手法では、今の答えを直し続けるべきか新しい答えを作り直すべきかの判断が難しく、固定スケジュールや追加の学習済み判定器に頼っていた。この研究は、修正がもう変化しなくなった(固定点に達した)ことを検出して、その分の計算を新しい独立したサンプルに回す Adaptive Replay Refinement(ARR)を提案した。MATH500 では、多数決と同等の精度 84.6% を、多数決が必要とする直列実行数のわずか 41% で達成した。
papers.why: 追加の学習やモデル変更なしに推論時の計算配分を改善できる手法で、推論コストを削るサービング側にそのまま使える。
papers.summary_en: Test-time scaling must decide whether to keep refining a solution or try a new one; existing methods use fixed schedules, self-verification, or learned controllers. Adaptive Replay Refinement (ARR) is training-free: it detects when a stationary revision reaches a fixed point and reallocates the released compute to a new independent sample, using replay decoding to verify unchanged tokens in parallel. Across seven models and seven benchmarks, ARR matches majority voting on three of five mathematical reasoning benchmarks at equal compute, reducing critical-path serial passes by up to 2.4 times; on MATH500, ARR achieves 84.6% accuracy with only 41% of the serial passes required by majority voting.
papers.why_en: A training-free inference-time compute allocation method directly usable to cut serving cost for reasoning workloads.

papers.title: Beyond the Point Mass: Acceptance-Derived Weights and Distributional Losses for Speculative Decoding
papers.abstract: In speculative decoding, a lightweight draft model proposes tokens that the target model verifies in parallel, speeding up generation without changing the target distribution. D-PACE (Wu et al., 2026) trains such drafters with a loss that weights each position by its contribution to the expected accepted length. Both its weights and its cross-entropy (CE) loss use only the draft's probability of the recorded target token, treating the target as a point mass. Under rejection sampling, however, a sampled draft token is accepted with probability equal to the overlap of the draft and target distributions, one minus their total variation (TV). We derive D-PAL (Dynamic Position-wise Acceptance Loss) from the exact expected accepted length, using this overlap as the acceptance signal. This yields overlap-based position weights with log acceptance (LA) as the per-position loss, and the objective reduces to D-PACE for a point-mass target. Since the weights are detached, any per-position loss can replace LA in practice. We show that forward KL divergence and Rényi divergence of order 1/2 match or exceed LA, and that Rényi-1/2 provably bounds the true acceptance rate from above and below. Replacing CE with Rényi-1/2 improves acceptance length under both D-PACE's weights and ours. On six benchmarks with a Qwen3-4B target, D-PAL raises mean acceptance length over D-PACE from 4.50 to 4.57 at T=0 and from 4.20 to 4.28 at T=1, and consistently achieves higher throughput at both temperatures.
papers.ja_title: 受理率を直接見積もって投機的デコードの下書きモデルを学習
papers.summary: 投機的デコード(軽いドラフトモデルが候補トークンを提案し、本体モデルが並列に検証して生成を速くする手法)の既存の学習損失 D-PACE は、本体モデルの予測を 1 点の正解とみなして計算していた。この研究は、実際の受理確率がドラフトと本体の分布の重なり(全変動距離の 1 引いたもの)で決まることに基づき、その重なりを直接使う損失 D-PAL を導いた。Qwen3-4B を本体とした 6 つのベンチマークで、平均受理長が D-PACE の 4.50 から 4.57(温度 0)、4.20 から 4.28(温度 1)に伸び、両温度でスループットも上回った。
papers.why: ドラフトモデルの学習損失を理論的に正しい受理確率に合わせ直す手法で、投機的デコードの実装を見直す人に使える。
papers.summary_en: D-PACE trains speculative-decoding drafters with a loss that weights each position by its contribution to expected accepted length, treating the target as a point mass. D-PAL instead uses the exact overlap between draft and target distributions (one minus total variation) as the acceptance signal, with log acceptance as the per-position loss. On six benchmarks with a Qwen3-4B target, D-PAL raises mean acceptance length over D-PACE from 4.50 to 4.57 at T=0 and from 4.20 to 4.28 at T=1, and consistently achieves higher throughput at both temperatures.
papers.why_en: Corrects the theoretical target of drafter training losses in speculative decoding, directly relevant to serving-side latency optimization.

papers.title: Don't Skip the Baseline: A Controlled Comparison of Dynamic Expert Skipping in MoEs
papers.abstract: A growing body of work proposes dynamic expert-skipping methods for Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models that adjust the number of experts activated per token during inference, aiming to preserve model quality while further reducing the number of active parameters. These methods have added calibrated importance scores, inter-expert similarity metrics, or learned per-token allocators in order to identify experts to skip. However, different calibration regimes, different reductions in the effective number of experts, and evaluation suites make comparisons difficult. We classify four representative prior methods into a unified taxonomy and benchmark them against a natural, simple baseline: statically reducing the number of experts $k$ (i.e., same reduced $k$ across all layers and tokens). We provide a fair comparison of these methods at matched expert-compute budget, on two modern MoEs (Gemma4-26B-A4B and Qwen3-30B-A3B) in a text-only setting and a contemporary vision-language model (Qwen3-VL) in a multimodal setting. Surprisingly, we find that the simple baseline is hard to outperform consistently across models, modalities, benchmarks, and calibration settings. The methods we benchmark often underperform the baseline and achieved gains, when present, are minor. We further find that the effective $k$ achieved (or optimized for) in calibration can diverge from the effective $k$ in testing, resulting in over- or under-estimating the compute at inference time. Based on these findings, we recommend a calibration-free per-modality static $k$ reduction and validate this on a held-out model and modality. We further argue that a static control at matched measured compute is the baseline any dynamic skipping method must beat.
papers.ja_title: MoE の専門家スキップ手法は単純な固定削減に勝てていない
papers.summary: MoE モデルでトークンごとに使う専門家の数を動的に減らす手法が多数提案されてきたが、較正方法や削減幅の設定がそれぞれ違い公平な比較が難しかった。この研究は 4 つの代表的な手法を統一した分類にまとめ、全層・全トークンで専門家数 k を同じだけ減らす単純な手法と、計算量を揃えた条件で比較した。驚くべきことに、Gemma4-26B-A4B や Qwen3-30B-A3B など複数モデル・モダリティで単純な手法に動的スキップ手法が一貫して勝てず、改善があっても小さかった。
papers.why: 新手法を評価する際に単純な固定削減を比較対象として必ず置くべきだという、ベンチマーク設計上の教訓を示している。
papers.summary_en: Dynamic expert-skipping methods for MoE models add calibrated importance scores, similarity metrics, or learned allocators, but different calibration regimes and evaluation suites make comparisons hard. This work classifies four representative prior methods into a unified taxonomy and benchmarks them at matched expert-compute budget against a simple static reduction of k. Surprisingly, the simple baseline is hard to outperform consistently across models (Gemma4-26B-A4B, Qwen3-30B-A3B, Qwen3-VL), modalities, benchmarks, and calibration settings, with the benchmarked methods often underperforming it and gains, when present, minor.
papers.why_en: A cautionary benchmarking result: a static baseline matched at compute should be the bar any dynamic MoE method must clear.

review.note: 動的スキップ手法を比べる際、較正条件が違うと優劣が逆転する。計算量を揃えた固定削減という単純な比較対象を必ず置かないと、新手法の優位性が見かけ上のものになる、という評価設計の落とし穴を示す。
review.note_en: Comparisons of dynamic MoE expert-skipping methods flip when calibration regimes differ; without a compute-matched static-k baseline, apparent gains from a new method can be an artifact of the comparison setup.

papers.title: RACE: RoPE-Aligned Attention Compression Based on Query-Key Activation Energies
papers.abstract: Head-dimension compression can reduce the memory required by the key-value (KV) cache, but existing methods often reconstruct full-dimensional representations during inference, adding significant decoding FLOPs overhead. We formalize the design considerations for converting pretrained attention into a natively reduced-dimensional form that reduces both KV-cache storage and attention computation using a calibration set. Specifically, we consider reductions that (1) apply a shared projection to queries and keys so that they remain in a common reduced feature space, (2) derive this projection jointly from query and key activations to better preserve their interaction, and (3) are compatible with the pretrained RoPE transformation. To obtain a reconstruction-free realization of this reduction, we restrict it to coordinate selection and theoretically show that RoPE compatibility then holds if and only if complete rotary pairs are retained. Building on this characterization, we introduce RACE, a post-training method that selects rotary pairs using their joint query-key activation energy. We theoretically show that this criterion minimizes a separable, calibration-dependent upper bound on post-RoPE query-key product approximation error. The resulting reductions are folded into the model weights and require neither runtime reconstruction nor specialized kernels. Across three model families and different compression levels, RACE outperforms structured pruning and remains competitive with reconstruction-based methods on language-modeling, zero-shot, and long-context tasks. At 50% KV-cache retention and 256K context, RACE reduces total inference FLOPs by 47.8%, yielding 1.79x higher throughput, 43.2% lower time-to-first-token (TTFT), and 28.1% lower allocated GPU memory in comparison to an uncompressed model.
papers.ja_title: RoPE と相性の良い次元を選んで KV キャッシュを圧縮する RACE
papers.summary: KV キャッシュ(推論中に使い回す鍵と値の記憶)の次元を削ってメモリを減らす手法は、推論時にフルサイズへ復元する処理が必要でデコードの計算量が増えてしまう問題があった。この研究は RoPE(回転位置埋め込み)と相性が保たれる座標の組だけを、クエリとキーの活性化エネルギーを基準に選ぶ RACE を提案し、復元処理も専用カーネルも不要な圧縮を実現した。KV キャッシュを 50% 残し文脈長 256K の条件で、RACE は推論全体の FLOPs を 47.8% 減らし、スループットを 1.79 倍、初回応答までの時間(TTFT)を 43.2% 短縮した。
papers.why: 復元処理なしでそのまま重みに畳み込める圧縮手法であり、長文脈サービングのメモリとレイテンシを下げる実装にそのまま使える。
papers.summary_en: Head-dimension compression can reduce KV-cache memory, but existing methods often reconstruct full-dimensional representations during inference, adding decoding FLOPs overhead. RACE selects rotary pairs using their joint query-key activation energy, requiring neither runtime reconstruction nor specialized kernels, and folds the reduction into model weights. At 50% KV-cache retention and 256K context, RACE reduces total inference FLOPs by 47.8%, yielding 1.79x higher throughput, 43.2% lower time-to-first-token, and 28.1% lower allocated GPU memory compared with an uncompressed model.
papers.why_en: A reconstruction-free, RoPE-compatible KV-cache compression method directly deployable without new serving kernels.

papers.title: When Copying Is Hard: Copy-Constrained Decoding for Exact Span Reproduction
papers.abstract: Precisely reproducing a target span verbatim within a long context is a fundamental capability test for LLMs: even when the target string is present in context, models often still drift within the span or fail to stop correctly, revealing limitations in source grounding and boundary control. This capability has broad practical relevance. For instance, code generation often requires embedding sensitive strings such as API keys exactly as they appear in context. In this work, we construct a benchmark to test exact span reproduction ability across contracts, scientific literature, code, and random sequences, and find that current models still make surprisingly frequent errors. To address this, we propose CopyGen, a lightweight copy-constrained plugin for frozen LLMs that turns copying from a byproduct of next-token prediction into a controlled process. Our key idea is to decompose copying into three distinct decisions: when to copy, how far to copy, and when to stop. Concretely, CopyGen first determines whether to enter copy mode, then predicts a tentative copy length, and finally verifies the generated span token by token. During verification, we adaptively adjust the logits of copy continuation tokens to incentivize or suppress continuation, and emit only the longest valid prefix. Across three LLM backbones and four benchmark tasks, CopyGen improves average exact match by 35% relative without model finetuning, and integrates seamlessly with SFT to further improve it by 4%, while substantially accelerating generation. These results suggest that reliable exact copying is not something LLMs obtain for free, but a decoding-time control problem that requires explicit modeling. Code is available at https://github.com/mbzuai-nlp/CopyGen.
papers.ja_title: 長い文脈から一字一句を正確に写すためのデコード制御
papers.summary: LLM は、答えとなる文字列が文脈の中に存在していても一字一句そのまま写すのが苦手で、API キーのような機密文字列をコードに埋め込む場面などで誤りが起きやすい。この研究は、いつ写すか・どこまで写すか・いつ止めるかの 3 つの判断に分けて制御する軽量プラグイン CopyGen を提案した。3 つのモデルと 4 つのベンチマークで、追加学習なしに平均の完全一致率が相対 35% 改善し、SFT と組み合わせるとさらに 4% 改善した。
papers.why: 正確なコピーをデコード時の制御問題として扱う発想は、生成の信頼性を上げるデコード手法を考える人に使える。
papers.summary_en: Precisely reproducing a target span verbatim within a long context is a fundamental capability test for LLMs, with broad practical relevance such as embedding sensitive strings like API keys exactly as they appear in context. CopyGen decomposes copying into when to copy, how far to copy, and when to stop, verifying the generated span token by token. Across three LLM backbones and four benchmark tasks, CopyGen improves average exact match by 35% relative without finetuning, and integrates with SFT to further improve it by 4%, while substantially accelerating generation.
papers.why_en: Frames exact copying as a decoding-time control problem rather than a free byproduct of next-token prediction, useful for serving pipelines needing verbatim reproduction.

papers.title: Stratified Sparse Attention: Reducing the Sparse-to-Dense Gap at Extreme Sparsity
papers.abstract: Large Language Model inference over long contexts is increasingly bottlenecked by the cost of attending to a growing Key-Value (KV) cache. Sparse attention reduces this cost by accessing only a fraction of the cache, but existing methods face a trade-off between deterministic retrieval, which captures high-scoring tokens but discards residual attention mass, and sampling, which improves coverage at the cost of higher variance. Hybrid methods combine top-$k$ retrieval with uniform sampling, yet still exhibit a substantial gap from dense attention at aggressive sparsity. We introduce \emph{Stratified Sparse Attention (SSA)}, a unified framework combining deterministic retrieval with score-guided sampling. SSA deterministically attends to high-scoring tokens while sampling the residual using proxy attention scores and correcting for their inclusion probabilities, thereby recovering attention mass beyond the retrieval set. SSA encompasses top-$k$, top-$p$, and hybrid top-$k$+sampling as special cases. Across RULER, LongBench, LOFT, and AIME, and five models ranging from 3B to 27B parameters, SSA consistently improves over the baselines at matched sparsity. On RULER-HARD with Ministral-3-8B, SSA improves accuracy over the strongest practical baseline from 81.8\% to 84.2\% at 32K and from 63.8\% to 69.3\% at 128K under $50\times$ attention sparsity, recovering 94\% and 85\% of dense-attention performance, respectively. With optimized CUDA kernels, SSA achieves up to $2.96\times$ decode speedup over FlashInfer at 1M context, demonstrating that its accuracy gains translate into practical long-context inference acceleration. We open-source our code at https://github.com/skylight-org/SSA-Paper-Code.
papers.ja_title: 確定選択とスコア付きサンプリングを両立させるスパースアテンション
papers.summary: 長文脈の推論では KV キャッシュ全体を見るコストが問題になり、上位トークンだけを確定で選ぶ方式は取りこぼしがあり、サンプリングを混ぜる方式は分散(ばらつき)が増えるという trade-off があった。この研究は、スコアの高いトークンを確定で選びつつ残りをスコアに基づくサンプリングで補い、選ばれる確率の偏りを補正する Stratified Sparse Attention(SSA)を提案した。RULER-HARD で Ministral-3-8B を使い 50 倍のスパース化条件で、文脈長 32K では精度を 81.8% から 84.2% に、128K では 63.8% から 69.3% に改善し、最適化した CUDA カーネルで文脈長 1M において FlashInfer 比 2.96 倍のデコード高速化を達成した。
papers.why: 確定選択とサンプリングの中間を理論的に正しく補正する方法を示し、長文脈サービングのスパースアテンション実装にそのまま使える。
papers.summary_en: LLM inference over long contexts is bottlenecked by KV-cache attention cost; deterministic top-k retrieval discards residual attention mass while sampling increases variance. Stratified Sparse Attention (SSA) deterministically attends to high-scoring tokens while sampling the residual using proxy attention scores, correcting for inclusion probabilities. On RULER-HARD with Ministral-3-8B, SSA improves accuracy over the strongest practical baseline from 81.8% to 84.2% at 32K and from 63.8% to 69.3% at 128K under 50x attention sparsity, and with optimized CUDA kernels achieves up to 2.96x decode speedup over FlashInfer at 1M context.
papers.why_en: Unifies top-k and sampling-based sparse attention under one correctable framework, with measured kernel speedups at extreme sparsity and context length.

papers.title: GraphCast-Mamba: Learning Non-Markovian Corrections for Weather Forecasting
papers.abstract: Unresolved atmospheric processes can introduce history dependence beyond the short input windows used by many weather forecasting models. We introduce GraphCast--Mamba, which augments a frozen, pretrained $1^\circ$ GraphCast backbone with a trainable Mamba correction branch combining graph message passing and Mamba layers. The branch retains a temporal memory state across successive six-hour forecast steps, learning corrections informed by temporal context beyond GraphCast's two-frame input. Training is confined to the correction branch, using ERA5 data from 2015--2021. After 2,500 optimizer updates, including warm-up, the selected model achieves substantial improvements relative to the uncorrected GraphCast backbone. It reduces the GraphCast loss (normalized weighted mean-squared error; MSE) by 14.42% when aggregated over the full ten-day forecast and by 21.66% at day 10 (240 h after forecast initialization). At this final forecast lead time, root-mean-square error (RMSE) decreases by 7.09--14.60% across all 11 evaluated variable groups, spanning temperature, wind, pressure, geopotential, specific humidity, and precipitation. These results demonstrate broad improvements in ten-day weather forecasts through a short correction-training schedule while retaining the pretrained backbone.

papers.title: Beyond 4 bits: Data-Centric Post-training Quantization and Recovery
papers.abstract: Post-training quantization (PTQ) compresses the weights of a trained model with limited compute and data. Down to 4 bits it is near-lossless, but at 2 bits scalar PTQ configurations fall to chance-level accuracy. We study three choices usually treated as implementation details that matter little at 4 bits but decide 2-bit quality: the quantization representation, the calibration data, and the recovery fine-tuning data, across six dense and mixture-of experts models (ranging from $3.8$ to $32$B parameters). Representation is the largest factor and vector codebooks restore usable models where scalar PTQ pipelines collapse. Most of the remaining loss in accuracy is on \emph{generative} tasks, and the amount of performance drop is model-dependent. Furthermore, at a short recovery budget, calibration and recovery data are coupled. The best recovery data depends on the calibration data, so the two must be chosen jointly. The resulting recipe involves a vector codebook representation, a small task-aligned calibration mixture, and an inexpensive codebook-only recovery stage. Including codebooks, it uses about $2.3$ effective bits per weight and retains $89$ to $97\%$ of full-precision question-answering (QA) accuracy where scalar PTQ is at chance, and, including recovery, uses $1.4$ to $30\times$ less compute than the strongest quantization-aware-training (QAT) baseline.
papers.ja_title: 2 bit 量子化の品質を決めるのは較正データと回復データの組み合わせ
papers.summary: 学習後量子化(PTQ)は 4 bit までならほぼ無劣化だが、2 bit まで落とすと従来の素朴な量子化では精度がランダム並みまで落ちる。この研究は、表現方法(ベクトルコードブックか否か)・較正データ・回復用の微調整データという 3 つの選択が 2 bit での品質を左右することを 3.8B から 32B までの 6 モデルで確かめ、較正データと回復データは組み合わせて選ぶ必要があると示した。ベクトルコードブックと少量の回復学習を使う手法は、1 重みあたり約 2.3 bit で質問応答精度の 89〜97% を保ち、最も強い量子化前提学習(QAT)基準より計算量を 1.4〜30 倍少なく済ませた。
papers.why: 4 bit では問題にならない細部の選択が 2 bit では品質を決めるという知見は、低 bit 量子化パイプラインを作る人への実務的な指針になる。
papers.summary_en: Post-training quantization is near-lossless down to 4 bits, but at 2 bits scalar PTQ configurations fall to chance-level accuracy. This work studies three choices (quantization representation, calibration data, recovery fine-tuning data) across six dense and MoE models from 3.8B to 32B parameters, finding representation is the largest factor and that calibration and recovery data must be chosen jointly. The resulting recipe, using a vector codebook and inexpensive codebook-only recovery, uses about 2.3 effective bits per weight and retains 89 to 97% of full-precision QA accuracy where scalar PTQ is at chance, using 1.4 to 30x less compute than the strongest QAT baseline.
papers.why_en: Identifies which implementation details that don't matter at 4 bits become decisive at 2 bits, a practical recipe for low-bit quantization pipelines.

papers.title: The Token-Energy Law of LLM Decode: Active Bytes and Realized Time Account for Joules per Token
papers.abstract: Energy-efficient deployment of large language models requires understanding how model architecture, hardware, and serving settings shape energy per generated token. We introduce the Token-Energy Law, a compact, interpretable model of GPU-board energy per output token for dense, full-history decoding. It relates token energy to two core dimensions: active bytes and realized decode time. Active bytes describe logical byte demand per output, separating dense weights shared within a decode iteration from private key--value (KV) histories read and updated for each request. Realized decode time is the elapsed decode duration divided by the number of output tokens produced. We combine the two byte coordinates and time in a common affine form, with coefficients calibrated for each model and hardware/runtime configuration. This formulation explains how batching amortizes shared-weight work, longer attended histories increase private KV demand, and throughput determines the time-associated cost per output. Our experiments cover three models under BF16 decoding on NVIDIA Hopper and Blackwell GPUs, including two-GPU tensor parallelism on Hopper. Using fixed coefficients and observed decode time, held-out condition-mean energy estimates differ from measurements by at most 3.73%.
papers.ja_title: 出力 1 トークンあたりの消費電力を説明する Token-Energy Law
papers.summary: LLM を省エネに動かすには、モデルの構造やハードウェア、サービングの設定がトークンあたりの消費電力をどう決めるかを理解する必要がある。この研究は、デコード 1 回の反復で全リクエストが共有する重みの読み込み量(active bytes)と、実際にかかったデコード時間という 2 つの量から、GPU のボード消費電力をシンプルな式で表す Token-Energy Law を作った。NVIDIA の Hopper と Blackwell の GPU 上で 3 つのモデルを使った実験では、固定した係数と観測したデコード時間から見積もったエネルギーが実測値と最大 3.73% しか違わなかった。
papers.why: バッチングや文脈長が電力に与える影響を数式で説明できるため、サービング設定を電力コストの観点から最適化する際の指標に使える。
papers.summary_en: Energy-efficient LLM deployment requires understanding how architecture, hardware, and serving settings shape energy per generated token. The Token-Energy Law relates token energy to active bytes (shared weight versus private KV-history demand) and realized decode time, calibrated per model and hardware/runtime configuration. Across three models under BF16 decoding on NVIDIA Hopper and Blackwell GPUs, including two-GPU tensor parallelism on Hopper, held-out condition-mean energy estimates differ from measurements by at most 3.73%.
papers.why_en: A compact, interpretable energy model that explains how batching and KV-history length drive joules per output token, usable for serving-cost optimization.

papers.title: Cache Engineering for Agents
papers.abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) agents can handle increasingly complex tasks, navigating long trajectories of observations and actions. As these trajectories grow, key-value (KV) cache I/O and storage become the dominant cost. Trajectories can also exceed the LLM's maximum context length, requiring control over active cache growth. Prior work uses context engineering to reduce cache size by trimming or summarizing history. However, modifying the trajectory prefix invalidates subsequent cached states and triggers costly re-prefilling of retained context. Task accuracy can also suffer when too little context is retained to limit re-prefill costs. We propose cache engineering as a new scheme. It allows agents to directly control their active KV cache without modifying the trajectory or re-prefilling retained context. Specifically, agents can proactively use drop to exclude selected cache from future attention and repos to adjust retained keys' position encodings. We formalize these cache operations and identify history dependence as a serving challenge: identical token sequences can yield different cache states under different cache operation sequences, making prefix matching insufficient for correct cache reuse. Thus, we co-design the AKV serving engine. It provides a stateless interface compatible with existing serving APIs, while internally managing stateful cache reuse, eviction, and restoration. Experiments show that a tool-response rolling-drop cache policy improves average benchmark scores by 1.7 points and reduces average cost by 27.7%, compared with conventional threshold-triggered summarization. With AKV, it achieves up to 1.2x the output throughput and a 1.5x speedup in P95 request latency. Recursive self-improvement of cache policies further reduces cost by 7.1% over expert design. Our code is at https://github.com/thu-nics/AKV.
papers.ja_title: KV キャッシュを直接操作するエージェント向け Cache Engineering
papers.summary: 長い手順を踏む LLM エージェントでは KV キャッシュ(推論の記憶)の入出力と保存がコストの中心になり、文脈を縮めると以降のキャッシュが無効になって再計算が必要になるという問題があった。この研究は、履歴そのものは変えずに有効なキャッシュを直接操作する「cache engineering」を提案し、キャッシュの一部を今後の注意から除外する drop や、残したキーの位置情報を調整する repos という操作を定義した。これを支える AKV というサービングエンジンでは、ツール応答を順に間引くキャッシュ方針でベンチマーク平均点が 1.7 ポイント改善しコストを 27.7% 削減、出力スループットは最大 1.2 倍、P95 のレイテンシは 1.5 倍速くなった。
papers.why: 文脈の書き換えではなくキャッシュそのものの操作でコストを下げる発想は、エージェント向けサービングエンジンの設計にそのまま使える。
papers.summary_en: As agent trajectories grow, KV cache I/O and storage become the dominant cost, and modifying the trajectory prefix to shrink context invalidates subsequent cached states and triggers costly re-prefilling. Cache engineering lets agents directly control their active KV cache via drop (exclude cache from future attention) and repos (adjust retained keys' position encodings), co-designed with the AKV serving engine for stateful cache reuse behind a stateless interface. A tool-response rolling-drop cache policy improves average benchmark scores by 1.7 points and reduces average cost by 27.7% compared with threshold-triggered summarization, and with AKV achieves up to 1.2x output throughput and a 1.5x speedup in P95 request latency.
papers.why_en: Introduces direct, stateful KV-cache operations as an alternative to context rewriting, with a concrete serving-engine design for cache reuse under history dependence.

papers.title: Sage-A1.5: From Long-Horizon Execution to Scientific Exploration with Capability Composition
papers.abstract: In this report, we introduce Sage-A1.5, a 35B Mixture-of-Experts agentic model that builds on A1 to advance long-horizon problem solving through adaptive capability composition. Compared with A1, Sage-A1.5 learns not only to solve individual tasks, but also to organize work and revise its approach during execution. Sage-A1.5 highlights three improvements: agentic orchestration, verification, and open scientific discovery. First, agentic orchestration extends single-agent execution through task delegation and parallel collaboration among subagents with isolated contexts, enabling complex tasks to be decomposed and addressed concurrently and supporting efficient execution while reducing interference across concurrent subagents. Second, agentic verification strengthens long-horizon reliability through progress checking, evidence validation, and reflective strategy revision, allowing the agent to recognize unproductive search paths and pursue alternative approaches. Third, open scientific discovery extends agentic capabilities beyond answering predefined questions to conducting exploratory research, connecting scientific inquiry with interactive analysis and inspectable research artifacts. We showcase these capabilities through complicated agentic tasks and multidisciplinary scientific applications. Besides, we hope Sage-A1.5 provides the community with an accessible foundation for open scientific discovery, offering a practical path from long-horizon task execution to collaborative, verifiable, and inspectable scientific exploration.

papers.title: Capable Teacher, Myopic Scorer: Reward-Free Teacher Repair for Agentic On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract: Agentic on-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student agent on its own trajectories while a teacher scores every token. A natural explanation of where it goes wrong is compounding error: the student's mistakes carry its trajectories beyond the region where the teacher is reliable, so recent methods keep training inside that region, through episode-length curricula, teacher-guided turns, prefix replay, or teacher intervention where the two disagree. We show this explanation is incomplete. From the states where the student departs most from the teacher, the teacher's own takeovers still finish the task, yet the student trained on its token scores keeps running out of turns. We attribute this to the myopia of next-token scoring. The teacher rates each token without seeing where the episode ends, so its scores let through the safe, delaying moves that outcome-based RL would punish with zero reward, a penalty agentic OPD lacks. We call this difference between what the teacher does and what it scores the rollout-scorer gap. We propose Rollout-to-Scorer Distillation (R2S), which repairs the scorer before distillation by mining high-disagreement states from the untrained student, running teacher takeovers from them, keeping the states where enough takeovers pass a reward-free check such as consensus or an LLM judge, and fine-tuning the teacher to give its takeover-informed scores on every assistant token from the divergence turn onward, without the takeover in context. The repaired teacher is frozen as the sole scorer for standard OPD, requiring no task reward during repair or training. Across three environments, two teachers and four students, R2S outperforms three state-of-the-art agentic-OPD methods in all twelve teacher-student-environment cells, by 12.8 success points on average over the best of them in each cell. Project page: https://tree-shu-zhao.github.io/r2s/.
papers.ja_title: 教師の採点基準を直してからエージェントに蒸留する R2S
papers.summary: エージェント向けオンポリシー蒸留では教師が生徒の軌跡の全トークンを採点するが、生徒が教師の得意な範囲から外れた状態になっても教師が実際に代わりに操作(takeover)すればタスクを完了できることが分かった。この研究は、教師のトークン採点が「このまま続けると最終的にどうなるか」を見ずに点を付けてしまう近視眼(myopia)が原因だと見抜き、生徒がよくズレる状態を集めて教師に実際に操作させ、その結果を踏まえて教師の採点自体を修正する R2S を提案した。3 つの環境・2 つの教師・4 つの生徒の全 12 通りの組み合わせで、R2S は既存の最良のエージェント蒸留手法を平均 12.8 ポイント上回った。
papers.why: 教師モデルそのものの採点基準を直すという視点は、エージェント向け蒸留やオンポリシー蒸留のパイプラインを作る人に直接効く。
papers.summary_en: Agentic on-policy distillation trains a student on its own trajectories while a teacher scores every token, and recent methods try to keep training inside the region where the teacher is reliable. This work shows that explanation is incomplete: from states where the student departs most from the teacher, the teacher's own takeovers still finish the task, yet the student trained on its token scores keeps running out of turns, attributed to the myopia of next-token scoring. Rollout-to-Scorer Distillation (R2S) repairs the scorer before distillation by mining high-disagreement states, running teacher takeovers from them, and fine-tuning the teacher to give takeover-informed scores; across three environments, two teachers, and four students, R2S outperforms three state-of-the-art agentic-OPD methods in all twelve teacher-student-environment cells, by 12.8 success points on average over the best of them in each cell.
papers.why_en: Identifies scorer myopia as the actual failure mode behind agentic on-policy distillation and fixes the teacher itself rather than the training curriculum, a reusable idea for agent RL pipelines.

papers.title: Weight Placement Is Not Enough: Synchronization in Multi-Node CPU Decoding of Ternary LLMs
papers.abstract: Ternary LLMs read only a few gigabytes per decoded token, yet on dual-socket servers with four NUMA nodes the fastest ternary runtime we found uses less than half of the memory bandwidth. Placing each weight on the node of the thread that reads it is necessary but not enough: in a decode engine with node-local weights that reuses ik_llama's kernels, threads on two generations of Xeon servers still spend 20-48% of each token waiting at synchronization points. Per-thread barrier traces show that most of the wait is for the slowest threads of each node; the barriers' own latency (microseconds each, but up to 12% of the token for the smallest model) and serial per-node work are smaller parts. On identical kernels, a Megatron-style column split beats a row-owned split without cross-node reductions in every configuration we measured, and isolating the number of barriers shows that most of its gain comes from its threads waiting less for each other and for their node leaders, and only a minority from having fewer barriers. Where decoding is DRAM-bound, the resulting engine is 1.5-2.1x faster than ik_llama with all cores and 1.5-1.9x faster than ik_llama at its fastest thread count (3.2x and 2.8x for a small model that runs from the L3 cache), at the same accuracy and with less energy per token.
papers.ja_title: 重みの配置だけでは足りない、3 値 LLM の複数ノード CPU デコード同期
papers.summary: 3 値(ternary)LLM はトークンごとに読むメモリが数 GB と少ないのに、4 つの NUMA ノードを持つ 2 ソケットサーバー上で見つけた最速のランタイムでもメモリ帯域の半分以下しか使えていなかった。この研究は、各スレッドが読む重みをそのスレッドのノードに置くだけでは足りず、2 世代の Xeon サーバーでスレッドがトークン処理時間の 20〜48% をバリア(同期待ち)で浪費していることを、スレッドごとのバリア記録で突き止めた。同じカーネルで比べると Megatron 流の列分割がノード間の集約をしない行分割より常に速く、DRAM 帯域が制約となる条件では、全コアを使った場合に ik_llama 比 1.5〜2.1 倍、最速スレッド数で比べても 1.5〜1.9 倍速くなった(小さいモデルでは 3.2 倍・2.8 倍)。
papers.why: ボトルネックをバリア待ちの時間という実測値まで分解した診断の立て方が、マルチノード CPU/GPU 推論の性能調査にそのまま応用できる。
papers.summary_en: Ternary LLMs read only a few gigabytes per decoded token, yet on dual-socket, four-NUMA-node servers the fastest ternary runtime found uses less than half of the memory bandwidth. Placing each weight on the node of the thread that reads it is necessary but not enough: per-thread barrier traces on two generations of Xeon servers show threads still spend 20-48% of each token waiting at synchronization points, mostly for the slowest threads of each node. A Megatron-style column split beats a row-owned split without cross-node reductions in every configuration measured; where decoding is DRAM-bound, the resulting engine is 1.5-2.1x faster than ik_llama with all cores and 1.5-1.9x faster at its fastest thread count (3.2x and 2.8x for a small model that runs from the L3 cache), at the same accuracy and with less energy per token.
papers.why_en: Decomposing a CPU-decode bottleneck down to measured barrier-wait time rather than stopping at a design-level explanation is a reusable investigative pattern for multi-node inference performance work.

review.note: 性能の原因を『重みの配置』という設計判断だけで説明せず、スレッドごとのバリア待ち時間を実測して浪費の正体(遅いスレッドを待つ時間)を突き止めている。性能劣化の原因を分解して実測で特定する調査の型として参考になる。
review.note_en: Rather than attributing performance to a single design choice (weight placement), the work measures per-thread barrier wait time directly, isolating most of the waste to waiting for the slowest threads per node, a model for decomposing and measuring the actual cause of a performance gap.

papers.title: Learning Adaptable Dexterous Skills via Hybrid Dexterous Mimicking
papers.abstract: Dexterous multi-finger hands hold promise to unlock diverse skills like functional grasps, in-hand reorientation, and dynamic handover that the human-designed world assumes, yet existing learning recipes force a trade-off. Goal-reaching reinforcement learning generalizes to arbitrary object poses but, lacking any human prior, converges to unnatural and unreliable finger strategies; motion tracking reproduces human-like behavior from a single clip but cannot deviate from it. We present AdaDex, a goal-conditioned RL framework that turns a single hand-object trajectory of a few seconds---from mocap data or HOI reconstruction from in-the-wild RGB(D) video---into an adaptable dexterous skill. At the core of AdaDex is Hybrid Dexterous Mimicking: a shared policy is trained on two populations of massively parallel environments: motion tracking environments trained with dense motion tracking objective, which instill the human prior from human motion; and generalization environments with noised initial states and goals and a sparse object-success reward, which force the skill to work far off the reference. From seconds of human motion per skill, the resulting policies can learn diverse adaptable dexterous skills, such as functional grasping, object reposing, in-hand reorientation with finger gaiting, and dynamic behaviors like throw-and-catch. Our method outperforms baselines in terms of generalization and functionality, and we demonstrate transfer across simulators and to the real world. Project page: https://yuxuank.com/AdaDex/.

blogs.title: Day-0 Support for Flint on vLLM
blogs.excerpt: vLLM supports both Flint checkpoints (40B total, 2.5B active) from day 0, decoding a single request at about 500 tokens/s on one GPU.
blogs.ja_title: 40B の MoE モデル Flint に vLLM が発売日対応
blogs.summary: vLLM は Recursive の新モデル Flint を公開初日からサポートした。Flint は合計 400 億パラメータのうち 1 トークンあたり 25 億パラメータしか使わない MoE で、ほとんどの層がスライディングウィンドウ注意、26.2 万トークンまでの文脈に対応する。NVFP4 と BF16 の 2 種類のチェックポイントが用意され、GB200 1 枚で 10 万トークンの文脈を使っても 1 リクエストあたり 500 トークン/秒ほどで復号できるという。
blogs.why: 長い文脈でも KV キャッシュを持つ層を 49 層中 14 層に絞るなど、スライディングウィンドウと全文脈注意を混ぜたアーキテクチャが、どのように 1 GPU での高速な単一リクエスト復号につながるかの実例になる。
blogs.summary_en: vLLM supports Recursive's Flint from day 0: both its NVFP4 and BF16 checkpoints run on a single GPU, and a single request decodes at about 500 tokens/s on one GB200, even with 100K tokens of context. Flint is a 40B-parameter MoE that activates only about 2.5B parameters per token, with sliding-window attention in most layers and a 262K-token context; only 14 of its 49 layers keep KV for the whole sequence.
blogs.why_en: It is a concrete example of how mixing sliding-window and full-context attention, so that only a small fraction of layers carry the full-sequence KV cache, translates into fast single-GPU, single-request decoding.

blogs.title: Announcing Humming: Fast, Flexible Kernels for Quantized Inference
blogs.excerpt: Introducing Humming, a quantized inference kernel library from Ant Group and the vLLM community, with broad GPU and quantization support, dense and MoE performance results, and vLLM integration.
blogs.ja_title: Ant Group と vLLM が公開した量化推論カーネル Humming
blogs.summary: MoE モデルは 1 トークンごとに使う専門家は一部でも、全部の重みを置いておく必要があるため、メモリ容量と帯域が制約になりやすい (例として DeepSeek-V3 は総パラメータ 6710 億のうち 1 トークンで使うのは 370 億)。Ant Group と vLLM コミュニティは、重みと活性化の量化形式 (WnA16、W8A8、W4A8、W4A4 など) を 1 つの統一表現で扱える汎用カーネルライブラリ Humming を公開した。Turing 以降の NVIDIA GPU や T-Head Zhenwu 810E のような CUDA 互換デバイスに対応し、既存の vLLM Marlin・FlashInfer・DeepGEMM と比べて多くの代表的な処理で大きく性能が上回るという。
blogs.why: 量化の形式 (ビット幅、スケーリング粒度、対称/非対称) が組み合わせ爆発する中で、dense と MoE の両方を 1 つのアーキテクチャで統一的にチューニング・JIT コンパイルする設計が、カーネル実装を増やし続けたい人への参考になる。
blogs.summary_en: As models and inference workloads grow, memory capacity, memory bandwidth, and compute costs increasingly constrain deployment, especially for MoE models where the full set of weights still needs to be stored even though each token activates only a subset of experts (DeepSeek-V3 has 671B total parameters with 37B activated per token). Ant Group and the vLLM community are open-sourcing Humming, a general-purpose, high-performance kernel library for quantized inference that supports NVIDIA GPU architectures from Turing onward plus CUDA-compatible devices such as T-Head's Zhenwu 810E, and a unified architecture covering diverse weight/activation format combinations for dense and MoE workloads. The post states Humming significantly outperforms existing implementations from vLLM Marlin, FlashInfer, and DeepGEMM across many representative workloads.
blogs.why_en: It shows a unified architecture for tuning and JIT-compiling across the exploding combination space of quantization formats (bit widths, scaling granularity, symmetric/asymmetric) for both dense and MoE kernels, useful for anyone maintaining a growing set of quantized kernels.

blogs.title: Introducing vLLM TorchTPU
blogs.excerpt: vllm-torchtpu is a new vLLM backend for Google Cloud TPUs built on TorchTPU, with Pallas kernels, multi-host parallelism, KV cache offloading, and disaggregated serving.
blogs.ja_title: vLLM に TPU 向けバックエンド vLLM TorchTPU が登場
blogs.summary: vLLM TorchTPU は Google の TorchTPU 基盤の上に作られた新しい vLLM バックエンドで、vLLM に既にあるモデル実装をそのまま使って Google Cloud TPU 上で動かせる。スケジューラ・ワーカー・KV キャッシュ管理・API サーバーは GPU 版と変わらず、TPU 固有の処理は attention や MoE、量化行列積のための JAX/Pallas カーネルとして下に差し込まれる仕組みになっている。各 TPU デバイスは `torch.compile(backend="tpu")` で XLA にコンパイルされ、デバイス間通信は `torch.distributed` を通る。
blogs.why: GPU と TPU で同じスケジューラ・KV キャッシュ管理・API サーバーを使い回しつつ、ハードウェア固有の部分だけをプラグインに切り出す設計が、複数ハードウェアに対応する推論基盤を作る人の参考になる。
blogs.summary_en: vLLM TorchTPU is a new out-of-tree vLLM platform plugin built on Google's TorchTPU stack that lets most models already defined in vLLM run on Cloud TPUs without changes to the model code; the scheduler, workers, KV cache manager, and API server are all unmodified upstream vLLM, while TPU-specific work sits in a set of JAX/Pallas kernels for attention, MoE, and quantized matmul. Each TPU device runs models through torch.compile(backend="tpu"), which lowers to XLA, with communication between devices going through torch.distributed.
blogs.why_en: It demonstrates reusing the same scheduler, KV cache manager, and API server across GPU and TPU while isolating hardware-specific work in a plugin, a useful pattern for anyone building a multi-hardware serving stack.

blogs.title: Achieving near-zero-downtime scaling in Elastic Expert Parallelism
blogs.excerpt: How asynchronous preparation and NIXL EP enabled near-zero-downtime Elastic EP scaling in vLLM.
blogs.ja_title: vLLM の Elastic EP、GPU を増減してもほぼ無停止に
blogs.summary: これまで vLLM で MoE サービングの GPU 数を変えるにはエンジンの再起動が必要で、DeepSeek V4 Pro を 16 枚から 20 枚に増やす際には 197 秒間サービスが止まっていた。前回の Elastic EP では再起動は避けられたものの、新しいワーカーの初期化や通信グループの準備、重みの読み込み、カーネルのウォームアップで、16→20 枚で 100 秒、20→16 枚で 56 秒の停止が残っていた。今回は非同期の準備作業と NIXL EP を組み合わせることで、この停止時間を 16→20 枚で 0.82 秒、20→16 枚で 1.96 秒まで短縮したという。
blogs.why: 通信グループの準備・重み転送・ウォームアップをバックグラウンドで進め、切り替えの瞬間だけ短いコミットにする 2 段構成が、サービス停止を最小化したい大規模 MoE サービングの実例になる。
blogs.summary_en: Restarting vLLM to scale DeepSeek V4 Pro from 16 to 20 GB200 GPUs previously stopped serving for 197 seconds, and even the earlier Elastic EP approach (data-parallel attention with expert-parallel MoE, scaled without a full restart) still paused serving for 100 seconds scaling up and 56 seconds scaling down while new workers were initialized and warmed up. By combining asynchronous preparation with NIXL EP, the authors reduced that downtime to 0.82 seconds scaling from 16 to 20 GPUs and 1.96 seconds scaling back to 16, allowing them to scale up and down with almost no impact on serving performance.
blogs.why_en: It is a concrete example of splitting reconfiguration into background preparation plus a short commit, minimizing downtime for large-scale MoE serving that needs to scale GPU count while live.

blogs.title: Hyper Optimizing Kimi K3 in vLLM: Moving Fast and Responsibly
blogs.excerpt: How agent-assisted CuTe DSL optimizations accelerate Kimi K3 decode on NVIDIA GB300, and how scoped changes, correctness tests, and reproducible benchmarks help ship them responsibly.
blogs.ja_title: エージェントが書いた Kimi K3 用 CuTe DSL カーネルを安全に出す仕組み
blogs.summary: NVIDIA のチームは Kimi K3 の復号を高速化するため、GB300 上で attention・MoE・通信をまとめて扱う CuTe DSL の復号パスをコーディングエージェントに書かせ、GB300 16 枚・バッチ 1 で DSpark 併用時に 840 トークン/秒以上、複数の設定でデコードスループットが 1.5〜2 倍、AgentX ワークロードでは P90 の対話性が最大 1.8 倍になったという。一方で、エージェントが書いた最適化コードは人がレビューできる速さを上回っており、1 行ずつ理解する従来のレビューでは追いつかないという課題も述べている。そこで変更をモデルのコードの中に閉じ込め、対応ハードウェアと必須機能を明確にスコープを決め、正しさと性能を系統的に検証する、という進め方を提案している。
blogs.why: エージェントが生成した性能最適化コードを、どこまで人がレビューし、どこを自動検証に任せるかという切り分け方を具体的に示しており、AI 生成コードのレビュー体制を考える人への観点になる。
blogs.summary_en: Using agent-assisted development to build a unified CuTe DSL decode path on NVIDIA GB300 covering attention, MoE, and communication, the team reports Kimi K3 decode of over 840 tokens/s at batch 1 on 16 GB300 GPUs with DSpark, 1.5–2x higher decode throughput in several tested configurations, and up to 1.8x higher P90 interactivity on the AgentX workload. The post also states that agent-optimized inference code is now outpacing the team's manual review and maintenance workflow, so it proposes isolating changes within the model's code, bounding the supported hardware and workloads while preserving must-have features, and validating correctness and performance systematically.
blogs.why_en: It directly addresses how to split review responsibility between humans and automated checks for agent-generated performance-optimization code, a useful lens for anyone designing a review process for AI-written code.

blogs.title: Scaling Kimi K3 on AMD Instinct MI355X: Matching NVIDIA HGX B300 Throughput per GPU on AgentX
blogs.excerpt: Inside the Kimi K3 optimization effort: understanding the bottlenecks and the decisions that made inference faster
blogs.ja_title: AMD MI355X で Kimi K3 を最適化し NVIDIA B300 と同等以上の性能に
blogs.summary: AMD と Embedded LLM は、AgentX ワークロードにおいて 8 枚の AMD Instinct MI355X で Kimi K3 を vLLM サービングした結果、ユーザー体感速度 (interactivity) P90 で 50 トークン/秒/ユーザーという条件のとき、NVIDIA HGX B300 より GPU 1 枚あたりの総トークン数で 24.4% 多く、ベンチマークの保有コストモデルでは 1 ドルあたりのトークン数で 87.4% 多いという結果を報告した。会話状態のキャッシュ共有や重複 MoE 計算の削減、MLA/KDA の AMD AITER アセンブリ実装、投機的デコードのトークン数選択など、複数の最適化を組み合わせている。
blogs.why: キャッシュ共有・MoE の重複排除・メモリコピー削減・アテンション実装・投機的デコードという複数のレイヤーを横断した最適化を 1 つずつ説明しており、他ハードウェアへの移植時に見るべき最適化の一覧として使える。
blogs.summary_en: On AgentX, an eight-GPU AMD Instinct MI355X system serving Kimi K3 with vLLM delivers 24.4% more total tokens per second per GPU than NVIDIA HGX B300 at 50 tokens/s/user P90 interactivity, and under the benchmark's ownership-cost model it delivers 87.4% more tokens per dollar. The post walks through optimizations across cache reuse for conversation state, removing duplicate MoE work across GPUs, fusing memory operations, AMD AITER assembly for faster MLA decoding, parallelizing KDA prefill and speculative verification, and choosing how many tokens to draft.
blogs.why_en: It walks through optimizations spanning cache reuse, MoE deduplication, memory-copy reduction, attention implementation, and speculative decoding as a layered checklist, useful when porting similar optimizations to other hardware.

blogs.title: Serving Reflection Beam on vLLM from Day 0
blogs.excerpt: vLLM supports Reflection's Beam-1.0 (501B total, 23B active) from day 0, with agent-driven optimization that cut decode latency 2.71× and DFlash2 speculative decoding with adaptive verification.
blogs.ja_title: 501B の MoE モデル Beam、vLLM 発売日対応でエージェントが自動最適化
blogs.summary: vLLM は Reflection の Beam (総パラメータ 5010 億、1 トークンあたり有効 230 億) を公開初日から対応させ、NVIDIA Blackwell 向けに最適化した。コーディングエージェントが自律的にモデルを最適化し、最初の実装に比べてバッチ 1 の復号を 2.71 倍、prefill を 1.87 倍速くしたという。さらに Beam 専用の投機的デコード DFlash2 では、1 リクエストで TP8 のとき 708 トークン/秒、受理長 3.7 を達成し、各ステップで検証すべきドラフトトークン数を適応的に決める仕組みで高並列時のスループットがさらに 10% 増える。
blogs.why: エージェントによる自律最適化と、ステップごとに検証量を変える適応的投機的デコードという 2 つの手法を、新モデルの発売日対応という短い期間でどう組み合わせたかの実例になる。
blogs.summary_en: vLLM supports Reflection's Beam, a 501B-parameter MoE with 23B active parameters per token, from day 0 and optimizes it on NVIDIA Blackwell; coding agents optimized the model autonomously, making batch-1 decode 2.71x faster and prefill 1.87x faster than the first implementation. With Beam's DFlash2 drafter, a single request reaches 708 tokens/s on TP8 with an acceptance length of 3.7, and adaptive verification, which decides each step how many draft tokens are worth verifying, adds 10% more throughput at high concurrency.
blogs.why_en: It is a concrete example of combining autonomous agent-driven optimization with step-by-step adaptive speculative decoding under the short timeline of day-0 support for a new model.

blogs.title: Day 0 support for Muse Spark Open on vLLM
blogs.excerpt: Day-0 vLLM support for Muse Spark Open: 816B MoE, 1M context, multimodal inputs, DSpark speculative decoding, NVIDIA and AMD serving, initial TPU support, and LoRA RL.
blogs.ja_title: Meta の 816B MoE Muse Spark Open に vLLM が発売日対応
blogs.summary: vLLM は Meta Superintelligence Labs と協力し、総パラメータ 8160 億・1 トークンあたり有効 420 億、文脈 100 万トークンの MoE モデル Muse Spark Open を公開初日からサポートした。BF16 と NVFP4 のチェックポイントに加え AMD が MXFP4 版の重みを公開しており、NVIDIA と AMD の両方でテンソル並列・パイプライン並列を使え、NVIDIA では Expert Parallel・Tensor+Expert Parallel・Data+Expert Parallel・PD 分離サービングにも対応する。投機的デコード用のドラフトモデル DSpark も訓練されており、CUDA と ROCm の両方で動作を確認している。
blogs.why: 1 つのモデルを NVIDIA・AMD・TPU という複数ハードウェアと複数の並列化方式 (TP/PP/EP/TEP/DEP/PD 分離) にまとめて対応させる際の、量化形式とハードウェアの組み合わせの整理の仕方が参考になる。
blogs.summary_en: vLLM worked with Meta Superintelligence Labs to bring Muse Spark Open, an 816B-parameter MoE with 42B active parameters per token and a 1M-token context window, to vLLM on day 0. Meta released BF16 and NVFP4 checkpoints and AMD released MXFP4 weights; the model supports Tensor and Pipeline Parallelism on both NVIDIA and AMD, plus EP, TEP, DEP and PD disaggregation on NVIDIA, with initial TPU support also available, and a trained DSpark draft model that accelerates performance on both CUDA and ROCm.
blogs.why_en: It shows how one model's quantization formats are organized across multiple hardware vendors and parallelism schemes (TP/PP/EP/TEP/DEP/PD disaggregation) for day-0 support.

blogs.title: Announcing Day 0 Support for NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL on vLLM
blogs.excerpt: Run NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL on vLLM for multimodal agent workflows with image, document, and video understanding, OpenAI-compatible serving, and multi-token prediction.
blogs.ja_title: Mamba とトランスフォーマーを混ぜた NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL
blogs.summary: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL は、総パラメータ 1200 億・1 トークンあたり有効 120 億の MoE アーキテクチャに、Mamba とトランスフォーマーを混ぜたハイブリッド構造を採用し、テキスト・画像・文書・動画の理解とツール利用を 1 つのモデルにまとめている。マルチトークン予測と NVFP4 量化を組み合わせることで生成効率を上げ、同時に動かせる長文脈セッションの数を増やせるよう設計されているという。vLLM による高速な推論サービングと、投機的デコードによる長時間エージェントワークフローの高速化にも対応する。
blogs.why: 常時稼働のマルチモーダルエージェント向けに、Mamba/トランスフォーマーのハイブリッド構造とマルチトークン予測、低精度量化をどう組み合わせて設計するかの具体例になる。
blogs.summary_en: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is built on a 120-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts architecture with 12 billion active parameters, combining reasoning, instruction following, and tool use with text, image, document, and video understanding in one model. A hybrid Mamba-Transformer architecture, multi-token prediction, and NVFP4 quantization are designed to improve generation efficiency and create headroom for more concurrent long-context sessions, and the model is served through vLLM with speculative decoding to accelerate long-running agentic workflows.
blogs.why_en: It is a concrete example of combining a hybrid Mamba-Transformer architecture with multi-token prediction and low-precision quantization for always-on multimodal agent serving.

blogs.title: Elastic Expert Parallelism Scaling in SGLang: Growing a Live MoE Deployment with NIXL
blogs.excerpt: Inference deployments operate under changing load and must adapt their capacity while maintaining throughput and latency targets. For large Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models, the standard options are horizontal scaling, which adds another complete replica, and vertical scaling, which restarts the deployment with a wider expert-parallel topology.
blogs.ja_title: SGLang が NIXL で実現した MoE サービングのその場拡張
blogs.summary: 大規模 MoE モデルのサービングで GPU を増やすには、丸ごと別レプリカを追加する水平スケーリングか、より広い専門家並列 (expert-parallel) 構成でデプロイを再起動する垂直スケーリングのどちらかが一般的だった。SGLang はこれに対し、既に稼働中のデプロイに GPU ランクを追加するだけで済む Elastic EP スケールアップを実装し、例として 20 GPU のデプロイを 24 GPU に増やす際も、実行中のサービスを置き換えずにランクを追加できるようにした。報告された比較では、Elastic EP スケーリングは再起動に比べて最初のリクエストが完了するまでの時間が 5.3〜8.2 倍速かったという。
blogs.why: 障害からの復旧フロー (実行中にメンバーが予期せず変わる) と計画的なスケールアップ (ランクを計画的に増やす) を同じ仕組みの上に乗せる設計が、MoE サービングのオートスケーリングを作る人の参考になる。
blogs.summary_en: For large Mixture-of-Experts models, the standard scaling options are horizontal scaling, which adds a full replica, or vertical scaling, which restarts the deployment with a wider expert-parallel topology. SGLang's Elastic EP scale-up instead lets a deployment add GPUs in fine-grained increments without deploying a full replica or restarting; in the reported comparisons, Elastic EP Scaling reached the first completed request 5.3x-8.2x faster than restart, illustrated by a 20-to-24-GPU example that adds four ranks to a running deployment.
blogs.why_en: It builds planned scale-up on the same mechanism already used for unplanned membership changes during recovery, a useful pattern for anyone building autoscaling for MoE serving.

blogs.title: SGLang-TorchTPU: PyTorch-Native Production Serving on TPUs
blogs.excerpt: Today we are launching SGLang-TorchTPU, a native PyTorch backend that brings SGLang's full serving stack to Google Cloud TPU. SGLang's serving engine and model implementations are built on PyTorch, and with TorchTPU the same codebase serves on both GPUs and TPUs, so you can pick the hardware that best fits each workload and its deployment economics.
blogs.ja_title: SGLang に TPU 向け PyTorch ネイティブサービング SGLang-TorchTPU
blogs.summary: SGLang-TorchTPU は、SGLang のサービングエンジンとモデル実装をそのまま使って Google Cloud TPU 上で動かす、PyTorch ネイティブな新バックエンドである。TPU 固有の処理はプラグインに切り出され、スケジューラや RadixAttention、API サーバーは SGLang 本体のものをそのまま使う。TPU コアごとに TorchTPU 経由で PyTorch プロセスが動き、`torch.compile` で XLA にコンパイルされ、グラフキャプチャの代わりに prefill のトークン数と decode のバッチサイズをバケット単位に固定長化してコンパイル結果を再利用する仕組みになっている。
blogs.why: GPU と同じコードベースを使い回しつつ、TPU 固有の attention/MoE カーネルや形状バケット化だけを差し替える移植パターンが、他ハードウェアへの推論基盤の移植を考える人の参考になる。
blogs.summary_en: SGLang-TorchTPU is a native PyTorch backend that brings SGLang's full serving stack to Google Cloud TPU, built so that the same codebase serves on both GPUs and TPUs; the scheduler, RadixAttention, and API server are SGLang's own, while TPU-specific components stay isolated in the plugin. Each TPU core runs its own PyTorch process through TorchTPU, the model runs under torch.compile and lowers to XLA, and instead of graph capture, the runner pads each forward to a fixed set of token-count buckets for prefill and batch-size buckets for decode, so each bucket compiles once and later steps dispatch to the cached program by shape.
blogs.why_en: It shows a porting pattern of reusing the same serving codebase across GPU and TPU while swapping out only the hardware-specific attention/MoE kernels and shape bucketing, useful for anyone porting a serving stack to new hardware.

blogs.title: SGLang Low-Latency Mode: Kernels and Runtime
blogs.excerpt: Low-latency inference offers many opportunities for optimizations tailored to specific models, hardware and workloads. These optimizations often require extensive kernel fusion and duplicate code across implementations, making them difficult to maintain.
blogs.ja_title: SGLang Low-Latency Mode、NVIDIA と AMD で専用カーネルを追加
blogs.summary: 低遅延な推論にはモデルやハードウェア、ワークロードごとの専用最適化が有効だが、カーネルの融合処理が重複しやすく保守が難しいという課題があった。SGLang はこれをプラグインの仕組みで取り込む Low-Latency Mode を導入し、AgentX のトレース再生で 4 枚の NVIDIA GB300 を使う場合、同時セッション 1 の P90 ユーザー別トークン生成速度が 671.2 トークン/秒から 928.4 トークン/秒 (1.38 倍) に向上した。4 枚の AMD MI355X では、同時セッション 4 のとき 331.6 トークン/秒から 516.0 トークン/秒 (1.56 倍) に向上したという。ウォームアップ済みの CUDA グラフでは、検証用グラフのカーネル数は 1,205 個から 1,189 個とほぼ変わらないのに、1 デコーダ層あたりの中央値レイテンシは 96.8 マイクロ秒から 68.4 マイクロ秒まで下がっている。
blogs.why: カーネル数を大きく減らさずに、依存関係の待ちやカーネル間の重なりを減らすだけでレイテンシを下げられたという測定結果が、低遅延最適化で見るべき指標の例になる。
blogs.summary_en: Low-latency inference offers many opportunities for model-, hardware-, and workload-specific optimizations, but these often require extensive kernel fusion and duplicate code across implementations that is hard to maintain. SGLang's new Low-Latency Mode brings specialized kernels into SGLang through a plugin framework; in AgentX trace replay on four NVIDIA GB300 GPUs, P90 per-user token generation speed increases from 671.2 to 928.4 tokens/s (1.38x) at one concurrent session, and on four AMD MI355X GPUs it increases from 331.6 to 516.0 tokens/s (1.56x) at four concurrent sessions. In warmed CUDA-graph profiles, the plugin reduces the verify graph from 1,205 kernels to 1,189 but cuts the median decoder-layer latency from 96.8 microseconds to 68.4 microseconds.
blogs.why_en: The measurement that latency drops mostly from reducing waits and overlapping dependent work, rather than from cutting the kernel count, is a useful signal for what to look at in low-latency optimization.

blogs.title: SGLang Powers Beam in Production
blogs.excerpt: Reflection’s Beam is a 501B-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 23B active parameters per token, built for software engineering and long-horizon agentic tasks.
blogs.ja_title: SGLang が Reflection の本番 API を支える Beam サービング最適化
blogs.summary: Reflection の Beam は総パラメータ 5010 億・1 トークンあたり有効 230 億のソフトウェア開発・長期エージェント向け MoE モデルで、SGLang が Reflection の本番 API をそのまま支えている。SGLang は BF16・NVFP4・動的 FP8 のチェックポイントに対応し、DFlash2 投機的デコードやハイブリッドアテンション向けのメモリ管理を伴うプレフィックスキャッシュで文脈の再利用を効率化した上で、射影のパッキングや注意機構と残差接続の境界をまたぐ融合、FP32 ルーター用の専用 BF16x3 GEMM、GB300 向け MoE チューニングといったカーネル最適化を加えている。
blogs.why: 本番トラフィックを支える MoE モデルにおいて、量化形式の選択・投機的デコード・キャッシュ再利用・カーネル融合をどのレイヤーで組み合わせているかの実例として参考になる。
blogs.summary_en: Reflection's Beam is a 501B-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 23B active parameters per token, built for software engineering and long-horizon agentic tasks, and SGLang now supports Beam natively and powers Reflection's production API. The post covers BF16, ModelOpt NVFP4, and compressed-tensors dynamic FP8 checkpoint support, DFlash2 speculative decoding, prefix caching with hybrid-attention memory management, and kernel optimizations including projection packing, fusion across attention and residual boundaries, a specialized BF16x3 GEMM for the FP32 router, and GB300 MoE tuning.
blogs.why_en: It is a concrete example of how quantization choice, speculative decoding, cache reuse, and kernel fusion are layered together for an MoE model serving real production traffic.

blogs.title: SGLang and Miles Add Day-0 Support for Muse Spark Open
blogs.excerpt: Muse Spark Open combines a sparse language decoder with visual and audio encoders, bringing multimodal inputs into a shared token-generation pipeline.
blogs.ja_title: SGLang、Meta の MoE モデル Muse Spark Open に Day-0 対応
blogs.summary: Muse Spark Open はテキスト・画像・音声・動画を扱う MoE (専門家混合) モデルで、合計 816 B (ビリオン=10 億) パラメータのうち 1 トークンあたり約 42 B だけを使う。長い文脈 (最大 100 万トークン) を扱うため GQA (グループ化クエリ注意) とスライディングウィンドウ+グローバル注意を組み合わせている。SGLang は NVIDIA B300 GPU 8 基で NVFP4 (4 bit 浮動小数点) 版を動かし、同時実行数 1 では GPU 1 基あたり 14.8 K トークン/秒 (ユーザーあたり 543 トークン/秒)、同時実行数 128 では GPU 1 基あたり 80.3 K トークン/秒 (ユーザーあたり 61 トークン/秒) を達成した。
blogs.why: 大規模 MoE モデルを長文脈かつマルチモーダルで、同時実行数に応じたスループットとレイテンシのトレードオフまで数値で示した実例として、サービング基盤を作る人の参考になる。
blogs.summary_en: Muse Spark Open is an open-weight multimodal MoE model with an 816B-parameter text transformer backbone and about 42B active parameters per token, accepting text, image, video, and audio with a 1M-token context window achieved via GQA combined with sliding-window and global attention. On an OpenHands multi-turn agentic coding replay with the NVFP4 checkpoint on 8 NVIDIA B300 GPUs, SGLang reaches 14.8K total tokens/sec per GPU at 543 tokens/sec per user (p50) at concurrency 1, and 80.3K total tokens/sec per GPU at 61 tokens/sec per user (p50) at concurrency 128.
blogs.why_en: Gives a concrete concurrency-vs-per-user-latency tradeoff, measured end to end on real hardware for a frontier-scale multimodal MoE model, useful for anyone building serving infrastructure for similar models.

blogs.title: SGLang Adds Day-0 Support for NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL
blogs.excerpt: Always-on AI agents must do more than generate text. They need to interpret visual information, reason across long-running tasks, and use tools reliably across documents, applications, and video.
blogs.ja_title: SGLang が NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL にも Day-0 対応
blogs.summary: Nemotron 3.5 Super VL はテキスト・画像・文書・動画を入力しテキストを出すエージェント向けの MoE モデルで、総パラメータ 120 B のうち 1 トークンあたり 12 B だけを使う。C-RADIOv4 の画像エンコーダ、Mamba と Transformer を混ぜたハイブリッド構造、複数トークン同時予測 (MTP)、NVFP4 量子化を組み合わせ、SGLang で連続バッチ処理・プレフィックス再利用・投機的デコードに対応する。1 枚の DGX Spark や RTX PRO 6000 でもローカル実行でき、RTX PRO 6000 では 243.9 トークン/秒を達成した。
blogs.why: Mamba-Transformer ハイブリッドと MTP、NVFP4 を組み合わせたマルチモーダル MoE を、1 枚のエッジ GPU で実測スループットまで示した例として、小規模サービング環境の設計者に参考になる。
blogs.summary_en: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is an open multimodal mixture-of-experts model with 120 billion total parameters and 12 billion active parameters per token, taking text, image, document, and video in and producing text out, built with C-RADIOv4 vision encoding, a hybrid Mamba-Transformer architecture, multi-token prediction (MTP), and NVFP4 quantization. It runs locally on a single DGX Spark and RTX PRO 6000, achieving 243.9 tok/s on the latter, with SGLang providing continuous batching, prefix caching, and speculative decoding for production serving.
blogs.why_en: Shows a Mamba-Transformer hybrid, MTP, and NVFP4 quantization combined in one deployed multimodal MoE model with a measured single-GPU throughput number, useful for anyone sizing small-footprint serving setups.

blogs.title: Beyond the KV cache: Training and serving i14’s Laplace 3B linear attention model on AWS Trainium2 with native PyTorch
blogs.excerpt: Learn how i14 trained and served Laplace 3B, a linear attention model, on AWS Trainium2 using native PyTorch. Its recurrent state stays fixed at 29.5 MB per sequence regardless of context length, avoiding the growing key-value cache of transformer models and keeping serving memory predictable.
blogs.ja_title: KV キャッシュを捨てた線形注意モデル Laplace 3B を Trainium2 で学習・推論
blogs.summary: 通常の Transformer は会話が長くなるほど KV (key-value) キャッシュが大きくなり、同時に処理できる会話数や推論コストに響く。i14 社の Laplace 3B は GLA (ゲート付き線形注意) で状態を固定サイズの行列に圧縮し、文脈の長さに関係なく 1 系列あたり 29.5 MB で一定にした。AWS の TorchNeuron Native を使い、Trainium2 の trn2.48xlarge インスタンス 1 台で学習時は毎秒約 12 万トークン、推論時は 1,280 件の同時実行で毎秒 11,544 トークンの出力を達成した。
blogs.why: KV キャッシュが増え続ける問題を線形注意で解決し、Trainium2 上で学習と推論の両方を実測した例として、分散学習・推論基盤の設計に新しい選択肢を示す。
blogs.summary_en: Standard transformer softmax attention grows its KV cache with context length, which can reduce concurrency and increase serving cost. i14's Laplace 3B uses Gated Linear Attention (GLA) to compress prior context into a fixed-size matrix state, keeping the recurrent state at 29.5 MB per sequence regardless of context length, with training attention changing from O(T^2) to O(T). Using AWS TorchNeuron Native to preserve the GLA design and Muon optimizer, Laplace 3B trained at about 120,000 tokens per second on one trn2.48xlarge instance and served 11,544 output tokens per second across 1,280 concurrent sequences.
blogs.why_en: Demonstrates a fixed-size-state linear attention architecture ported natively to Trainium2 with both training and serving throughput measured, offering an alternative to the growing-KV-cache transformer design for training/serving infrastructure builders.

blogs.title: Fine-tuning GPT-OSS-20B for multilingual reasoning on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod
blogs.excerpt: Learn how we fine-tuned GPT-OSS-20B for multilingual reasoning on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod, and how to decide between supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning with GRPO. SFT took reasoning-language accuracy from 22% to 100%, and GRPO added measurable gains where headroom existed.
blogs.ja_title: 多言語推論で GPT-OSS-20B を鍛える: SFT と GRPO はどちらを使うべきか
blogs.summary: GPT-OSS-20B は「フランス語で考えて」と頼んでも英語で考えてしまう推論モデルで、50 件のテストでは目標言語で思考できたのはわずか 22% (ほぼ全部が英語の問題) だった。SageMaker HyperPod 上で教師あり微調整 (SFT) を行うとこの割合は 100% まで上がり、SFT が伸びにくい部分だけを GRPO (グループ相対方策最適化、強化学習の一種) が追加で改善した。さらに Qwen2.5-7B で能力の差が異なる 2 つの課題を比較する対照実験を行い、GRPO が効くのは SFT だけでは届かない「伸びしろ」がある場合だと確かめた。
blogs.why: SFT と GRPO のどちらを使うかを「できる/できないの差の大きさ」という測れる基準で選べることを、対照実験つきで示しており、強化学習による後段チューニングを設計する人の判断材料になる。
blogs.summary_en: GPT-OSS-20B is an open-weight reasoning model that thinks in English even when asked to reason in French, German, Spanish, or Italian; on a 50-example test the base model reasoned in the correct target language only 22 percent of the time, almost entirely the English examples. Fine-tuning it with supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod closed that gap, and reinforcement learning with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) added measurable value on top where headroom remained; a controlled Qwen2.5-7B experiment across two tasks with different capability gaps was run to understand more broadly when GRPO helps. The authors' short answer: SFT does most of the work, GRPO refines when there is headroom to refine, and matching the technique to the capability gap is what decides the outcome.
blogs.why_en: Gives a measured, controlled comparison for deciding between SFT and GRPO based on the size of the capability gap, useful for anyone designing an RL-based post-training pipeline.
